questions.title: Rewilding
questions.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, conservation meant protecting what remained: fencing off reserves, counting species and managing landscapes to keep them as they were. Rewilding takes a different view. Rather than preserving a particular snapshot of nature, it aims to restore the natural processes that shape ecosystems, such as flooding, grazing and predation, and then to let the landscape find its own form.

The best-known example is the return of wolves to Yellowstone National Park in 1995. With predators back, elk stopped lingering along riverbanks, young willow and aspen recovered, and the regrowth stabilised the banks and created habitats for beavers and songbirds. Smaller projects in Europe have reintroduced bison, beavers and free-roaming cattle with similar, if less dramatic, effects.

Critics point out that rewilding can conflict with farming and that the Yellowstone story may have been simplified, since drought and human hunting also changed elk behaviour. Supporters accept that outcomes are hard to predict, but argue that this uncertainty is the point: ecosystems are more resilient when they are allowed to change than when they are frozen in place.
questions.model: Unlike traditional conservation, which preserves landscapes as they are, rewilding restores natural processes such as predation, as the return of wolves to Yellowstone illustrated, and although critics note conflicts with farming and oversimplified success stories, supporters argue that allowing ecosystems to change makes them more resilient.

zh.For most of the twentieth century, conse: 在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，保育的意思就是保護僅存的一切：把保護區圍起來、計算物種數量，並管理地景以維持原貌。「再野化」則抱持不同的觀點。它不是要保存自然在某一刻的樣貌，而是要恢復塑造生態系的自然過程，例如洪水、放牧和掠食，然後讓地景自行發展出自己的樣貌。
zh.The best-known example is the return of: 最著名的例子是 1995 年狼群重返黃石國家公園。掠食者回來之後，麋鹿不再在河岸逗留，幼小的柳樹和白楊恢復生長，重新長出的植被穩固了河岸，也為河狸和鳴禽創造了棲地。歐洲一些規模較小的計畫重新引進了野牛、河狸和自由放養的牛隻，產生了類似的效果，只是沒那麼顯著。
zh.Critics point out that rewilding can con: 批評者指出，再野化可能與農業發生衝突，而且黃石公園的故事可能被簡化了，因為乾旱和人類狩獵也改變了麋鹿的行為。支持者承認結果難以預測，但他們認為這種不確定性正是重點所在：讓生態系可以改變，比把它們凍結在原地更能增強其韌性。
zh.Unlike traditional conservation, which p: 傳統保育是維持地景的原貌，而再野化則是恢復掠食等自然過程，黃石公園狼群的回歸就是一例；雖然批評者指出它與農業的衝突以及成功故事被過度簡化，但支持者認為，讓生態系得以改變能使其更具韌性。

questions.title: The paradox of choice
questions.passage:
Economic theory has traditionally assumed that more choice is always better: a shopper who can pick from fifty options is at least as well off as one who can pick from five, because she can always choose the same item. In the early 2000s, psychologists began to challenge this assumption. In a well-known study, a supermarket display offering twenty-four varieties of jam attracted more attention than one offering six, but far fewer shoppers actually made a purchase.

The explanation proposed was that large choice sets impose costs of their own. Comparing many options takes effort, raises expectations and increases the likelihood of regret, because it becomes easier to imagine that a better option was missed. People faced with too many retirement plans, for example, are more likely to postpone joining any plan at all.

Later research has complicated the picture. Attempts to replicate the jam study produced mixed results, and the effect appears only under certain conditions: when options are hard to compare, when people lack clear preferences, or when the decision feels important. The practical lesson is therefore not that choice is harmful, but that choices should be organised so that people can navigate them easily.
questions.model: Although economics assumes more choice is always beneficial, psychological studies suggest large choice sets can discourage decisions by increasing effort and regret, yet since later research shows this happens only under specific conditions, the real lesson is to organise choices so they are easy to navigate.

zh.Economic theory has traditionally assume: 經濟理論傳統上假設選擇越多越好：一位可以從五十個選項中挑選的購物者，至少和只能從五個選項中挑選的人過得一樣好，因為她總是可以選擇同一件商品。在 2000 年代初期，心理學家開始挑戰這個假設。在一項著名的研究中，超市裡陳列二十四種果醬的攤位比只陳列六種的攤位吸引了更多目光，但實際購買的顧客卻少得多。
zh.The explanation proposed was that large: 當時提出的解釋是，龐大的選項組合本身就會帶來成本。比較許多選項需要花費心力、會提高期望，也會增加後悔的可能性，因為人們更容易想像自己錯過了更好的選擇。例如，面對太多退休金方案的人，更有可能延後加入任何一個方案。
zh.Later research has complicated the pictu: 後來的研究讓情況變得更加複雜。重做果醬研究的嘗試得出了分歧的結果，而且這種效應只在特定條件下才會出現：當選項難以比較、當人們缺乏明確的偏好，或當這個決定感覺很重要時。因此，實際的教訓並不是選擇有害，而是應該把選項組織好，讓人們能夠輕鬆地做出選擇。
zh.Although economics assumes more choice i: 雖然經濟學假設選擇越多越有利，但心理學研究顯示，龐大的選項組合可能因增加心力與後悔而讓人不願做決定；然而後來的研究顯示這只在特定條件下發生，因此真正的教訓是把選項組織得易於選擇。

questions.title: Why so few new antibiotics?
questions.passage:
Antibiotic resistance is often described as a scientific problem, but it is increasingly understood as an economic one. Bacteria evolve resistance to every drug eventually, so new antibiotics are constantly needed. Yet very few are being developed: most large pharmaceutical companies have left the field, and several small firms that brought new antibiotics to market have gone bankrupt shortly afterwards.

The reason lies in how drugs earn money. A new cancer medicine is prescribed widely and for long periods, generating large revenues. A new antibiotic, by contrast, is deliberately held in reserve by doctors to slow the development of resistance, and when it is used, a course lasts only a week or two. The very behaviour that protects its long-term value destroys its commercial value.

Several governments are now experimenting with a subscription model, in which health systems pay a fixed annual fee for access to a new antibiotic, regardless of how much is used. This separates the company’s income from sales volume. It is too early to know whether the approach will revive research, but it reflects a growing recognition that markets alone will not solve the problem.
questions.model: Although resistance makes new antibiotics essential, companies have abandoned them because doctors rightly reserve new drugs and prescribe only short courses, destroying their commercial value, so governments are testing subscription payments that separate income from sales volume in recognition that markets alone cannot solve the problem.

zh.Antibiotic resistance is often described: 抗生素抗藥性常被描述為一個科學問題，但人們越來越認識到它是一個經濟問題。細菌最終會對每一種藥物產生抗藥性，因此一直需要新的抗生素。然而正在研發的新抗生素卻非常少：大多數大型藥廠已經退出這個領域，而好幾家把新抗生素推向市場的小公司，不久之後就破產了。
原因在於藥物賺錢的方式。一種新的抗癌藥會被廣泛且長期地開立，帶來龐大的收入。相較之下，一種新的抗生素會被醫師刻意保留備用，以減緩抗藥性的產生，而且即使使用，一個療程也只持續一、兩週。正是保護其長期價值的這種做法，摧毀了它的商業價值。
zh.Several governments are now experimentin: 有幾個國家的政府目前正在試行一種「訂閱制」模式，由醫療體系每年支付固定費用以取得某種新抗生素的使用權，無論實際用量多少。這使藥廠的收入與銷售量脫鉤。現在要判斷這種做法能否重振研發還言之過早，但它反映出人們越來越體認到，光靠市場無法解決這個問題。
zh.Although resistance makes new antibiotic: 雖然抗藥性使新抗生素不可或缺，但由於醫師理所當然地保留新藥並只開短期療程，摧毀了其商業價值，藥廠因而放棄研發，於是各國政府正在試行使收入與銷量脫鉤的訂閱制付費，體認到光靠市場無法解決這個問題。

questions.title: Vertical farming
questions.passage:
Vertical farms grow crops indoors on stacked shelves under artificial light, with nutrients delivered in water rather than soil. Their supporters point to impressive numbers. Because growing conditions are controlled precisely, a vertical farm can produce many times more food per square metre than a field, uses up to ninety per cent less water, and needs no pesticides. It can also be built inside a city, close to the people who will eat its produce, reducing the distance food travels.

The difficulty is energy. Sunlight is free, whereas the lamps that replace it are not, and lighting and climate control can account for more than half of a vertical farm’s operating costs. As a result, the approach currently makes economic sense only for a narrow range of crops, such as lettuce, herbs and microgreens, which grow quickly, sell at high prices and are mostly water by weight. Staple crops like wheat or rice, which need large amounts of light to produce a small amount of grain, remain far cheaper to grow outdoors.

Several high-profile vertical farming companies have closed in recent years as energy prices rose. Researchers argue that the technology is best seen not as a replacement for conventional agriculture but as a complement to it, useful where land and water are scarce and renewable electricity is cheap.
questions.model: Although vertical farms produce far more food per square metre with much less water and no pesticides, their high energy costs limit them to fast-growing, high-value crops such as lettuce and herbs, so they are best regarded as a complement to conventional farming where land and water are scarce and renewable electricity is cheap.

zh.Vertical farms grow crops indoors on sta: 垂直農場在室內的層架上、利用人工光源種植作物，並以水而非土壤輸送養分。支持者提出了令人印象深刻的數據。由於生長條件受到精確控制，垂直農場每平方公尺的產量可以是農田的許多倍，用水量最多可減少百分之九十，而且不需要農藥。它還能建在城市裡，靠近食用其農產品的人，縮短食物運送的距離。
zh.The difficulty is energy. Sunlight is fr: 問題在於能源。陽光是免費的，但取代陽光的燈具卻不是，照明和溫控可能占垂直農場營運成本的一半以上。因此，這種做法目前只對少數作物具有經濟效益，例如萵苣、香草和芽菜，這些作物生長快速、售價高，而且重量大部分是水分。像小麥或稻米這類主食作物，需要大量光照才能產出少量穀物，在戶外種植仍然便宜得多。
zh.Several high-profile vertical farming co: 近年來，隨著能源價格上漲，好幾家備受矚目的垂直農業公司已經倒閉。研究人員認為，這項技術最好被視為傳統農業的補充，而不是替代品，適用於土地和水資源稀少、再生能源電力便宜的地方。
zh.Although vertical farms produce far more: 雖然垂直農場每平方公尺的產量高得多，用水更少且不需農藥，但高昂的能源成本使它只適用於萵苣、香草等生長快速的高價值作物，因此最好把它視為傳統農業的補充，適用於土地和水資源稀少、再生能源電力便宜的地方。

questions.title: The doctor who said wash your hands
questions.passage:
In the 1840s, a doctor named Ignaz Semmelweis noticed something disturbing at the Vienna General Hospital. Women who gave birth in the ward run by doctors and medical students died of fever far more often than those in the ward run by midwives. After a colleague died from an infection caught during an autopsy, Semmelweis concluded that doctors were carrying something from the bodies they dissected to the women they examined.

He introduced a simple rule: before examining patients, staff had to wash their hands in a chlorine solution. Deaths in his ward fell dramatically, from around one in ten to about one in a hundred. Yet his colleagues largely rejected the idea. Some were offended by the suggestion that gentlemen doctors could be the cause of disease, and Semmelweis himself did little to help his case, publishing slowly and responding to critics with angry letters rather than evidence.

Handwashing was accepted only decades later, after the work of Louis Pasteur and Joseph Lister established that germs cause infection. The story is often told as one of a lone genius ignored, but historians draw a more useful lesson: evidence alone rarely changes practice without a convincing explanation and effective communication.
questions.model: When Semmelweis showed in the 1840s that handwashing with chlorine dramatically cut deaths among new mothers, his colleagues rejected the idea, partly from pride and partly because he communicated poorly, and it was accepted only after germ theory explained it, showing that evidence needs a convincing explanation and good communication to change practice.

zh.In the 1840s, a doctor named Ignaz Semme: 1840 年代，一位名叫伊格納茲・塞麥爾維斯的醫師在維也納總醫院注意到一件令人不安的事。在由醫師和醫學生負責的病房中分娩的婦女，死於產褥熱的比例遠高於由助產士負責的病房。在一位同事因解剖時受到感染而死亡之後，塞麥爾維斯得出結論：醫師把某種東西從他們解剖的屍體上帶到了他們檢查的婦女身上。
zh.He introduced a simple rule: before exam: 他制定了一條簡單的規定：在檢查病人之前，工作人員必須用氯溶液洗手。他病房中的死亡率大幅下降，從大約十分之一降到約百分之一。然而，他的同事大多拒絕接受這個想法。有些人對於「紳士醫師可能是疾病的來源」這種說法感到被冒犯，而塞麥爾維斯本人也沒有為自己的主張加分，他遲遲才發表研究成果，而且用憤怒的信件而不是證據來回應批評者。
zh.Handwashing was accepted only decades la: 直到數十年後，路易・巴斯德和約瑟夫・李斯特的研究確立了細菌會導致感染，洗手才被接受。這個故事常被描述為一位孤獨天才遭到忽視，但歷史學家從中得出一個更有用的教訓：沒有令人信服的解釋和有效的溝通，光靠證據很少能改變實際做法。
zh.When Semmelweis showed in the 1840s that: 塞麥爾維斯在 1840 年代證明用氯溶液洗手能大幅降低產婦的死亡率，但他的同事部分出於自尊、部分因為他溝通不佳而拒絕接受，直到細菌理論提出解釋後才被採納，這顯示證據需要令人信服的解釋和良好的溝通才能改變實際做法。

questions.title: Too many tourists?
questions.passage:
Tourism is one of the world’s largest industries, and for many cities it is a vital source of income and jobs. In recent years, however, places such as Venice, Barcelona and Amsterdam have begun to describe tourism as a problem rather than a blessing. Residents complain of crowded streets, rising rents as flats are converted into short-term holiday lets, and local shops being replaced by souvenir stalls that serve visitors rather than the community.

The difficulty is that the benefits and costs of tourism fall on different people. Hotel owners, airlines and the city’s tax revenue benefit from rising visitor numbers, while the costs are borne by residents in the most popular neighbourhoods. Because visitors are concentrated in a few famous areas and at the same times of year, a city can feel overwhelmed even when its total number of tourists is not unusually high.

Cities are experimenting with different responses, from entry fees for day-trippers and limits on cruise ships to restrictions on holiday rentals. Most experts agree that the aim should not be to stop tourism, which would damage local economies, but to spread visitors more evenly across places and seasons and to ensure that residents share in the benefits.
questions.model: Although tourism brings vital income, cities such as Venice and Barcelona face overcrowding, rising rents and lost local shops because the benefits go to businesses while residents in popular areas bear the costs, so experts recommend spreading visitors across places and seasons and ensuring residents share the benefits rather than stopping tourism.

zh.Tourism is one of the world’s largest in: 觀光是世界上最大的產業之一，對許多城市來說，它是重要的收入和就業來源。然而近年來，威尼斯、巴塞隆納和阿姆斯特丹等地開始把觀光描述為一個問題，而不是一種恩惠。居民抱怨街道擁擠、公寓被改建為短期度假出租使得房租上漲，以及當地商店被服務遊客而非社區的紀念品攤位取代。
zh.The difficulty is that the benefits and: 問題在於，觀光的好處和代價落在不同的人身上。飯店業者、航空公司和城市的稅收從不斷增加的遊客人數中獲益，而代價則由最熱門街區的居民承擔。由於遊客集中在少數幾個著名地區，而且集中在一年中的相同時段，即使一座城市的遊客總數並不特別多，它仍可能感到不堪負荷。
zh.Cities are experimenting with different: 各城市正在嘗試不同的因應方式，從向當日往返的遊客收取入城費、限制郵輪停靠，到限制度假出租。大多數專家同意，目標不應該是阻止觀光，因為那會損害地方經濟，而是讓遊客更平均地分散到不同地點和季節，並確保居民也能分享觀光帶來的好處。
zh.Although tourism brings vital income, ci: 雖然觀光帶來重要的收入，但由於好處歸於企業、代價卻由熱門地區的居民承擔，威尼斯和巴塞隆納等城市面臨擁擠、房租上漲和在地商店消失等問題，因此專家建議不要阻止觀光，而是把遊客分散到不同地點和季節，並確保居民分享其好處。

questions.title: Loneliness and health
questions.passage:
Loneliness was once regarded as a private misfortune, but it is increasingly treated as a public health issue. Large studies have found that people who report persistent loneliness have a higher risk of heart disease, stroke and dementia, and one widely cited analysis compared its effect on mortality to that of smoking fifteen cigarettes a day. That comparison has been criticised as exaggerated, yet even cautious researchers accept that the link with poorer health is real.

Loneliness is not the same as being alone. Many people live alone and feel well connected, while others feel lonely despite being surrounded by family or colleagues. What matters is the gap between the relationships a person has and the relationships they want. This is one reason why loneliness is common not only among older people but also among young adults, particularly those who have recently moved for study or work.

Some governments have responded by appointing ministers for loneliness and funding programmes that encourage social activity. The evidence on what works is still limited, but interventions that give people a meaningful shared role, such as volunteering or community groups built around a common task, appear more effective than simply increasing social contact.
questions.model: Loneliness, now treated as a public health issue because it is linked to heart disease, stroke and dementia, depends on the gap between the relationships people have and those they want rather than on living alone, so it affects young adults as well as older people, and interventions offering a meaningful shared role seem most effective.

zh.Loneliness was once regarded as a privat: 孤獨曾被視為個人的不幸，但如今越來越被當作一個公共衛生問題。大型研究發現，長期感到孤獨的人罹患心臟病、中風和失智症的風險較高，一項被廣泛引用的分析甚至把它對死亡率的影響，比作每天抽十五支菸。這個比較被批評為誇大其詞，但即使是謹慎的研究人員也承認，孤獨與較差的健康狀況之間確實有關聯。
zh.Loneliness is not the same as being alon: 孤獨並不等於獨處。許多人獨自生活，卻感覺與他人緊密連結，而另一些人即使身邊圍繞著家人或同事，仍然感到孤獨。重要的是一個人擁有的人際關係與他想要的人際關係之間的落差。這也是為什麼孤獨不只常見於年長者，也常見於年輕人，尤其是那些最近為了讀書或工作而搬家的人。
zh.Some governments have responded by appoi: 有些政府的因應方式是任命「孤獨事務大臣」，並資助鼓勵社交活動的計畫。關於哪些做法有效，證據仍然有限，但那些讓人擁有有意義的共同角色的介入措施，例如志工服務或圍繞共同任務組成的社區團體，似乎比單純增加社交接觸更有效。
zh.Loneliness, now treated as a public heal: 孤獨因為與心臟病、中風和失智症有關而被視為公共衛生問題，它取決於一個人擁有的人際關係與想要的人際關係之間的落差，而不是是否獨居，因此它影響年輕人也影響年長者，而提供有意義共同角色的介入措施似乎最有效。

questions.title: The Green Revolution
questions.passage:
Between the 1960s and the 1980s, a set of agricultural changes known as the Green Revolution transformed food production in much of Asia and Latin America. Scientists developed new varieties of wheat and rice with short, strong stems that could carry heavy heads of grain without falling over. When combined with fertiliser, irrigation and pesticides, these varieties doubled or even tripled yields, and countries such as India moved from recurring famine to producing surplus grain.

The achievements were enormous. Economists estimate that without the higher yields, hundreds of millions more people would have gone hungry, and far more forest would have been cleared to grow food. Yet the benefits were uneven. Farmers with irrigation and access to credit gained the most, while poorer farmers on rain-fed land were often left behind.

The environmental costs have also become clearer over time. Heavy use of fertiliser and water has degraded soils and lowered water tables in some of the most productive regions, and reliance on a small number of crop varieties has reduced genetic diversity. Many researchers now argue that a second revolution is needed, one that raises yields while protecting the soil and water on which future harvests depend.
questions.model: The Green Revolution’s high-yield wheat and rice, combined with fertiliser and irrigation, greatly increased food production and prevented widespread hunger, but its benefits favoured wealthier farmers and it damaged soils, water supplies and crop diversity, so researchers call for a new approach that raises yields while protecting natural resources.

zh.Between the 1960s and the 1980s, a set o: 在 1960 年代到 1980 年代之間，一系列被稱為「綠色革命」的農業變革，改變了亞洲和拉丁美洲大部分地區的糧食生產。科學家培育出新的小麥和稻米品種，它們的莖短而強壯，能支撐沉重的穀穗而不倒伏。這些品種搭配肥料、灌溉和農藥，使產量增加了兩倍甚至三倍，而像印度這樣的國家，也從饑荒頻繁轉變為糧食過剩。
zh.The achievements were enormous. Economis: 這些成就非常巨大。經濟學家估計，如果沒有這些更高的產量，將會有數億人挨餓，也會有更多森林被砍伐來種植糧食。然而，好處的分配並不平均。擁有灌溉設施和能取得貸款的農民獲益最多，而在靠雨水灌溉的土地上耕作的較貧窮農民，則常常被拋在後頭。
zh.The environmental costs have also become: 隨著時間過去，它對環境造成的代價也變得更加明顯。大量使用肥料和水，已經使一些產量最高的地區土壤退化、地下水位下降，而且依賴少數幾種作物品種，也降低了遺傳多樣性。許多研究人員現在主張需要第二次革命，一次既能提高產量、又能保護未來收成所仰賴的土壤和水資源的革命。
zh.The Green Revolution’s high-yield wheat: 綠色革命的高產量小麥和稻米搭配肥料與灌溉，大幅提高了糧食產量並避免了大規模饑荒，但其好處偏向較富裕的農民，也破壞了土壤、水資源和作物多樣性，因此研究人員呼籲採取一種既能提高產量又能保護自然資源的新做法。

questions.prompt: Some people believe that governments should spend money on space exploration, while others argue that the money should be used to solve problems on Earth first. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: paraphrase the question and state your position clearly.
Body 1: the case for space spending - scientific discovery, technology spin-offs, long-term survival.
Body 2: the case for Earth first - poverty, health, climate, and the opportunity cost of every budget.
Weigh them: space budgets are small relative to total spending, and much space research serves Earth, such as climate and weather satellites.
Conclusion: restate your view and why, without introducing new arguments.

zh.Some people believe that governments sho: 有些人認為政府應該把錢花在太空探索上，但也有人主張這些錢應該先用來解決地球上的問題。請討論這兩種觀點，並提出你自己的看法。
zh.Introduction: paraphrase the question an: 引言：改寫題目，並清楚表明你的立場。
zh.Body 1: the case for space spending - sc: 主體段一：支持太空支出的理由——科學發現、技術的衍生應用、人類的長期存續。
zh.Body 2: the case for Earth first - pover: 主體段二：支持先解決地球問題的理由——貧窮、健康、氣候，以及每一筆預算的機會成本。
zh.Weigh them: space budgets are small rela: 權衡兩方：太空預算相對於總支出而言很小，而且許多太空研究是為地球服務的，例如氣候與氣象衛星。
zh.Conclusion: restate your view and why, w: 結論：重申你的觀點和理由，不要提出新的論點。

questions.prompt: Working from home has become common in many professions. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages? Use examples to support your answer.
plan: Take a clear position in the introduction: mostly outweigh, mostly do not, or depends on the job.
Advantages: no commute, flexibility, and a wider pool of talent for employers.
Disadvantages: isolation, weaker mentoring for junior staff, and blurred boundaries between work and home.
Use one concrete example, such as a named industry or type of role, in each body paragraph.
Conclusion: summarise the balance, perhaps recommending a hybrid arrangement.

zh.Working from home has become common in m: 在家工作在許多職業中已經變得很普遍。這個趨勢的優點是否大於缺點？請用例子支持你的答案。
zh.Take a clear position in the introductio: 在引言中表明清楚的立場：大致利大於弊、大致弊大於利，或視工作性質而定。
zh.Advantages: no commute, flexibility, and: 優點：不用通勤、彈性大，雇主也能從更廣的人才庫中招募。
zh.Disadvantages: isolation, weaker mentori: 缺點：孤立感、對資淺員工的指導變弱，以及工作與家庭之間的界線變得模糊。
zh.Use one concrete example, such as a name: 每個主體段都使用一個具體的例子，例如某個特定產業或某種職務。
zh.Conclusion: summarise the balance, perha: 結論：總結利弊的權衡，或許可以建議採用混合式的工作安排。

questions.prompt: Some people think that museums and art galleries should be free for everyone, while others believe visitors should pay an entry fee. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
plan: Introduction: restate the issue and give your view clearly.
Body 1: the case for free entry - access for all incomes, education, higher visitor numbers.
Body 2: the case for fees - maintenance and conservation costs, and the fairness of making visitors pay rather than all taxpayers.
Consider a middle way, such as free entry for residents, students or on certain days, with charges for special exhibitions.
Conclusion: summarise both sides and restate your position.

zh.Some people think that museums and art g: 有些人認為博物館和美術館應該對所有人免費開放，但也有人認為參觀者應該支付入場費。請討論這兩種觀點，並提出你自己的看法。
zh.Introduction: restate the issue and give: 引言：重述議題並清楚表明你的觀點。
zh.Body 1: the case for free entry - access: 主體段一：支持免費入場的理由——讓各種收入的人都能參觀、教育意義、提高參觀人數。
zh.Body 2: the case for fees - maintenance: 主體段二：支持收費的理由——維護與典藏的成本，以及由參觀者付費而非全體納稅人負擔的公平性。
zh.Consider a middle way, such as free entr: 考慮折衷的做法，例如居民、學生免費或特定日子免費，而特展則另外收費。
zh.Conclusion: summarise both sides and res: 結論：總結雙方論點，並重申你的立場。

questions.prompt: Many people believe that learning a foreign language at primary school is more effective than learning it later in life. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
plan: State how far you agree in the introduction, for example largely but not completely.
Arguments for an early start: better pronunciation, less anxiety, more total years of exposure.
Arguments against: older learners progress faster at first, and early lessons are often too few hours to matter.
Use an example, such as the difference between two hours a week and immersion.
Conclusion: an early start helps only when there is enough regular exposure.

zh.Many people believe that learning a fore: 許多人認為，在小學學習外語比在人生較晚的階段學習更有效。你在多大程度上同意或不同意這個說法？
zh.State how far you agree in the introduct: 在引言中說明你同意的程度，例如大致同意但並非完全同意。
zh.Arguments for an early start: better pro: 支持及早開始的論點：發音較好、焦慮較少、接觸語言的總年數較多。
zh.Arguments against: older learners progre: 反對的論點：年紀較大的學習者一開始進步較快，而且早期的課程時數往往太少，起不了作用。
zh.Use an example, such as the difference b: 舉一個例子，例如每週兩小時和沉浸式學習之間的差別。
zh.Conclusion: an early start helps only wh: 結論：只有在有足夠且規律的接觸時，及早開始才會有幫助。

questions.prompt: In many countries, people are living longer than ever before. What problems does an ageing population create, and what solutions can you suggest?
plan: Introduction: note the trend and outline the problems and solutions you will discuss.
Problem 1: pension and healthcare costs rising as fewer workers support more retirees.
Problem 2: labour shortages and pressure on families who care for older relatives.
Solutions: flexible later retirement, investment in preventive healthcare, and support for carers.
Conclusion: an ageing population is a challenge, but also a sign of success that can be managed.

zh.In many countries, people are living lon: 在許多國家，人們的壽命比以往任何時候都長。人口老化會造成哪些問題？你能提出哪些解決辦法？
zh.Introduction: note the trend and outline: 引言：指出這個趨勢，並概述你將討論的問題和解決辦法。
zh.Problem 1: pension and healthcare costs: 問題一：由於越來越少的勞動者要供養越來越多的退休者，退休金和醫療成本不斷上升。
zh.Problem 2: labour shortages and pressure: 問題二：勞動力短缺，以及照顧年長親人的家庭所承受的壓力。
zh.Solutions: flexible later retirement, in: 解決辦法：彈性的延後退休、投資於預防性醫療，以及支援照顧者。
zh.Conclusion: an ageing population is a ch: 結論：人口老化是一項挑戰，但也是一種成就的象徵，而且是可以應對的。

questions.title: Monsoon trade
parts: For centuries, sailors in the Indian Ocean relied on the monsoon, a seasonal
of the winds that blow from the south-west in summer and from the north-east in winter. By timing their voyages
, merchants could sail from Arabia to India and return within a single year. This predictable rhythm made long-distance trade far less
than it was in other oceans, and ports on both coasts grew wealthy as a
why: The winds blow “from the south-west in summer and from the north-east in winter”, so they change direction: a reversal. A collapse, shortage or reduction would mean less wind, not wind from the opposite side.

Merchants timed their voyages to fit the winds just described, which is what “accordingly” means. “reluctantly” and “eventually” add ideas the passage never supports, and “separately” makes no sense with “timing”.
A “predictable rhythm” removes uncertainty, so trade became less risky. Less popular or less frequent trade would contradict the ports growing wealthy, and “less familiar” makes no sense here.
Fixed phrase: “as a result” links the wealth to the trade that produced it. “as a reason” and “as a cause” are not idiomatic here, and “as a purpose” reverses the logic.

zh.For centuries, sailors in the Indian Oce: 數個世紀以來，印度洋上的水手依賴季風，也就是風向的季節性 ____ ：夏季的風從西南方吹來，冬季則從東北方吹來。只要 ____ 安排航程時間，商人就能從阿拉伯航行到印度，並在一年內返回。這種可預測的節奏，使這裡的長途貿易遠不像其他海洋那樣 ____ ，而兩岸的港口也因此（as a ____ ）變得富裕。
zh.The winds blow “from the south-west in s: 風「夏季從西南方吹來，冬季從東北方吹來」，表示風向改變了，也就是 reversal（反轉）。collapse、shortage 或 reduction 都表示風變少，而不是風從相反方向吹來。
zh.Merchants timed their voyages to fit the: 商人依照剛剛描述的風向來安排航程，這正是 accordingly（據此、相應地）的意思。reluctantly 和 eventually 加入了文章沒有支持的概念，而 separately 和「安排時間」搭配起來沒有意義。
zh.A “predictable rhythm” removes uncertain: 「可預測的節奏」消除了不確定性，所以貿易變得比較不 risky（危險）。如果貿易變得較不受歡迎或較不頻繁，就與港口變得富裕互相矛盾，而 less familiar 在這裡沒有意義。
zh.Fixed phrase: “as a result” links the we: 固定用語：as a result（因此）把財富和帶來財富的貿易連結起來。as a reason 和 as a cause 在這裡都不是道地的說法，而 as a purpose 則把邏輯顛倒了。

questions.title: The Mediterranean diet
parts: The Mediterranean diet, rich in vegetables, olive oil and fish, is
linked with lower rates of heart disease. Much of the early evidence, however, came from observational studies, which cannot easily
the effect of diet from that of other habits such as exercise. A large Spanish trial later
participants to different diets and found a clear benefit, although the study was criticised when problems with its randomisation came to
why: The next sentence qualifies the evidence with “however”, which only makes sense if this sentence states a strong, repeated finding. “rarely”, “hardly” and “barely” would already deny the link.

Collocation: you separate one effect from another. Observational studies struggle to disentangle diet from exercise; “combine … from” is not English, and “measure” or “prevent … from” change the meaning.

In a trial, researchers assign participants to groups, which is exactly what observational studies cannot do. “advised”, “attracted” and “allowed … to different diets” do not describe random allocation.
Fixed idiom: problems “came to light” when they were discovered. “came to mind” means someone thought of them, and “came to hand” and “came to view” are not used for revealed problems.

zh.The Mediterranean diet, rich in vegetabl: 富含蔬菜、橄欖油和魚類的地中海飲食，____ 與較低的心臟病發生率有關。然而，早期的證據大多來自觀察性研究，而這類研究很難把飲食的影響與運動等其他習慣的影響 ____ 。後來西班牙一項大型試驗把受試者 ____ 到不同的飲食組，並發現了明顯的益處，不過當這項研究的隨機分組問題 ____ 時，它也受到了批評。
zh.The next sentence qualifies the evidence: 下一句用 however 對證據加以保留，這只有在本句陳述的是一個強烈且反覆出現的發現時才說得通。rarely、hardly 和 barely 都等於已經否定了這個關聯。
zh.Collocation: you separate one effect fro: 固定搭配：separate A from B（把 A 與 B 區分開來）。觀察性研究難以把飲食和運動的影響區分開來；combine … from 不是正確的英文，而 measure 或 prevent … from 則會改變句意。
zh.In a trial, researchers assign participa: 在試驗中，研究人員會把受試者 assign（分派）到不同組別，而這正是觀察性研究做不到的。advised、attracted 和 allowed … to different diets 都無法描述隨機分組。
zh.Fixed idiom: problems “came to light” wh: 固定慣用語：問題 came to light 表示問題被發現、曝光。came to mind 的意思是某人想到了它們，而 came to hand 和 came to view 都不用來描述被揭露的問題。

questions.title: Crowdfunding
parts: Crowdfunding platforms allow entrepreneurs to raise money directly from thousands of small
rather than from banks or professional investors. Supporters argue that this
access to capital, since a good idea no longer depends on knowing the right people. Yet studies show that most campaigns fail to reach their targets, and success is strongly
with having a large social network before the campaign begins. In practice, the crowd often
the connections it was supposed to replace.
why: The contrast is with banks and investors, so the gap needs people who supply money: backers. Borrowers take money, and competitors and critics do not fund anything.

“since a good idea no longer depends on knowing the right people” argues for wider, fairer access to money, which is what “democratises” means. The other verbs describe the opposite of what supporters would claim.

Collocation: success is “associated with” a factor when the two occur together in the data. “compared with” and “confused with” change the meaning, and “combined with” does not report a statistical link.

The paradox is that crowdfunding still favours people who already have networks: it rewards the connections it claimed to make unnecessary. “replaces” repeats the word the sentence contrasts with, and “ignores” or “weakens” contradict the evidence.

zh.Crowdfunding platforms allow entrepreneu: 群眾募資平台讓創業者能直接向成千上萬的小額 ____ 募集資金，而不是向銀行或專業投資人籌資。支持者認為，這 ____ 了取得資金的機會，因為一個好點子不再取決於是否認識對的人。然而研究顯示，大多數募資活動都未能達成目標，而成功與否和活動開始前是否擁有龐大的社交網絡密切 ____ 。實際上，群眾往往 ____ 了它原本應該取代的人脈關係。
zh.The contrast is with banks and investors: 這裡的對比對象是銀行和投資人，所以空格需要一群提供資金的人：backers（支持者、出資者）。borrowers 是借錢的人，而 competitors 和 critics 都不會出資。
zh.“since a good idea no longer depends on: 「因為一個好點子不再取決於是否認識對的人」是在主張更廣泛、更公平地取得資金，這正是 democratises（使大眾化、民主化）的意思。其他動詞描述的都與支持者的主張相反。
zh.Collocation: success is “associated with: 固定搭配：當某個因素與成功在數據中同時出現時，就說成功 is associated with（與…相關）這個因素。compared with 和 confused with 會改變句意，而 combined with 並不表示統計上的關聯。
zh.The paradox is that crowdfunding still f: 這裡的矛盾在於，群眾募資仍然偏袒已經擁有人脈的人：它 rewards（獎勵）了它聲稱要讓其變得不必要的人脈。replaces 重複了句子所對比的那個字，而 ignores 或 weakens 則與證據矛盾。

questions.title: Glaciers as water towers
parts: Mountain glaciers act as natural water towers, storing winter snow as ice and
it gradually as meltwater through the dry summer months. In parts of Central Asia and the Andes, this meltwater
for a large share of river flow when rainfall is lowest. As the climate warms, glaciers first release more water than usual, creating a temporary
. Once the ice has shrunk past a certain point, however, summer flows decline sharply, with serious
for farming and hydropower.
why: A water tower stores water and then lets it out, and “gradually as meltwater” describes water being released. Reducing, removing or refusing it would not supply the rivers.
Collocation: something “accounts for” a share of a total. “allows for”, “calls for” and “makes for” all exist, but none of them means “makes up a proportion of”.
Releasing “more water than usual” produces a temporary surplus. The shortage comes later, “once the ice has shrunk”, so “shortage” puts the effect in the wrong place.
“decline sharply” and “serious” point to harmful effects, so the noun is consequences. “benefits” contradicts the decline, and “instructions” and “exceptions” do not fit “serious … for farming”.

zh.Mountain glaciers act as natural water t: 高山冰川就像天然的水塔，把冬天的積雪儲存成冰，然後在乾燥的夏季月份以融水的形式逐漸 ____ 出來。在中亞和安地斯山脈的部分地區，當降雨量最少時，這些融水 ____ 了河川流量的一大部分。隨著氣候暖化，冰川起初會釋放比平常更多的水，造成暫時的 ____ 。然而一旦冰縮小到某個程度以下，夏季的水流量就會急遽下降，對農業和水力發電造成嚴重的 ____ 。
zh.A water tower stores water and then lets: 水塔會先儲水再把水放出來，而「以融水的形式逐漸」描述的正是水被 releasing（釋放）。減少、移除或拒絕給水都無法供應河川。
zh.Collocation: something “accounts for” a: 固定搭配：某物 accounts for（占）總數的一部分。allows for、calls for 和 makes for 都是存在的片語，但沒有一個是「占…比例」的意思。
zh.Releasing “more water than usual” produc: 釋放「比平常更多的水」會造成暫時的 surplus（過剩）。短缺是之後才發生的，也就是「一旦冰縮小之後」，所以 shortage 把效應放錯了時間點。
zh.“decline sharply” and “serious” point to: 「急遽下降」和「嚴重的」都指向有害的影響，所以名詞是 consequences（後果）。benefits 與下降相矛盾，而 instructions 和 exceptions 都無法搭配「對農業造成嚴重的…」。

questions.title: Before vaccines
parts: Long before vaccines, people in China, India and parts of Africa practised variolation, deliberately
healthy people with material from smallpox sores. The procedure usually produced a mild illness followed by lifelong
. It was not without danger, since a small
of patients developed severe smallpox and could infect others. When Edward Jenner showed in 1796 that material from cowpox gave the same protection far more safely, variolation was gradually
why: Giving healthy people material from smallpox sores is deliberate infection. “treating” implies they were already ill, and “feeding” and “warning … with material” make no sense.

The point of variolation was protection: a mild illness “followed by” lifelong immunity. Lifelong weakness or illness would make the practice pointless, and the last sentence calls Jenner’s method “the same protection”.
Patients can be counted, so they form a “proportion”. “quantity” and “amount” go with uncountable nouns, and “a small size of patients” is not English.
A safer method made the older one unnecessary, so variolation was abandoned. “adopted”, “invented” and “expanded” contradict the logic of “far more safely”.

zh.Long before vaccines, people in China, I: 早在疫苗出現之前，中國、印度和非洲部分地區的人就已經在施行「人痘接種法」，也就是刻意用天花膿瘡的物質 ____ 健康的人。這種做法通常會引起輕微的疾病，之後便能獲得終身的 ____ 。它並非沒有危險，因為有一小 ____ 的病人會發展成嚴重的天花，並可能傳染給他人。當愛德華・詹納在 1796 年證明牛痘的物質能以安全得多的方式提供同樣的保護後，人痘接種法便逐漸被 ____ 了。
zh.Giving healthy people material from smal: 把天花膿瘡的物質給健康的人，就是刻意 infecting（使感染）。treating 表示他們原本就生病了，而 feeding 和 warning … with material 在語意上都說不通。
zh.The point of variolation was protection:: 人痘接種的目的是保護：輕微的疾病「之後」獲得終身 immunity（免疫力）。終身虛弱或生病會使這種做法毫無意義，而且最後一句把詹納的方法稱為「同樣的保護」。
zh.Patients can be counted, so they form a: 病人是可數的，所以用 proportion（比例）。quantity 和 amount 用於不可數名詞，而 a small size of patients 不是正確的英文。
zh.A safer method made the older one unnece: 更安全的方法讓舊方法變得不必要，所以人痘接種被 abandoned（放棄）了。adopted、invented 和 expanded 都與「安全得多」的邏輯相矛盾。

questions.title: Citizen science
parts: Citizen science projects invite members of the public to
to genuine research, from counting garden birds to classifying galaxies in telescope images. Scientists were initially
about data collected by untrained volunteers. Studies have since shown, however, that with clear instructions and several independent checks of each observation, volunteer data can be as
as data gathered by professionals. The greatest benefit may lie in the sheer
of observations that no research team could collect alone.
why: Collocation: people contribute to research. You attend an event, object to something you oppose and belong to a group; none of these describes taking part in the work.
“however” in the next sentence introduces evidence that overturned an early doubt, so scientists must have been sceptical. “enthusiastic” and “certain” leave no doubt to overturn.
The comparison is about data quality once it has been checked, so volunteer data can be as reliable as professional data. Quantity is dealt with separately in the final sentence.
“that no research team could collect alone” points to the enormous number of observations: their scale. Speed, style and price do not describe what a team could not “collect”.

zh.Citizen science projects invite members: 公民科學計畫邀請一般民眾為真正的研究 ____ ，從計算庭院裡的鳥類，到為望遠鏡影像中的星系分類都有。科學家起初對未受過訓練的志工所收集的數據抱持 ____ 的態度。然而，後來的研究顯示，只要有清楚的說明，並對每一筆觀察進行數次獨立的檢核，志工的數據可以和專業人員收集的數據一樣 ____ 。最大的好處或許在於觀察數量之龐大 ____ ，這是任何研究團隊都無法獨力收集的。
zh.Collocation: people contribute to resear: 固定搭配：人們 contribute to（貢獻於）研究。attend 是參加活動，object to 是反對某事，belong to 是屬於某個團體；這些都無法描述參與研究工作。
zh.“however” in the next sentence introduce: 下一句的 however 引出了推翻早期疑慮的證據，所以科學家當初一定是 sceptical（懷疑的）。enthusiastic 和 certain 都表示沒有疑慮可以被推翻。
zh.The comparison is about data quality onc: 這裡比較的是經過檢核後的數據品質，所以志工的數據可以和專業數據一樣 reliable（可靠）。數量的部分在最後一句另外討論。
zh.“that no research team could collect alo: 「這是任何研究團隊都無法獨力收集的」指的是觀察數量之多：也就是它們的 scale（規模）。速度、風格和價格都無法描述團隊無法「收集」的東西。

questions.title: Words for colour
parts: Languages
widely in how many basic colour terms they use. Some have only two or three, while English has eleven. Researchers have long debated whether these differences
what speakers actually see. Experiments suggest a modest effect: Russian speakers, whose language has separate words for light and dark blue, are slightly faster at
between those shades. The underlying perception is the same, but language appears to sharpen attention at the
that it names.
why: “Some have only two or three, while English has eleven” describes variation, so languages vary. Languages do not “agree widely”, and “depend” and “consist” need other prepositions (on, of).
The debate is whether language affects perception, and the experiments then measure “a modest effect”. “describe” and “repeat” are not effects on perception, and “prevent” is far too strong.
Collocation: distinguish between two things. The experiment is about telling shades apart; you do not “mix”, “paint” or “name” between shades.
Russian names the boundary between light and dark blue, and that is exactly where its speakers become faster. “moments”, “languages” and “speakers” are not things a language names in this sense.

zh.Languages ____ widely in how many basic: 各種語言所使用的基本顏色詞彙數量 ____ 很大。有些語言只有兩三個，而英語有十一個。研究人員長久以來一直爭論，這些差異是否會 ____ 說話者實際看到的東西。實驗顯示有些許影響：俄語中淺藍色和深藍色是不同的詞，而說俄語的人在 ____ 這兩種色調時稍微快一些。基本的感知是相同的，但語言似乎會在它所命名的 ____ 上提高人們的注意力。
zh.“Some have only two or three, while Engl: 「有些語言只有兩三個，而英語有十一個」描述的是差異，所以語言 vary（各不相同）。語言不會 agree widely，而 depend 和 consist 需要搭配其他介系詞（on、of）。
zh.The debate is whether language affects p: 爭論的是語言是否會影響感知，而實驗接著測量到「些許影響」。describe 和 repeat 都不是對感知的影響，而 prevent 則太過強烈。
zh.Collocation: distinguish between two thi: 固定搭配：distinguish between（區分）兩樣東西。這項實驗是關於分辨色調；我們不會說在色調之間 mix、paint 或 name。
zh.Russian names the boundary between light: 俄語為淺藍與深藍之間的 boundary（界線）命名，而說俄語的人正是在這裡反應變快。moments、languages 和 speakers 都不是語言在這個意義上所命名的東西。

questions.title: The Rosetta Stone
parts: The Rosetta Stone, discovered in Egypt in 1799, carries the same decree written in three
: hieroglyphs, a later Egyptian script and ancient Greek. Because scholars could already read Greek, the stone offered a key to the
. Even so, decoding hieroglyphs took more than twenty years, since researchers had wrongly
that each symbol stood for a whole idea. The breakthrough came when Jean-François Champollion showed that many signs actually
sounds.
why: The list after the colon — hieroglyphs, a later Egyptian script and Greek — names writing systems, so the word is “scripts”. Colours, chapters and volumes do not describe that list.
“a key to the …” needs whatever was still unread: the other two scripts. Readable Greek unlocked “the others”; answers, errors and owners make no sense here.
A mistaken belief is something people “wrongly assumed”. “denied” or “doubted” would mean the idea was true, which contradicts the next sentence.
Champollion showed that signs stood for sounds: they “represented” sounds. The other verbs do not describe what a written sign does.

zh.The Rosetta Stone, discovered in Egypt i: 1799 年在埃及發現的羅塞塔石碑，刻有以三種 ____ 寫成的同一份詔令：象形文字、一種較晚期的埃及文字，以及古希臘文。由於學者早已能讀懂希臘文，這塊石碑便成了解讀其 ____ 的鑰匙。即便如此，破解象形文字仍花了二十多年，因為研究人員錯誤地 ____ 每個符號都代表一個完整的概念。突破出現在商博良證明許多符號其實 ____ 的是聲音。
zh.The list after the colon — hieroglyphs,: 冒號後面列出的象形文字、較晚期的埃及文字和希臘文都是書寫系統，所以答案是 scripts（文字）。colours、chapters 和 volumes 都無法描述這份清單。
zh.“a key to the …” needs whatever was stil: 「…的鑰匙」需要的是當時還讀不懂的東西：另外兩種文字。能讀懂的希臘文解開了 the others（其他文字）；answers、errors 和 owners 在這裡都說不通。
zh.A mistaken belief is something people “w: 錯誤的信念是人們 wrongly assumed（錯誤地假設）的東西。denied 或 doubted 表示那個想法是正確的，與下一句矛盾。
zh.Champollion showed that signs stood for: 商博良證明了符號代表聲音：它們 represented（代表）聲音。其他動詞都無法描述書寫符號的功能。

questions.title: Urban foxes
parts: Red foxes have been living in British cities since at least the 1930s, when new suburbs with large gardens offered plenty of food and
. Although many people assume urban foxes survive mainly by raiding bins, studies of their diet show that a large
of their food is deliberately put out by residents. City foxes also tend to be bolder than rural ones, a difference that may
from generations of living close to people. Their presence remains
: some residents feed them, while others see them as pests.
why: “food and shelter” is the standard pair for what an animal needs. Danger, noise and competition are not things the suburbs “offered” as an attraction.
“a large … of their food” needs a word for a share of a total: a proportion. A reason, result or mistake is not a share of food.
Collocation: a difference may “result from” a cause, here generations of living near people. A difference cannot “benefit”, “suffer” or “escape” from generations.
The colon introduces opposing views — some feed them, others see them as pests — which is what “controversial” means. “extinct” and “invisible” contradict “presence”.

zh.Red foxes have been living in British ci: 至少從 1930 年代起，赤狐就一直生活在英國的城市中，當時擁有大花園的新郊區提供了充足的食物和 ____ 。雖然許多人以為都市狐狸主要靠翻垃圾桶維生，但針對牠們飲食的研究顯示，牠們有很大 ____ 的食物是居民刻意放出來的。城市狐狸往往也比鄉村狐狸大膽，這種差異可能 ____ 於好幾代與人類比鄰而居的生活。牠們的存在仍然 ____ ：有些居民會餵食牠們，另一些人則把牠們視為有害動物。
zh.“food and shelter” is the standard pair: food and shelter（食物和棲身之處）是描述動物需求的固定組合。danger、noise 和 competition 都不是郊區「提供」的吸引條件。
zh.“a large … of their food” needs a word f: 「牠們的食物中有很大的…」需要一個表示總量中某個份額的字：proportion（比例）。reason、result 或 mistake 都不是食物的份額。
zh.Collocation: a difference may “result fr: 固定搭配：差異可能 result from（源自）某個原因，這裡指好幾代與人類為鄰的生活。差異不能 benefit、suffer 或 escape from 世代。
zh.The colon introduces opposing views — so: 冒號引出了對立的看法——有人餵食、有人視為害獸——這正是 controversial（具爭議性）的意思。extinct 和 invisible 都與「存在」相矛盾。

questions.title: The minimum wage debate
parts: For decades, textbook economics predicted that raising the minimum wage would
jobs, since employers would hire fewer workers at a higher price. In the 1990s, a study comparing fast-food restaurants on either side of a state border found no such
after one state raised its minimum wage. The finding
a long and often heated debate that lasted more than twenty years. Most economists now accept that moderate increases have little effect on employment, though very large rises could still
harm, particularly in low-wage regions.
why: “employers would hire fewer workers” means jobs would be lost, so the prediction was that a higher minimum wage would destroy jobs. “create” is the opposite.
The study looked for the predicted job losses and did not find them: “no such effect”. The other nouns do not refer back to the prediction.
A debate that then “lasted more than twenty years” was started by the finding, so it sparked it. “ended”, “avoided” and “prevented” contradict the debate continuing.
Collocation: cause harm. You do not “take”, “keep” or “hold” harm.

zh.For decades, textbook economics predicte: 數十年來，教科書中的經濟學預測，提高最低工資會 ____ 工作機會，因為在價格較高的情況下，雇主會雇用較少的員工。1990 年代，一項比較州界兩側速食店的研究發現，在其中一州提高最低工資後，並沒有出現這樣的 ____ 。這項發現 ____ 了一場持續二十多年、經常很激烈的辯論。大多數經濟學家現在認為，適度的調漲對就業影響不大，不過非常大幅的調漲仍可能 ____ 傷害，尤其是在低工資地區。
zh.“employers would hire fewer workers” mea: 「雇主會雇用較少的員工」表示工作會減少，所以預測是提高最低工資會 destroy（摧毀）工作機會。create 則正好相反。
zh.The study looked for the predicted job l: 這項研究尋找預測中的就業減少，卻沒有找到：no such effect（沒有這樣的影響）。其他名詞都無法指回那個預測。
zh.A debate that then “lasted more than twe: 一場之後「持續二十多年」的辯論，是由這項發現引起的，所以是 sparked（引發）。ended、avoided 和 prevented 都與辯論持續進行相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: cause harm. You do not “tak: 固定搭配：cause harm（造成傷害）。英文不說 take、keep 或 hold harm。

questions.title: Second life for car batteries
parts: Electric cars depend on lithium-ion batteries, which contain valuable metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel. When a car battery can no longer hold enough
for driving, it often still has around seventy per cent of its original capacity, so it can be
for less demanding uses, such as storing solar power in homes. Eventually, however, the cells must be recycled. Current methods can
most of the metals, but they are energy-intensive, and researchers are trying to design batteries that are easier to take
why: A battery holds charge, and that is what fades as it ages. Batteries do not “hold enough weight, speed or heat” for driving.
A battery with seventy per cent capacity left can be reused for lighter tasks such as home solar storage. Nothing suggests it is repaired, and “rejected” contradicts the uses described.
Recycling aims to get the metals back: to recover them. Wasting or ignoring them is the opposite, and metals cannot be invented.
Phrasal verb: “take apart” means dismantle, which recycling requires. “take over”, “take off” and “take up” mean something quite different.

zh.Electric cars depend on lithium-ion batt: 電動車仰賴鋰離子電池，而電池中含有鋰、鈷和鎳等珍貴金屬。當汽車電池再也無法儲存足夠的 ____ 供行車使用時，它通常仍保有原始容量的百分之七十左右，所以可以被 ____ 於要求較低的用途，例如在家中儲存太陽能電力。然而，最終這些電池芯還是必須回收。目前的方法可以 ____ 大部分的金屬，但耗能很高，因此研究人員正試圖設計更容易 ____ 的電池。
zh.A battery holds charge, and that is what: 電池儲存的是 charge（電量），而這正是隨著老化而衰退的東西。電池不會為行車「儲存足夠的重量、速度或熱量」。
zh.A battery with seventy per cent capacity: 仍保有七成容量的電池可以被 reused（再利用）於較輕的用途，例如家用太陽能儲電。文中沒有提到修理，而 rejected 與文中描述的用途相矛盾。
zh.Recycling aims to get the metals back: t: 回收的目的是取回金屬：recover（回收、取回）。浪費或忽視金屬正好相反，而金屬也無法被發明。
zh.Phrasal verb: “take apart” means dismant: 片語動詞：take apart（拆解），這正是回收所需要的。take over、take off 和 take up 的意思完全不同。

questions.title: The Hanseatic League
parts: From the thirteenth to the fifteenth century, the Hanseatic League linked dozens of trading towns around the Baltic and North Sea. It was not a state but a
of merchants and cities that cooperated to protect their trade. Members shared
, set common standards for goods and, when necessary, organised boycotts against rulers who threatened their interests. The League’s power
as strong territorial states emerged and new trade routes shifted business towards the Atlantic, but several of its towns still
the title Hanseatic City today.
why: The sentence contrasts “not a state” with a looser structure of cooperating members: a network. “a state” repeats what the sentence denies, and a ruler or religion does not describe cooperating cities.
Members cooperated in practical ways, such as sharing information about prices and routes. Weather, ancestors and holidays are not things traders can decide to share.
New states emerging and trade moving to the Atlantic are causes of weakness, so the League’s power declined. The other verbs describe growth or return.
Collocation: a town “carries” a title, meaning it still holds it. “still lose”, “refuse” or “spend the title today” makes no sense.

zh.From the thirteenth to the fifteenth cen: 從十三世紀到十五世紀，漢薩同盟把波羅的海和北海周圍數十個貿易城鎮連結在一起。它不是一個國家，而是一個由商人和城市組成、為保護貿易而合作的 ____ 。成員之間共享 ____ ，為商品制定共同標準，必要時還會對威脅其利益的統治者發起抵制。隨著強大的領土國家興起，新的貿易路線又把生意轉向大西洋，同盟的勢力逐漸 ____ ，但它的一些城鎮至今仍 ____ 「漢薩城市」的稱號。
zh.The sentence contrasts “not a state” wit: 這句話把「不是一個國家」和一個由合作成員組成的鬆散結構對比：network（網絡）。state 重複了句子所否定的東西，而 ruler 或 religion 都無法描述互相合作的城市。
zh.Members cooperated in practical ways, su: 成員以實際的方式合作，例如分享價格和路線的 information（資訊）。天氣、祖先和假日都不是商人能決定分享的東西。
zh.New states emerging and trade moving to: 新國家興起和貿易轉向大西洋都是衰弱的原因，所以同盟的勢力 declined（衰退）。其他動詞描述的是成長或回歸。
zh.Collocation: a town “carries” a title, m: 固定搭配：城鎮 carries（擁有、保有）某個稱號。「至今仍失去、拒絕或花費這個稱號」都說不通。

questions.title: The value of wetlands
parts: Wetlands were long regarded as wasteland, and across Europe and North America more than half of them were
for farming or building. Scientists now recognise that they provide valuable services. A wetland acts like a sponge,
excess water during storms and releasing it slowly, which reduces flooding downstream. Wetland plants also filter pollutants, and peat bogs store more carbon per hectare than most
. Restoring wetlands is therefore increasingly seen as a cheap way to
against both floods and climate change.
why: Turning a wetland into farmland means removing its water, which is draining it. “protected” contradicts “regarded as wasteland”, and a wetland is already wet, so “flooded” makes no sense.
A sponge absorbs water: the wetland takes in storm water and releases it slowly. The other verbs do not describe holding water.
The comparison is with other natural carbon stores, and forests are the obvious benchmark. Factories, engines and roads release carbon rather than storing it.
Collocation: “insure against” a risk, meaning protect yourself from it. “compete”, “argue” and “vote against” do not describe protection from floods.

zh.Wetlands were long regarded as wasteland: 濕地長久以來被視為荒地，在歐洲和北美，超過一半的濕地被 ____ 以供耕作或建築使用。科學家現在認識到，濕地提供了寶貴的功能。濕地就像一塊海綿，在暴風雨期間 ____ 多餘的水，再慢慢釋放出來，減少下游的洪水。濕地植物還能過濾污染物，而泥炭沼澤每公頃儲存的碳比大多數 ____ 還多。因此，恢復濕地越來越被視為一種 ____ 洪水和氣候變遷的低成本方法。
zh.Turning a wetland into farmland means re: 把濕地變成農田就是移除其中的水，也就是 drained（排乾）。protected 與「被視為荒地」相矛盾，而濕地本來就是濕的，所以 flooded 說不通。
zh.A sponge absorbs water: the wetland take: 海綿會 absorb（吸收）水：濕地吸收暴雨的水再慢慢釋放。其他動詞都無法描述蓄水的作用。
zh.The comparison is with other natural car: 這裡比較的是其他天然的碳儲存庫，而 forests（森林）是最明顯的比較基準。工廠、引擎和道路會排放碳，而不是儲存碳。
zh.Collocation: “insure against” a risk, me: 固定搭配：insure against（防範）某種風險，也就是保護自己免受其害。compete、argue 和 vote against 都無法描述防範洪水。

questions.title: Music lessons and the brain
parts: It is often claimed that learning a musical instrument makes children more intelligent. Brain scans do show that musicians have
differences in areas involved in hearing and movement. However, controlled trials, in which children are randomly
to music lessons or another activity, have found little effect on general intelligence or school results. The benefits appear to be more
: musical training improves musical skills and perhaps some aspects of listening, but it is not a
to broader academic ability.
why: Brain scans detect the differences, so they are measurable. “invisible” and “imaginary” contradict what the scans show.
Randomised trials assign children to groups at random, which is what makes them controlled. “invited” and “paid” do not describe random allocation.
The colon lists narrow effects on musical skill and listening, so the benefits are specific. “general” contradicts “little effect on general intelligence”.
The point is that music is not a quick route to wider academic gains: it is not a shortcut to them. Reply, sequel and receipt make no sense with “to broader academic ability”.

zh.It is often claimed that learning a musi: 人們常說學習樂器能讓孩子變得更聰明。腦部掃描確實顯示，音樂家在負責聽覺和動作的腦區中有 ____ 的差異。然而，把孩子隨機 ____ 到音樂課或其他活動的對照試驗，發現這對一般智力或學業成績的影響很小。音樂訓練的好處似乎比較 ____ ：它能提升音樂技能，或許也能改善某些方面的聽力，但它並不是通往更廣泛學業能力的 ____ 。
zh.Brain scans detect the differences, so t: 腦部掃描偵測到了這些差異，所以它們是 measurable（可測量的）。invisible 和 imaginary 都與掃描結果相矛盾。
zh.Randomised trials assign children to gro: 隨機試驗會把孩子隨機 assigned（分派）到不同組別，這正是對照試驗的特點。invited 和 paid 都無法描述隨機分配。
zh.The colon lists narrow effects on musica: 冒號後面列出的是對音樂技能和聽力的狹窄影響，所以好處是 specific（特定的）。general 與「對一般智力影響很小」相矛盾。
zh.The point is that music is not a quick r: 重點在於音樂並不是通往更廣泛學業成就的快速途徑：它不是一條 shortcut（捷徑）。reply、sequel 和 receipt 搭配「通往更廣泛的學業能力」都說不通。

questions.title: Finding lost cities with lasers
parts: For centuries, dense jungle hid the ruins of ancient Maya cities in Central America. Lidar, a technique that fires laser pulses from an aircraft and
how long they take to bounce back, has changed that. By filtering out the signals reflected by leaves, researchers can create detailed maps of the ground beneath the
. Surveys have revealed tens of thousands of previously unknown structures, suggesting that the Maya population was far
than once believed. The technique does not replace excavation, but it tells archaeologists where to
why: Lidar works by timing the reflections, so it measures how long they take. Guessing or ignoring the time would produce no map.
“signals reflected by leaves” points to the layer of treetops above the ground: the canopy. The passage is about jungle, not an ocean, desert or city.
Tens of thousands of new structures imply more people, so the population was larger than believed. “smaller” reverses the evidence.
Excavation means digging, and lidar shows archaeologists where to dig. The other verbs have nothing to do with excavation.

zh.For centuries, dense jungle hid the ruin: 數個世紀以來，茂密的叢林掩蓋了中美洲古代馬雅城市的遺跡。光達是一種從飛機上發射雷射脈衝、並 ____ 脈衝反彈回來所需時間的技術，它改變了這種情況。研究人員濾除樹葉反射的訊號後，就能繪製出 ____ 下方地面的詳細地圖。調查發現了數以萬計過去未知的建築，顯示馬雅人口遠比過去認為的 ____ 。這項技術並不能取代挖掘，但它能告訴考古學家該在哪裡 ____ 。
zh.Lidar works by timing the reflections, s: 光達的原理是計算反射的時間，所以它 measures（測量）反彈所需的時間。猜測或忽略時間都無法產生地圖。
zh.“signals reflected by leaves” points to: 「被樹葉反射的訊號」指的是地面上方的樹頂層：canopy（樹冠層）。這篇文章談的是叢林，而不是海洋、沙漠或城市。
zh.Tens of thousands of new structures impl: 數以萬計的新建築意味著人口更多，所以人口比過去認為的 larger（更多）。smaller 把證據顛倒了。
zh.Excavation means digging, and lidar show: 挖掘就是 dig（挖），而光達告訴考古學家該在哪裡挖。其他動詞都與挖掘無關。

questions.title: Why expectations matter for inflation
parts: Central banks pay close attention not only to current inflation but also to what people
it to be in the future. If workers believe prices will rise quickly, they ask for larger pay increases, and firms raise prices in
, which can make the belief come true. For this reason, central banks try to keep expectations
by stating a clear inflation target and acting consistently. When that credibility is lost, bringing inflation back
can require much higher interest rates.
why: The topic is expectations, and “what people expect it to be in the future” is the natural construction. “remember” refers to the past, and “prefer” and “forbid” are not predictions.
Fixed phrase: “in anticipation” means in advance of something expected. Firms raise prices because they anticipate rises; the other nouns do not form a fitting phrase.
Economists say expectations are “anchored” when they stay steady around the target, which is the aim of a clear target. Hidden, doubled or reversed expectations are not.
Phrasal verb: “bring inflation back down” to the target. “out”, “away” and “off” do not express reducing it.

zh.Central banks pay close attention not on: 中央銀行不僅密切關注目前的通貨膨脹，也關注人們 ____ 未來的通膨會是多少。如果勞工相信物價會迅速上漲，他們就會要求更高的加薪，而企業也會 ____ 地提高價格，這可能讓這種信念成真。因此，中央銀行會透過明確的通膨目標和一致的行動，努力讓預期保持 ____ 。一旦失去了這種公信力，要把通膨重新 ____ 可能需要高得多的利率。
zh.The topic is expectations, and “what peo: 主題是預期，而「人們 expect（預期）未來的通膨會是多少」是自然的句構。remember 指的是過去，而 prefer 和 forbid 都不是預測。
zh.Fixed phrase: “in anticipation” means in: 固定用語：in anticipation（預先、預期地）表示在預料的事情發生之前。企業因為預期物價上漲而漲價；其他名詞都無法構成合適的片語。
zh.Economists say expectations are “anchore: 當預期穩定地維持在目標附近時，經濟學家會說預期被 anchored（錨定），這正是設定明確目標的目的。hidden、doubled 或 reversed 的預期都不是目的。
zh.Phrasal verb: “bring inflation back down: 片語動詞：bring inflation back down（讓通膨回落）到目標水準。out、away 和 off 都無法表示降低。

questions.title: Antarctic krill
parts: Antarctic krill are small shrimp-like animals, rarely longer than six centimetres, yet their combined weight may
that of all the humans on Earth. They form the base of the Southern Ocean food
, feeding whales, seals, penguins and fish. Krill depend on algae that grow on the underside of sea ice, so the
of winter ice in some regions is a serious concern. A growing fishery for krill, used in fish feed and supplements, adds further
on the population.
why: “small … yet” sets up a surprisingly large total: their combined weight may exceed that of all humans. The other verbs do not make a comparison of size.
Ecologists call the feeding relationships in an ecosystem the food web. A food bank or food store is something quite different.
Krill depend on algae under the ice, so the concern must be losing that ice. Growth of winter ice would help them.
A fishery removes krill, so it adds pressure on the population. Support and protection are the opposite of what a fishery does.

zh.Antarctic krill are small shrimp-like an: 南極磷蝦是一種外形像蝦的小型動物，體長很少超過六公分，但牠們的總重量可能 ____ 地球上所有人類的總重量。牠們是南冰洋食物 ____ 的基礎，餵養了鯨魚、海豹、企鵝和魚類。磷蝦依賴生長在海冰底面的藻類，所以某些地區冬季海冰的 ____ 是一個嚴重的問題。日益擴大的磷蝦漁業被用於製造魚飼料和營養補充品，對磷蝦族群造成了更多 ____ 。
zh.“small … yet” sets up a surprisingly lar: 「體型很小…但是」鋪陳了一個出乎意料的龐大總量：牠們的總重量可能 exceed（超過）所有人類。其他動詞都無法構成大小的比較。
zh.Ecologists call the feeding relationship: 生態學家把生態系中的攝食關係稱為 food web（食物網）。food bank（食物銀行）或 food store 則是完全不同的東西。
zh.Krill depend on algae under the ice, so: 磷蝦依賴海冰下的藻類，所以令人擔憂的一定是海冰的 loss（消失）。冬季海冰增加反而對牠們有利。
zh.A fishery removes krill, so it adds pres: 漁業會捕撈磷蝦，所以它對族群增加了 pressure（壓力）。support 和 protection 都與漁業的作用相反。

questions.title: Who maintains open-source software?
parts: Much of the software that runs the internet is open source, meaning its code is freely available for anyone to use,
and share. Many projects are maintained by volunteers, sometimes by only one or two people, even though large companies
on them every day. This creates a risk: a small team with no
may struggle to fix security problems quickly. In recent years, some companies and governments have begun to
the maintainers of critical projects, recognising that free software still has costs.
why: Open-source licences let people use, modify and share code. Hiding or deleting it contradicts “freely available”.
Collocation: depend on. The sentence stresses how much large companies rely on volunteer work every day.
The last sentence says free software “still has costs”, so the risk is a team without money: no funding.
Recognising that the software has costs explains why they began to pay the maintainers. Ignoring or criticising them would not meet those costs.

zh.Much of the software that runs the inter: 支撐網際網路運作的軟體中，有很大一部分是開放原始碼軟體，也就是任何人都可以免費使用、____ 和分享其程式碼。許多專案是由志工維護的，有時只有一兩個人，即使大公司每天都 ____ 這些專案。這就造成了一種風險：一個沒有 ____ 的小團隊，可能很難迅速修補安全漏洞。近年來，一些公司和政府開始 ____ 關鍵專案的維護者，因為他們認識到免費軟體仍然有成本。
zh.Open-source licences let people use, mod: 開放原始碼授權讓人們可以使用、modify（修改）和分享程式碼。隱藏或刪除程式碼與「免費提供」相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: depend on. The sentence str: 固定搭配：depend on（依賴）。這句話強調大公司每天有多麼依賴志工的工作。
zh.The last sentence says free software “st: 最後一句說免費軟體「仍然有成本」，所以風險在於團隊沒有錢：no funding（沒有資金）。
zh.Recognising that the software has costs: 認識到軟體有成本，就解釋了他們為什麼開始 pay（支付報酬給）維護者。忽視或批評他們都無法支付這些成本。

questions.title: Do sugar taxes work?
parts: Several countries have introduced taxes on sugary soft drinks to
obesity and tooth decay. Critics predicted that consumers would simply pay the higher price, but the evidence has been more encouraging. In the United Kingdom, the tax was designed to
manufacturers rather than shoppers: drinks with less sugar were taxed at a lower rate or not at all. Many companies
their recipes before the tax began, and the average sugar content of soft drinks fell sharply. The effect on obesity is harder to
, because diet depends on many other foods.
why: A health tax aims to reduce obesity and tooth decay. “cause”, “celebrate” and “advertise” make no sense as the purpose of the tax.
By taxing sugar content, the tax aimed at manufacturers rather than shoppers: it was designed to target them. It does not “reward” them.
The average sugar content fell because companies changed their recipes to avoid the tax. “protected” or “copied” their recipes would not lower the sugar.
“because diet depends on many other foods” explains why the effect is difficult to isolate, so it is harder to measure.

zh.Several countries have introduced taxes: 好幾個國家已經對含糖飲料課稅，以 ____ 肥胖和蛀牙。批評者預測消費者只會乖乖付更高的價錢，但證據卻更令人鼓舞。在英國，這項稅的設計是 ____ 製造商而不是消費者：含糖量較低的飲料稅率較低，甚至完全不課稅。許多公司在稅制開始之前就 ____ 了配方，飲料的平均含糖量也大幅下降。對肥胖的影響則比較難 ____ ，因為飲食還取決於許多其他食物。
zh.A health tax aims to reduce obesity and: 健康稅的目的是 reduce（減少）肥胖和蛀牙。cause、celebrate 和 advertise 作為課稅的目的都說不通。
zh.By taxing sugar content, the tax aimed a: 透過對含糖量課稅，這項稅針對的是製造商而不是消費者：它的設計是 target（針對）製造商，而不是獎勵他們。
zh.The average sugar content fell because c: 平均含糖量下降，是因為公司 changed（改變）了配方以避稅。protected 或 copied 配方都無法降低含糖量。
zh.“because diet depends on many other food: 「因為飲食還取決於許多其他食物」說明了這種影響很難單獨區分出來，所以比較難 measure（測量）。

questions.title: The first writing
parts: The earliest known writing, cuneiform, appeared in Mesopotamia around 3200 BCE. It did not begin as a way to record stories or laws but as a system for
goods such as grain and livestock. Scribes pressed a reed into wet clay to make wedge-shaped marks, and the tablets were then dried in the sun or
in kilns. Over centuries the signs became more abstract and began to
sounds as well as objects, allowing the script to record several different languages. Hundreds of thousands of tablets have
, because baked clay lasts far longer than paper.
why: Early writing was a form of accounting, so it was a system for counting goods such as grain and livestock. Cooking, painting or hiding goods is not what a writing system records.
Kilns are ovens for firing clay, so the tablets were baked. Clay cannot be frozen, washed or folded in a kiln.
Signs that stand for sounds represent them, and that is what allowed several languages to be written.
“because baked clay lasts far longer than paper” explains why so many tablets have survived. “disappeared” contradicts the reason given.

zh.The earliest known writing, cuneiform, a: 已知最早的文字——楔形文字——大約在西元前 3200 年出現於美索不達米亞。它最初並不是用來記錄故事或法律，而是一套用來 ____ 穀物和牲畜等物品的系統。書記員把蘆葦筆壓進濕黏土中，刻出楔形的記號，然後把泥板放在陽光下曬乾，或放進窯中 ____ 。數個世紀以來，這些符號變得越來越抽象，並開始 ____ 聲音和物體，使這種文字能記錄好幾種不同的語言。數十萬片泥板得以 ____ ，因為燒過的黏土比紙張持久得多。
zh.Early writing was a form of accounting,: 早期的文字是一種記帳方式，所以它是一套 counting（計算、點算）穀物和牲畜等物品的系統。烹煮、繪畫或隱藏物品都不是文字系統所記錄的內容。
zh.Kilns are ovens for firing clay, so the: 窯是燒製黏土的爐子，所以泥板被 baked（燒製）。黏土不能在窯中被冷凍、清洗或摺疊。
zh.Signs that stand for sounds represent th: 代表聲音的符號就是在 represent（代表）聲音，這正是讓好幾種語言得以被書寫的原因。
zh.“because baked clay lasts far longer tha: 「因為燒過的黏土比紙張持久得多」解釋了為什麼有這麼多泥板 survived（保存下來）。disappeared 與所給的理由相矛盾。

questions.title: The wisdom of crowds
parts: In 1906, the scientist Francis Galton visited a country fair where visitors guessed the weight of an ox. Individual guesses varied widely, but the
of all the guesses was within one per cent of the true weight. This effect, later called the wisdom of crowds, works only under certain
. The people must judge independently, because if they influence one another, their errors no longer
out. That is why a group discussion can sometimes produce a
estimate than simply averaging private opinions.
why: Combining many guesses into one number means taking their average. The “winner” would be a single person’s guess, not all of them.
“works only under certain conditions” is the standard phrase, and the next sentence goes on to give one condition.
Phrasal verb: errors “cancel out” when high and low guesses balance each other. That is exactly what independence allows.
Discussion makes people influence each other, which destroys independence, so it can produce a worse estimate than averaging private opinions.

zh.In 1906, the scientist Francis Galton vi: 1906 年，科學家法蘭西斯・高爾頓參觀了一個鄉村市集，那裡的遊客在猜一頭牛的重量。個別的猜測差異很大，但所有猜測的 ____ 與實際重量只差不到百分之一。這種後來被稱為「群眾智慧」的效應，只有在特定的 ____ 下才會成立。人們必須獨立做出判斷，因為如果他們互相影響，他們的誤差就不再能互相 ____ 。這就是為什麼小組討論有時會產生比單純平均個人意見更 ____ 的估計。
zh.Combining many guesses into one number m: 把許多猜測合併成一個數字，就是取它們的 average（平均值）。winner 只是一個人的猜測，而不是全部的猜測。
zh.“works only under certain conditions” is: works only under certain conditions（只有在特定條件下才成立）是標準用語，而下一句接著就提出了其中一個條件。
zh.Phrasal verb: errors “cancel out” when h: 片語動詞：當偏高和偏低的猜測彼此抵銷時，誤差就會 cancel out（互相抵消）。這正是獨立判斷所帶來的效果。
zh.Discussion makes people influence each o: 討論會讓人們互相影響，破壞了獨立性，所以它可能產生比平均個人意見更 worse（更差）的估計。

questions.passage: Artificial light at night has increased by roughly two per cent a year worldwide over the past decade, and satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs. The ecological effects are better documented than many people assume. Migrating birds that navigate by the stars are drawn towards illuminated buildings, where large numbers die in collisions. Sea turtle hatchlings, which instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea, crawl inland towards street lights instead. Insects are affected on a vast scale: a single street lamp can attract and exhaust moths from a wide area, disrupting the pollination of night-flowering plants. The effects on people are less certain. Exposure to light at night suppresses melatonin, a hormone involved in sleep, and some studies link bright outdoor lighting with poorer sleep, but it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life such as noise. Unlike many environmental problems, however, light pollution can be reversed almost instantly. Shielding lamps so that they point downwards, reducing their brightness late at night and choosing warmer colours can cut the impact dramatically without leaving streets unsafe.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated or implied in the passage?
o: Satellite data may underestimate the growth of artificial light.
Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by lights on land.
Bright outdoor lighting has been proven to cause poor sleep in humans.
Light pollution can be reduced quickly without making streets unsafe.
LED lighting has reduced the ecological impact of street lamps.
why: Correct. “satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs.”
Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea” but “crawl inland towards street lights instead”.
Wrong. The passage says “The effects on people are less certain” and that “it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life”. A link is not proof.
Correct. Light pollution “can be reversed almost instantly”, and the fixes cut the impact “without leaving streets unsafe”.
Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the impact. The only mention of LEDs is that satellites cannot detect their blue-rich light.

zh.Artificial light at night has increased: 過去十年來，全世界夜間的人造光每年增加約百分之二，而衛星測量可能低估了這個變化，因為感測器無法偵測現代 LED 燈所發出的富含藍光的光線。它對生態的影響，比許多人以為的有更充分的紀錄。靠星星導航的遷徙鳥類會被燈火通明的建築物吸引，大量的鳥因撞擊而死亡。剛孵化的小海龜本能地朝海面上較亮的地平線移動，卻反而朝內陸的路燈爬去。昆蟲受到的影響規模更是龐大：一盞路燈就能把廣大範圍內的飛蛾吸引過來並使其精疲力竭，干擾夜間開花植物的授粉。對人類的影響則比較不確定。夜間照光會抑制褪黑激素這種與睡眠有關的荷爾蒙，也有一些研究把明亮的戶外照明與較差的睡眠連結在一起，但很難把照明與噪音等都市生活的其他特徵區分開來。然而，與許多環境問題不同的是，光害幾乎可以立即逆轉。為燈具加上遮罩使其朝下照射、在深夜調降亮度，以及選擇較暖的色溫，都能大幅降低影響，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.Which of the following are stated or imp: 下列哪些是文章中陳述或暗示的內容？
zh.Satellite data may underestimate the gro: 衛星數據可能低估了人造光的增長。
zh.Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by l: 剛孵化的小海龜可能被陸地上的燈光誤導。
zh.Bright outdoor lighting has been proven: 已經證實明亮的戶外照明會導致人類睡眠品質不佳。
zh.Light pollution can be reduced quickly w: 光害可以迅速減少，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.LED lighting has reduced the ecological: LED 照明已經降低了路燈對生態的影響。
zh.Correct. “satellite measurements probabl: 正確。"satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs."
zh.Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move: 正確。小海龜 "instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea"，但卻 "crawl inland towards street lights instead"。
zh.Wrong. The passage says “The effects on: 錯誤。文章說 "The effects on people are less certain"，而且 "it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life"。有關聯並不等於有證據。
zh.Correct. Light pollution “can be reverse: 正確。光害 "can be reversed almost instantly"，而這些改善方法能降低影響 "without leaving streets unsafe"。
zh.Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the imp: 錯誤。文章沒有說 LED 降低了影響。唯一提到 LED 的地方，是衛星無法偵測它們富含藍光的光線。

questions.passage: The two-day weekend is a surprisingly recent invention. For most of history, working people had at most one day of rest, usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims. In nineteenth-century Britain, many factory workers informally extended their rest by taking Monday off, a custom known as Saint Monday, which employers found impossible to stamp out. Some manufacturers eventually offered a compromise: a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday. The full two-day weekend spread in the twentieth century. In the United States, the carmaker Henry Ford introduced a five-day week in 1926, arguing that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars. During the Great Depression, shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people. By the 1940s the Saturday–Sunday weekend was standard in much of the industrialised world. Today some economists predict that the same pressures, rising productivity and changing ideas about leisure, could eventually produce a three-day weekend, although so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.
questions.q: Which of the following statements are supported by the passage?
o: Before the modern weekend, the day of rest depended largely on religion.
Saturday half-days were partly a response to workers taking Mondays off.
Henry Ford introduced the five-day week mainly to reduce accidents in his factories.
Shorter working weeks were seen as a way to spread work during the Depression.
A three-day weekend has already become standard in several industrialised countries.
why: Correct. The one day of rest was “usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims.”
Correct. Employers offered “a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday”, because workers were taking Mondays off.
Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars.” Accidents are never mentioned.
Correct. “shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people.”
Wrong. “so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.” A prediction is not a present fact.

zh.The two-day weekend is a surprisingly re: 兩天的週末其實是相當晚近才出現的。在歷史的大部分時間裡，勞動者最多只有一天休息日，而且通常由宗教決定：基督徒是星期日，猶太人是星期六，穆斯林則是星期五。在十九世紀的英國，許多工廠工人會非正式地在星期一休假來延長休息時間，這種習俗被稱為「聖星期一」，雇主們發現根本無法杜絕。一些製造商最後提出了折衷方案：星期六放半天假，交換條件是星期一要確實出勤。完整的兩天週末在二十世紀普及開來。在美國，汽車製造商亨利・福特於 1926 年實施每週五天工作制，他主張擁有更多休閒時間的工人會購買更多消費品，包括汽車。在經濟大蕭條期間，縮短工時也被推廣為讓更多人分攤有限工作的一種方法。到了 1940 年代，星期六和星期日的週末已成為工業化世界大部分地區的標準。如今，一些經濟學家預測，同樣的壓力——生產力提高以及對休閒觀念的改變——最終可能會帶來三天的週末，不過到目前為止，試行只限於少數幾家公司。
zh.Which of the following statements are su: 下列哪些敘述有文章內容的支持？
zh.Before the modern weekend, the day of re: 在現代週末出現之前，休息日大多取決於宗教。
zh.Saturday half-days were partly a respons: 星期六放半天假，部分是為了回應工人在星期一休假的情況。
zh.Henry Ford introduced the five-day week: 亨利・福特實施每週五天工作制，主要是為了減少工廠裡的意外。
zh.Shorter working weeks were seen as a way: 縮短工時被視為在大蕭條期間分攤工作的一種方式。
zh.A three-day weekend has already become s: 三天的週末已經在好幾個工業化國家成為標準。
zh.Correct. The one day of rest was “usuall: 正確。一天的休息日 "usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims."
zh.Correct. Employers offered “a half-day o: 正確。雇主提供 "a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday"，因為工人會在星期一休假。
zh.Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with mo: 錯誤。福特主張 "that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars." 文章從未提到意外。
zh.Correct. “shorter weeks were also promot: 正確。"shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people."
zh.Wrong. “so far trials have been confined: 錯誤。"so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies." 預測並不是現在的事實。

questions.passage: Yawning is one of the most familiar human behaviours, yet its purpose remains disputed. The popular explanation, that we yawn to take in more oxygen, has not survived testing: people breathing air with extra oxygen yawn just as often, and those breathing air with extra carbon dioxide do not yawn more. A more promising idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. Yawns are more frequent when the brain is warm, and one study found that people holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning. Yawning is also contagious, at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs. Contagious yawning appears in children only at around the age of four or five, roughly when they begin to understand other people’s mental states, and some studies suggest it is more common between friends and relatives than between strangers. This has led researchers to link it with empathy, although the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.
questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
o: Experiments do not support the idea that yawning increases oxygen intake.
Cooling the forehead appears to reduce yawning.
Contagious yawning is found only in humans.
Newborn babies already yawn when they see others yawn.
The link between contagious yawning and empathy is not firmly established.
why: Correct. The oxygen explanation “has not survived testing”: extra oxygen does not reduce yawning, and extra carbon dioxide does not increase it.
Correct. People “holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning occurs “at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning “appears in children only at around the age of four or five.”
Correct. “the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.”

zh.Yawning is one of the most familiar huma: 打哈欠是人類最熟悉的行為之一，但它的目的至今仍有爭議。一般流行的解釋是我們打哈欠是為了吸入更多氧氣，但這個說法經不起檢驗：呼吸含氧量較高空氣的人，打哈欠的次數並沒有減少，而呼吸二氧化碳較多空氣的人，打哈欠的次數也沒有增加。一個較有希望的說法是，打哈欠有助於為大腦降溫。大腦溫度較高時，打哈欠的頻率較高，而一項研究發現，把冰敷袋貼在額頭上的人，在觀看別人打哈欠的影片時，打哈欠的次數較少。打哈欠也會傳染，至少在人類、黑猩猩和某些狗身上是如此。傳染性的打哈欠在兒童約四、五歲時才會出現，大約是他們開始理解他人心理狀態的時候，而且有些研究顯示，它在朋友和親人之間比在陌生人之間更常見。這使研究人員把它與同理心連結起來，不過證據並不一致，一些規模較大的研究發現，年齡比同理心更能解釋其中的差異。
zh.Which of the following can be concluded: 從文章中可以得出下列哪些結論？

zh.Wrong. Contagious yawning occurs “at lea: 錯誤。傳染性打哈欠出現在 "at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs."

questions.passage: Dogs were the first animals to be domesticated, but when and where it happened remains contested. Genetic studies suggest that dogs descend from a population of wolves that has since become extinct, rather than from the grey wolves alive today. Estimates of the timing range from about fifteen thousand to more than thirty thousand years ago, well before the beginning of farming. This timing matters, because it means dogs were domesticated by hunter-gatherers rather than settled farmers. One popular theory suggests that the process began without deliberate human effort. Wolves that were less fearful of people may have scavenged near human camps, gaining access to food scraps, and over many generations these bolder animals became increasingly tolerant of humans. People may later have valued them for hunting and as guards. Some researchers have also suggested that dogs were domesticated more than once, in both Europe and East Asia, although this remains a minority view. What is widely accepted is that the relationship shaped both species: dogs evolved the ability to digest starch, a change that tracks the spread of human agriculture.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Dogs were domesticated before humans began farming.
Modern grey wolves are the direct ancestors of dogs.
Domestication may have begun with wolves scavenging near human camps.
Most researchers agree that dogs were domesticated twice.
Dogs developed the ability to digest starch.
why: Correct. The timing is “well before the beginning of farming”, so dogs “were domesticated by hunter-gatherers rather than settled farmers”.
Wrong. Dogs descend from “a population of wolves that has since become extinct, rather than from the grey wolves alive today”.
Correct. “Wolves that were less fearful of people may have scavenged near human camps, gaining access to food scraps.”
Wrong. Two domestications is described as “a minority view”, the opposite of what most researchers think.
Correct. “dogs evolved the ability to digest starch, a change that tracks the spread of human agriculture.”

zh.Dogs were the first animals to be domest: 狗是最早被馴化的動物，但牠們在何時何地被馴化，至今仍有爭議。基因研究顯示，狗是從一群如今已經滅絕的狼演變而來的，而不是源自現存的灰狼。對於馴化時間的估計，從大約一萬五千年前到三萬多年前都有，遠早於農業開始之前。這個時間點很重要，因為這意味著狗是由狩獵採集者、而不是定居的農民所馴化的。一個廣為流傳的理論認為，這個過程並非人類刻意推動的。比較不怕人的狼可能在人類營地附近覓食，取得剩餘的食物，而經過許多世代，這些較大膽的動物變得越來越能容忍人類。人們後來可能看重牠們在狩獵和看守上的用處。也有一些研究人員認為，狗曾在歐洲和東亞被馴化過不只一次，不過這仍是少數人的看法。普遍被接受的是，這種關係塑造了兩個物種：狗演化出了消化澱粉的能力，而這個變化與人類農業的擴散相吻合。

questions.passage: Cities are usually thought of as hostile to wildlife, yet a surprising number of species thrive in them. Peregrine falcons nest on skyscrapers, which resemble the cliffs they use in the wild, and feed on the plentiful city pigeons. Some urban areas even contain more plant species than the surrounding countryside, partly because gardens and parks include many non-native plants and partly because intensive farming has reduced diversity in rural areas. However, species richness can be misleading. Cities tend to favour adaptable generalists, such as foxes, crows and rats, while specialists that depend on particular habitats disappear. As a result, urban wildlife around the world is becoming increasingly similar, a process ecologists call biotic homogenisation. There are also costs for the animals that succeed. Urban birds often sing at a higher pitch to be heard above traffic, and artificial light at night can disrupt their breeding cycles. Planners are increasingly trying to support urban wildlife through green roofs, wildlife corridors connecting parks, and the reduction of unnecessary lighting.
questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
o: Some cities have more plant species than nearby rural areas.
Cities benefit specialist species more than generalists.
Urban wildlife in different cities is becoming more alike.
Peregrine falcons avoid cities because they lack cliffs.
City life can impose costs even on species that do well there.
why: Correct. “Some urban areas even contain more plant species than the surrounding countryside.”
Wrong. The reverse: cities “favour adaptable generalists”, while specialists “disappear”.
Correct. “urban wildlife around the world is becoming increasingly similar”, which is called biotic homogenisation.
Wrong. Falcons nest on skyscrapers, “which resemble the cliffs they use in the wild”.
Correct. “There are also costs for the animals that succeed”, such as higher-pitched song and disrupted breeding.

zh.Cities are usually thought of as hostile: 城市通常被認為對野生動物不友善，但有數量驚人的物種在城市中繁衍興盛。遊隼在摩天大樓上築巢，因為摩天大樓很像牠們在野外使用的懸崖，而且牠們以城市中大量的鴿子為食。有些都市地區的植物種類甚至比周圍的鄉村還多，部分原因是花園和公園中有許多外來植物，部分原因則是集約農業降低了鄉村地區的多樣性。然而，物種豐富度可能會誤導人。城市往往有利於適應力強的泛化物種，例如狐狸、烏鴉和老鼠，而依賴特定棲地的特化物種則會消失。因此，世界各地的都市野生動物變得越來越相似，生態學家稱這個過程為「生物同質化」。對於那些成功適應的動物來說，也有代價。都市鳥類常常用更高的音調唱歌，好讓聲音蓋過車流聲，而夜間的人工照明可能會干擾牠們的繁殖週期。規劃者越來越常透過綠屋頂、連接公園的生態廊道，以及減少不必要的照明，來支持都市野生動物。
zh.Which of the following can be concluded: 從文章中可以得出下列哪些結論？

zh.Wrong. The reverse: cities “favour adapt: 錯誤。正好相反：城市 "favour adaptable generalists"，而特化物種則會 "disappear"。
