zh.Only when this final stage shows clear p: 只有當這個最後階段顯示出明確的保護效果時，主管機關才會考慮給予核准。
zh.Before a new vaccine can be approved, it: 一種新疫苗在獲得核准之前，必須通過好幾個階段的測試。——開頭句。它介紹了 "a new vaccine"，並預告了段落其餘部分要描述的各個階段。
zh.It is first given to a small group of he: 它首先會給一小群健康的志願者施打，以確認它是安全的。——"It is first given" 指回疫苗，並開始描述各個階段。
zh.If no serious side effects appear, a lar: 如果沒有出現嚴重的副作用，就會進行規模較大的試驗，研究最佳劑量和免疫反應。——"If no serious side effects appear" 取決於前一階段的安全性檢查。
zh.Finally, thousands of people take part i: 最後，數千人會參與一項比較疫苗與安慰劑的試驗。——"Finally" 標示最後一個測試階段，接在劑量試驗之後。
zh.Only when this final stage shows clear p: 只有當這個最後階段顯示出明確的保護效果時，主管機關才會考慮給予核准。——結尾句。"this final stage" 指回大型試驗，而核准結束了整個流程。

order: Sunlight looks white, but it is actually a mixture of all the colours of the rainbow.
When it enters the atmosphere, this light collides with the tiny molecules of gas in the air.
These molecules scatter short, blue wavelengths far more strongly than long, red ones.
As a result, blue light reaches our eyes from every direction, and the whole sky appears blue.
At sunset, however, light travels through much more air, so most of the blue is scattered away and the sky turns red.
why: The opener. It names sunlight in full and sets up the key fact that it contains every colour.
“it” and “this light” refer back to sunlight, which now enters the atmosphere.
“These molecules” are the gas molecules just mentioned, and the sentence explains what they do to the colours.
“As a result” gives the consequence of the scattering: a blue sky.
The closer. “however” introduces the exception at sunset, which only makes sense once the blue sky has been explained.

zh.Sunlight looks white, but it is actually: 陽光看起來是白色的，但它其實是彩虹中所有顏色的混合。
zh.When it enters the atmosphere, this ligh: 當這些光進入大氣層時，會與空氣中微小的氣體分子發生碰撞。
zh.These molecules scatter short, blue wave: 這些分子散射短波長藍光的程度，遠比散射長波長紅光強烈。
zh.As a result, blue light reaches our eyes: 因此，藍光從四面八方進入我們的眼睛，整片天空看起來就是藍色的。
zh.At sunset, however, light travels throug: 然而在日落時，光線要穿過更多的空氣，所以大部分的藍光都被散射掉，天空就變成了紅色。
zh.Sunlight looks white, but it is actually: 陽光看起來是白色的，但它其實是彩虹中所有顏色的混合。——開頭句。它完整說出「陽光」，並提出它包含所有顏色這個關鍵事實。
zh.When it enters the atmosphere, this ligh: 當這些光進入大氣層時，會與空氣中微小的氣體分子發生碰撞。——"it" 和 "this light" 指回陽光，而陽光現在進入了大氣層。
zh.These molecules scatter short, blue wave: 這些分子散射短波長藍光的程度，遠比散射長波長紅光強烈。——"These molecules" 就是剛才提到的氣體分子，而這句話說明了它們對顏色的作用。
zh.As a result, blue light reaches our eyes: 因此，藍光從四面八方進入我們的眼睛，整片天空看起來就是藍色的。——"As a result" 提出散射的結果：藍色的天空。
zh.At sunset, however, light travels throug: 然而在日落時，光線要穿過更多的空氣，所以大部分的藍光都被散射掉，天空就變成了紅色。——結尾句。"however" 引出日落時的例外，這只有在解釋了藍天之後才說得通。

order: The earliest bicycle, built in Germany in 1817, had no pedals at all.
Riders pushed it along with their feet, which made it tiring on anything but flat ground.
Pedals were added in the 1860s, but they were fixed to a huge front wheel that made the machine unstable.
The so-called safety bicycle of the 1880s solved this with two equal wheels and a chain driving the rear one.
Its basic design has hardly changed since, which is why a modern bicycle would look familiar to a Victorian rider.
why: The opener. It introduces “the earliest bicycle” with a date and refers back to nothing.
“pushed it along with their feet” explains how a bicycle without pedals was ridden.
Adding pedals solves the problem just described, but the huge wheel creates a new one.
“solved this” refers to the instability caused by the huge front wheel.
The closer. “Its basic design” refers back to the safety bicycle and brings the story to the present.

zh.The earliest bicycle, built in Germany i: 最早的自行車於 1817 年在德國製造，完全沒有踏板。
zh.Riders pushed it along with their feet,: 騎士用雙腳推著它前進，所以只要不是平地，騎起來就很累。
zh.Pedals were added in the 1860s, but they: 踏板在 1860 年代被加上去，但它們裝在一個巨大的前輪上，使這種車很不穩定。
zh.The so-called safety bicycle of the 1880: 1880 年代所謂的「安全自行車」解決了這個問題，它有兩個大小相同的輪子，並用鏈條帶動後輪。
zh.Its basic design has hardly changed sinc: 從那以後，它的基本設計幾乎沒有改變，這就是為什麼一輛現代自行車在維多利亞時代的騎士眼中也會很眼熟。
zh.The earliest bicycle, built in Germany i: 最早的自行車於 1817 年在德國製造，完全沒有踏板。——開頭句。它以年份介紹了「最早的自行車」，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.Riders pushed it along with their feet,: 騎士用雙腳推著它前進，所以只要不是平地，騎起來就很累。——"pushed it along with their feet" 說明了沒有踏板的自行車如何騎乘。
zh.Pedals were added in the 1860s, but they: 踏板在 1860 年代被加上去，但它們裝在一個巨大的前輪上，使這種車很不穩定。——加上踏板解決了剛才描述的問題，但巨大的前輪又造成了新的問題。
zh.The so-called safety bicycle of the 1880: 1880 年代所謂的「安全自行車」解決了這個問題，它有兩個大小相同的輪子，並用鏈條帶動後輪。——"solved this" 指的是巨大前輪造成的不穩定。
zh.Its basic design has hardly changed sinc: 從那以後，它的基本設計幾乎沒有改變，這就是為什麼一輛現代自行車在維多利亞時代的騎士眼中也會很眼熟。——結尾句。"Its basic design" 指回安全自行車，並把故事帶到現在。

order: By the early nineteenth century, astronomers had noticed that Uranus was not moving exactly as predicted.
Some suggested that the pull of an unknown planet further out was disturbing its orbit.
Working independently, two mathematicians used Uranus’s movements to calculate where that planet should be.
In 1846, an astronomer in Berlin pointed his telescope at the predicted position and found Neptune within an hour.
It was the first planet to be discovered through mathematics rather than by chance observation.
why: The opener. It sets the time and states the puzzle about Uranus, referring back to nothing.
“its orbit” refers to Uranus, and the sentence offers an explanation for the puzzle.
“that planet” refers to the unknown planet just suggested, which the mathematicians then located.
“the predicted position” is the result of the mathematicians’ calculations.
The closer. “It” refers to Neptune and states the significance of the whole story.

zh.By the early nineteenth century, astrono: 到了十九世紀初，天文學家注意到天王星的運行並不完全符合預測。
zh.Some suggested that the pull of an unkno: 有些人認為，是更外側一顆未知行星的引力擾亂了它的軌道。
zh.Working independently, two mathematician: 兩位數學家各自獨立地利用天王星的運動，計算出那顆行星應該在的位置。
zh.In 1846, an astronomer in Berlin pointed: 1846 年，柏林的一位天文學家把望遠鏡對準預測的位置，不到一個小時就發現了海王星。
zh.It was the first planet to be discovered: 它是第一顆透過數學計算、而不是偶然觀測而發現的行星。
zh.By the early nineteenth century, astrono: 到了十九世紀初，天文學家注意到天王星的運行並不完全符合預測。——開頭句。它設定了時間並提出關於天王星的謎題，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.Some suggested that the pull of an unkno: 有些人認為，是更外側一顆未知行星的引力擾亂了它的軌道。——"its orbit" 指的是天王星，而這句話為這個謎題提出了解釋。
zh.Working independently, two mathematician: 兩位數學家各自獨立地利用天王星的運動，計算出那顆行星應該在的位置。——"that planet" 指的是剛才提出的未知行星，數學家接著找出了它的位置。
zh.In 1846, an astronomer in Berlin pointed: 1846 年，柏林的一位天文學家把望遠鏡對準預測的位置，不到一個小時就發現了海王星。——"the predicted position" 是數學家計算的結果。
zh.It was the first planet to be discovered: 它是第一顆透過數學計算、而不是偶然觀測而發現的行星。——結尾句。"It" 指的是海王星，並說明了整個故事的意義。

order: Working memory is the mental space in which we hold information while we use it.
Unlike long-term memory, it has a very limited capacity, holding only a few items at once.
This limit explains why a long list of spoken instructions is so easily forgotten.
Teachers can reduce the problem by breaking tasks into steps and writing key points down.
In this way, the burden on working memory is lightened, leaving more capacity for actual learning.
why: The opener. It defines working memory in full and refers back to nothing.
“it” refers to working memory, and the sentence adds its key feature, a limited capacity.
“This limit” refers back to the limited capacity just described.
“the problem” is the forgetting explained in the previous sentence, and the teachers’ strategies address it.
The closer. “In this way” sums up the strategies and states their benefit.

zh.Working memory is the mental space in wh: 工作記憶是我們在使用資訊時暫時保存資訊的心智空間。
zh.Unlike long-term memory, it has a very l: 與長期記憶不同，它的容量非常有限，一次只能保存少數幾個項目。
zh.This limit explains why a long list of s: 這個限制解釋了為什麼一長串口頭指示這麼容易被忘記。
zh.Teachers can reduce the problem by break: 老師可以透過把任務拆成步驟，並把重點寫下來，來減少這個問題。
zh.In this way, the burden on working memor: 如此一來，工作記憶的負擔就會減輕，留下更多容量用於真正的學習。
zh.Working memory is the mental space in wh: 工作記憶是我們在使用資訊時暫時保存資訊的心智空間。——開頭句。它完整定義了工作記憶，而且沒有指涉前文的任何內容。
zh.Unlike long-term memory, it has a very l: 與長期記憶不同，它的容量非常有限，一次只能保存少數幾個項目。——"it" 指的是工作記憶，而這句話補充了它的關鍵特徵：容量有限。
zh.This limit explains why a long list of s: 這個限制解釋了為什麼一長串口頭指示這麼容易被忘記。——"This limit" 指回剛才描述的有限容量。
zh.Teachers can reduce the problem by break: 老師可以透過把任務拆成步驟，並把重點寫下來，來減少這個問題。——"the problem" 是前一句解釋的遺忘問題，而老師的策略正是針對它。
zh.In this way, the burden on working memor: 如此一來，工作記憶的負擔就會減輕，留下更多容量用於真正的學習。——結尾句。"In this way" 總結了這些策略並說明其好處。

questions.title: The story of zero
parts: Zero was not always
as a number. Babylonian scribes used a placeholder to mark an empty position, but it was Indian mathematicians around the seventh century who first set out
for calculating with it. The idea
to Europe through Arabic texts, where it met considerable
from merchants accustomed to Roman numerals.
why: “not always … as a number” needs a verb meaning accepted: zero was not always recognised as a number. “ignored” would miss the point that it later became one.
Indian mathematicians set out rules for calculating with zero, meaning how to use it in arithmetic. “symbols” repeats the placeholder idea, but the sentence is about calculating, not writing.
The idea spread to Europe through Arabic texts. “returned” wrongly implies that Europe had it before.
People accustomed to an old system resist a new one, so merchants used to Roman numerals showed resistance. “support” contradicts that.

zh.Zero was not always ____ as a number. Ba: 零並不是一直都被 ____ 為一個數字。巴比倫的書記官用一個占位符號來標示空位，但最早提出用它來計算的 ____ 的，是七世紀左右的印度數學家。這個概念透過阿拉伯文獻 ____ 到歐洲，並在那裡遭到習慣使用羅馬數字的商人相當大的 ____ 。
zh.“not always … as a number” needs a verb: 「並不是一直都被…為一個數字」需要一個表示「接受」的動詞：零並不是一直都被 recognised（承認）為數字。ignored 則忽略了它後來成為數字的重點。
zh.Indian mathematicians set out rules for: 印度數學家提出了用零計算的 rules（規則），也就是如何在算術中使用它。symbols 重複了占位符號的概念，但這句話談的是計算，而不是書寫。
zh.The idea spread to Europe through Arabic: 這個概念透過阿拉伯文獻 spread（傳播）到歐洲。returned 錯誤地暗示歐洲以前就有這個概念。
zh.People accustomed to an old system resis: 習慣舊制度的人會抗拒新制度，所以習慣羅馬數字的商人表現出 resistance（抗拒）。support 與此相矛盾。

questions.title: Octopus intelligence
parts: Octopuses are among the most intelligent
, able to open jars, escape from tanks and recognise individual humans. Remarkably, about two-thirds of their neurons are
in their arms rather than their brain, allowing each arm to
some decisions on its own. This
design suggests that intelligence can evolve along very different paths.
why: Octopuses are invertebrates, animals without a backbone. “mammals” is factually wrong, as octopuses are molluscs.
“located in their arms rather than their brain” says where the neurons are. “absent” contradicts the point that the arms can make decisions.
Collocation: make decisions. “cause some decisions” is not natural English.
Neurons spread through eight arms form a distributed design. “central” is the opposite of a system spread across the body.

zh.Octopuses are among the most intelligent: 章魚是最聰明的 ____ 之一，能打開罐子、從水族箱逃脫，還能辨認個別的人類。值得注意的是，牠們約有三分之二的神經元 ____ 在觸手中，而不是在大腦裡，使每一隻觸手都能自行 ____ 一些決定。這種 ____ 式的設計顯示，智能可以沿著非常不同的路徑演化。
zh.Octopuses are invertebrates, animals wit: 章魚是 invertebrates（無脊椎動物），也就是沒有脊椎的動物。mammals（哺乳動物）在事實上是錯的，因為章魚屬於軟體動物。
zh.“located in their arms rather than their: 「位於觸手中而不是大腦裡」說明了神經元的位置，所以是 located（位於）。absent 與觸手能夠做決定的重點互相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: make decisions. “cause some: 固定搭配：make decisions（做決定）。cause some decisions 不是自然的英文。
zh.Neurons spread through eight arms form a: 分布在八隻觸手中的神經元構成了 distributed（分散式）的設計。central 正好與分布全身的系統相反。

questions.title: Earthquake early warning
parts: Earthquake early warning systems cannot predict when a quake will
. Instead, they detect the first, faster seismic waves and send an alert before the slower, more
waves arrive. The warning may last only a few seconds, but that is enough to stop trains, open fire station doors and allow people to take
. The systems are most useful for cities located some
from the fault.
why: Collocation: an earthquake strikes. The sentence contrasts predicting the quake with detecting it once it has begun.
The slower waves are the damaging ones that people need warning about; “gentle” would make the warning pointless.
Fixed phrase: take cover, meaning protect yourself, for example under a table. “take place” means happen.
“some distance from the fault”: the further away a city is, the longer the gap between the two kinds of wave, and so the more warning it gets.

zh.Earthquake early warning systems cannot: 地震預警系統無法預測地震何時會 ____ 。它們的做法是偵測最先到達、速度較快的地震波，並在速度較慢、____ 較強的地震波到達之前發出警報。警報可能只有短短幾秒，但已足以讓列車停駛、打開消防隊的大門，並讓人們 ____ 。這類系統對距離斷層有一段 ____ 的城市最有用。
zh.Collocation: an earthquake strikes. The: 固定搭配：an earthquake strikes（地震發生、來襲）。這句話把「預測地震」和「在地震開始後偵測它」加以對比。
zh.The slower waves are the damaging ones t: 速度較慢的地震波才是人們需要被警告的破壞性（destructive）地震波；gentle（溫和的）會讓警報變得毫無意義。
zh.Fixed phrase: take cover, meaning protec: 固定用語：take cover（找掩護），也就是保護自己，例如躲到桌子底下。take place 的意思是「發生」。
zh.“some distance from the fault”: the furt: 「距離斷層有一段 distance（距離）」：城市離得越遠，兩種地震波之間的時間差就越長，得到的預警時間也就越多。

questions.title: Microfinance
parts: Microfinance began with a simple idea: small loans could help poor entrepreneurs start businesses that banks considered too
to fund. Early success stories attracted enormous
, and the model spread worldwide. Later randomised studies found more modest
: loans helped some existing businesses grow, but on average did little to
household incomes.
why: Banks refuse loans they think are too risky. “too profitable to fund” makes no sense.
Success stories attracted investment, which explains why “the model spread worldwide”. Criticism would not make it spread.
“more modest effects”: the studies measured outcomes, and found them smaller than hoped. “reasons” are not something a study finds to be modest.
“did little to raise household incomes”: the hope was that incomes would rise. “lower” reverses the goal.

zh.Microfinance began with a simple idea: s: 微型金融始於一個簡單的想法：小額貸款可以幫助貧窮的創業者開創銀行認為太 ____ 而不願資助的事業。早期的成功故事吸引了大量的 ____ ，這種模式也隨之擴展到全世界。後來的隨機試驗發現的 ____ 較為有限：貸款幫助了一些既有的事業成長，但平均而言，對 ____ 家庭收入幫助不大。
zh.Banks refuse loans they think are too ri: 銀行會拒絕它們認為太 risky（風險高）的貸款。「太 profitable（有利可圖）而不願資助」說不通。
zh.Success stories attracted investment, wh: 成功故事吸引了 investment（投資），這解釋了為什麼「這種模式擴展到全世界」。批評不會讓它擴展。
zh.“more modest effects”: the studies measu: 「較為有限的 effects（效果）」：這些研究測量的是成果，並發現成果比預期小。reasons（原因）不是研究會發現「有限」的東西。
zh.“did little to raise household incomes”:: 「對 raise（提高）家庭收入幫助不大」：原本的期望是收入會增加。lower 把目標顛倒了。

questions.title: Tea in Britain
parts: Tea arrived in Britain in the seventeenth century as an expensive
enjoyed by the wealthy. Over the next two hundred years, falling taxes and the growth of plantations in India made it
to ordinary households. By the nineteenth century it had become a daily
across all social classes, and its trade had become deeply
with the history of empire.
why: “expensive … enjoyed by the wealthy” describes a luxury. Tea itself was not a tax, although taxes appear in the next sentence.
Falling taxes and a bigger supply lower prices, making tea affordable. “unavailable” reverses the effect.
Drinking tea every day across all classes is a daily habit. A “ceremony” suggests a special occasion, which contradicts “daily”.
Collocation: deeply entangled with, meaning closely bound up with. “compared with” does not fit “had become deeply”.

zh.Tea arrived in Britain in the seventeent: 茶在十七世紀傳入英國時，是富人享用的昂貴 ____ 。在接下來的兩百年裡，稅賦降低加上印度茶園的擴張，使一般家庭也 ____ 得起茶。到了十九世紀，喝茶已成為各個社會階層的日常 ____ ，而茶葉貿易也與帝國的歷史深深地 ____ 在一起。
zh.“expensive … enjoyed by the wealthy” des: 「昂貴…富人享用的」描述的是 luxury（奢侈品）。茶本身不是 tax（稅），雖然下一句提到了稅。
zh.Falling taxes and a bigger supply lower: 稅賦降低、供應增加使價格下降，讓茶變得 affordable（負擔得起）。unavailable 把效果顛倒了。
zh.Drinking tea every day across all classe: 各階層每天都喝茶，是一種日常 habit（習慣）。ceremony（儀式）暗示特殊場合，與「日常」相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: deeply entangled with, mean: 固定搭配：deeply entangled with（與…深深糾纏、密不可分）。compared with 無法搭配「已經變得深深地…」。

questions.title: Improving photosynthesis
parts: Plants convert only about one per cent of the sunlight that reaches them into stored
. Much of the loss comes from an enzyme called RuBisCO, which sometimes
oxygen instead of carbon dioxide and wastes energy repairing the mistake. Scientists have
tobacco plants with a shortcut that recycles the waste more efficiently, and the modified plants grew about forty per cent
in field trials.
why: Photosynthesis stores sunlight as chemical energy; plants do not turn light into water.
The enzyme’s mistake is grabbing oxygen instead of carbon dioxide: it captures the wrong gas. “releases” describes a different process.
Adding a new chemical shortcut to a plant is genetic engineering. You cannot plant a plant “with a shortcut”.
A more efficient plant grows larger. “slower” contradicts the improvement.

zh.Plants convert only about one per cent o: 植物只能把照射到的陽光中約百分之一轉化為儲存的 ____ 。大部分的損失來自一種叫做 RuBisCO 的酵素，它有時會 ____ 氧氣而不是二氧化碳，並浪費能量去修正這個錯誤。科學家已經用一條能更有效率地回收這些浪費的捷徑 ____ 了菸草植株，而在田間試驗中，這些經過改造的植株長得 ____ 了約百分之四十。
zh.Photosynthesis stores sunlight as chemic: 光合作用把陽光儲存為化學 energy（能量）；植物不會把光轉化為水。
zh.The enzyme’s mistake is grabbing oxygen: 這種酵素的錯誤在於抓取氧氣而不是二氧化碳：它 captures（捕獲）了錯誤的氣體。releases（釋放）描述的是另一種過程。
zh.Adding a new chemical shortcut to a plan: 為植物加入一條新的化學捷徑屬於基因工程，所以是 engineered（改造）。你無法「用一條捷徑」去 plant（種植）一株植物。
zh.A more efficient plant grows larger. “sl: 效率更高的植物會長得更 larger（大）。slower 與改善的結果相矛盾。

questions.title: The seed vault
parts: Deep inside a mountain on a remote Norwegian island lies the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, which
duplicate samples of more than a million crop varieties. The site was chosen because the permanently frozen ground keeps the seeds cold even if the
fails. The vault acts as a backup: if a national seed bank is
by war or disaster, its collection can be
from Svalbard.
why: A vault holding duplicate samples stores them. It does not sell them, because it exists as a backup.
“keeps the seeds cold even if the … fails” points to refrigeration, which depends on power. Weather does not “fail” in this sense.
A backup is needed when a collection is lost, so the seed bank is destroyed by war or disaster. “founded by war” makes no sense.
The backup lets a lost collection be restored. “borrowed from Svalbard” wrongly implies the seeds must be given back.

zh.Deep inside a mountain on a remote Norwe: 在挪威一座偏遠島嶼的山體深處，坐落著斯瓦爾巴全球種子庫，它 ____ 了一百多萬種作物品種的備份樣本。之所以選擇這個地點，是因為即使 ____ 中斷，永久凍土也能讓種子保持低溫。這座種子庫扮演備份的角色：如果某個國家的種子銀行因戰爭或災難而被 ____ ，它的收藏就可以從斯瓦爾巴 ____ 。
zh.A vault holding duplicate samples stores: 保存備份樣本的種子庫會 stores（儲存）樣本。它不會出售樣本，因為它的存在是為了備份。
zh.“keeps the seeds cold even if the … fail: 「即使…中斷，也能讓種子保持低溫」指的是冷藏，而冷藏需要 power（電力）。天氣並不會在這個意義上「中斷」。
zh.A backup is needed when a collection is: 當收藏遺失時才需要備份，所以種子銀行是被戰爭或災難 destroyed（摧毀）。「被戰爭 founded（創立）」說不通。
zh.The backup lets a lost collection be res: 備份能讓遺失的收藏被 restored（恢復）。borrowed from Svalbard 錯誤地暗示種子必須歸還。

questions.title: The toughest animal
parts: Tardigrades are tiny animals, less than a millimetre long, that can survive conditions that would
almost any other creature. When their environment dries out, they curl into a ball and shut down their metabolism almost
. In this state they have endured extreme cold, intense radiation and even the
of outer space. Once water returns, they can
within hours and carry on as normal.
why: Surviving “conditions that would … almost any other creature” needs a harmful verb: kill. Conditions do not “feed” creatures.
To survive drying out, they shut their metabolism down almost completely. “partly” undercuts the extreme survival being described.
Outer space is known for its vacuum, the absence of air. Space carries no noise at all.
When water returns they recover. “disappear” contradicts “carry on as normal”.

zh.Tardigrades are tiny animals, less than: 水熊蟲是體長不到一公釐的微小動物，能在幾乎會 ____ 其他任何生物的環境中存活。當環境變乾時，牠們會捲成一團，把新陳代謝幾乎 ____ 關閉。在這種狀態下，牠們承受過極度的寒冷、強烈的輻射，甚至是外太空的 ____ 。一旦水分回來，牠們能在幾小時內 ____ ，並照常活動。
zh.Surviving “conditions that would … almos: 在「幾乎會…其他任何生物的環境」中存活，需要一個表示傷害的動詞：kill（殺死）。環境不會 feed（餵養）生物。
zh.To survive drying out, they shut their m: 為了在乾燥中存活，牠們把新陳代謝幾乎 completely（完全）關閉。partly 削弱了文中描述的極端存活能力。
zh.Outer space is known for its vacuum, the: 外太空以 vacuum（真空）著稱，也就是沒有空氣。太空中根本沒有噪音。
zh.When water returns they recover. “disapp: 水分回來後，牠們會 recover（恢復）。disappear 與「照常活動」相矛盾。

questions.title: When north becomes south
parts: The Earth’s magnetic field has
its direction hundreds of times, so that a compass which now points north would once have pointed south. Evidence comes from volcanic rocks, which record the
of the field at the moment they cooled. Reversals occur at irregular
, and the last one took place about 780,000 years ago. During a reversal the field weakens, which could
satellites to more radiation.
why: “so that a compass … would once have pointed south” describes the field flipping: it has reversed its direction. “kept” contradicts that.
The rocks record which way the field pointed when they cooled, its direction, and that is how past reversals are detected. A magnetic field has no temperature.
Collocation: “at irregular intervals”, meaning with uneven gaps of time between them.
A weaker field gives less shielding, so it could expose satellites to radiation. “protect” is the opposite.

zh.The Earth’s magnetic field has ____ its: 地球的磁場已經 ____ 方向數百次，所以一個現在指向北方的指南針，過去曾經會指向南方。證據來自火山岩，它們會記錄冷卻當下磁場的 ____ 。磁場反轉以不規則的 ____ 發生，最近一次大約發生在 78 萬年前。在反轉期間，磁場會減弱，這可能使人造衛星 ____ 於更多的輻射之中。
zh.“so that a compass … would once have poi: 「一個現在指向北方的指南針，過去曾經會指向南方」描述的是磁場翻轉：它已經 reversed（反轉）方向。kept 與此相矛盾。
zh.The rocks record which way the field poi: 岩石記錄了冷卻時磁場指向哪個方向，也就是它的 direction（方向），過去的反轉正是這樣被偵測出來的。磁場沒有溫度。
zh.Collocation: “at irregular intervals”, m: 固定搭配：at irregular intervals（以不規則的間隔），表示發生的時間間隔長短不一。
zh.A weaker field gives less shielding, so: 較弱的磁場提供的屏蔽較少，所以它可能讓衛星 expose（暴露）於輻射之中。protect 正好相反。

questions.title: Who built the pyramids?
parts: For a long time, the pyramids of Egypt were imagined as the work of slaves. Archaeologists now think they were built largely by paid
. Excavations near Giza have uncovered bakeries, breweries and
where these workers lived, along with tombs in which they were buried with honour. Their bones show signs of heavy
, but also of medical care, including broken limbs that had been carefully
why: The contrast with slaves requires workers who were paid: labourers. Tourists did not build pyramids.
“where these workers lived” needs somewhere to live: houses. Shops are not where people live.
Years of hard physical work leave marks on bones: heavy labour. Rain does not show on bones.
A doctor “sets” a broken bone so it heals straight, which is evidence of medical care. “painted” limbs has nothing to do with healing.

zh.For a long time, the pyramids of Egypt w: 長久以來，埃及金字塔一直被想像成奴隸的作品。考古學家現在認為，金字塔主要是由領取報酬的 ____ 建造的。吉薩附近的挖掘發現了麵包坊、釀酒坊以及這些工人居住的 ____ ，還有他們被隆重安葬的墓穴。他們的骨骼顯示出繁重 ____ 的痕跡，但也顯示出曾接受醫療照護，包括曾被仔細 ____ 的骨折肢體。
zh.The contrast with slaves requires worker: 與奴隸對比，需要的是領取報酬的工人：labourers（勞工）。遊客並沒有建造金字塔。
zh.“where these workers lived” needs somewh: 「這些工人居住的地方」需要一個住處：houses（房屋）。商店不是人們居住的地方。
zh.Years of hard physical work leave marks: 多年的繁重體力工作會在骨骼上留下痕跡：heavy labour（繁重勞動）。雨水不會在骨骼上留下痕跡。
zh.A doctor “sets” a broken bone so it heal: 醫生會把骨折的骨頭 set（接合、固定），讓它癒合得筆直，這就是醫療照護的證據。painted（上色的）肢體與癒合無關。

questions.title: The first paper money
parts: Paper money was first used widely in China around a thousand years ago. Merchants had grown tired of carrying heavy strings of iron
, so they began leaving them with trusted dealers in exchange for paper
. The government later took control of the system and issued its own notes. However, printing money was so easy that officials often produced too
, and prices rose
why: “heavy strings of iron” refers to metal money with holes, strung together: coins.
Merchants left their coins with dealers and got paper proving the deposit in return: receipts.
Because printing was easy, officials produced too many notes. “too few” would not make prices rise.
Too much money pushes prices up sharply. “slowly” weakens the cause and effect the passage describes.

zh.Paper money was first used widely in Chi: 紙幣大約在一千年前首先在中國被廣泛使用。商人們厭倦了攜帶一串串沉重的鐵 ____ ，於是開始把它們寄放在可信賴的商號，換取紙本的 ____ 。後來政府接管了這套制度，並發行自己的紙幣。然而，印鈔實在太容易了，官員常常印得太 ____ ，物價也隨之 ____ 上漲。
zh.“heavy strings of iron” refers to metal: 「一串串沉重的鐵…」指的是用繩子串起來的金屬貨幣：coins（錢幣）。
zh.Merchants left their coins with dealers: 商人把錢幣寄放在商號，換回證明寄存的紙張：receipts（收據）。
zh.Because printing was easy, officials pro: 由於印鈔很容易，官員印了 too many（太多）紙幣。too few 不會讓物價上漲。
錢太多會讓物價 sharply（急遽）上漲。slowly 削弱了文中描述的因果關係。

questions.title: Seeing with sound
parts: Many bats find their way in the dark by echolocation. They
high-pitched calls and listen to the echoes that bounce back from objects around them. By comparing the time and
of these echoes, a bat can judge the size, shape and distance of an insect with remarkable
. Some moths have evolved the ability to hear these calls and
them by diving suddenly towards the ground.
why: The bat makes the calls and then listens to the echoes: it produces them. A bat does not “swallow” its calls.
Echoes can be compared by when and from where they arrive: time and direction. Sound has no colour.
“with remarkable …” praises the bat’s accuracy: precision. “with remarkable difficulty” contradicts the skill described.
Moths dive to get away from bats, so they escape them. Prey does not “follow” a predator.

zh.Many bats find their way in the dark by: 許多蝙蝠靠回聲定位在黑暗中找路。牠們 ____ 高頻的叫聲，然後聆聽從周圍物體反彈回來的回聲。透過比較這些回聲的時間和 ____ ，蝙蝠能以驚人的 ____ 判斷昆蟲的大小、形狀和距離。有些飛蛾已經演化出聽到這些叫聲的能力，並會突然俯衝向地面來 ____ 蝙蝠。
zh.The bat makes the calls and then listens: 蝙蝠發出叫聲，然後聆聽回聲：牠們 produce（發出）叫聲。蝙蝠不會 swallow（吞下）自己的叫聲。
zh.Echoes can be compared by when and from: 回聲可以依到達的時間和來處加以比較：時間和 direction（方向）。聲音沒有顏色。
zh.“with remarkable …” praises the bat’s ac: 「以驚人的…」是在稱讚蝙蝠的準確度：precision（精確度）。with remarkable difficulty 與文中描述的技能相矛盾。
zh.Moths dive to get away from bats, so the: 飛蛾俯衝是為了避開蝙蝠，所以是 escape（逃離）牠們。獵物不會 follow（跟隨）掠食者。

questions.title: Machines that play chess
parts: In 1997, a computer called Deep Blue
the world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game match. The machine did not think like a human; it relied on raw
, examining around two hundred million positions every second. Modern programs work very differently. They learn by playing millions of games against
, and they have developed styles that grandmasters now
in order to improve their own play.
why: The match is famous because the computer won: Deep Blue defeated Kasparov. “taught the world champion” makes no sense for a match.
Examining two hundred million positions per second describes raw speed, not luck.
Modern programs learn through self-play, playing millions of games against themselves.
Grandmasters improve by studying the programs’ styles. Banning them would not help their own play.

zh.In 1997, a computer called Deep Blue ___: 1997 年，一台名為「深藍」的電腦在一場六局的比賽中 ____ 了世界西洋棋冠軍加里・卡斯帕洛夫。這台機器並不像人類那樣思考；它依靠的是純粹的 ____ ，每秒檢視大約兩億個棋局。現代的程式運作方式非常不同。它們透過與 ____ 對弈數百萬局來學習，並發展出特級大師們如今會 ____ 以提升自己棋藝的棋風。
zh.The match is famous because the computer: 這場比賽之所以出名，是因為電腦贏了：深藍 defeated（擊敗）了卡斯帕洛夫。「教導世界冠軍」用在比賽上說不通。
zh.Examining two hundred million positions: 每秒檢視兩億個棋局，描述的是純粹的 speed（速度），而不是運氣。
zh.Modern programs learn through self-play,: 現代程式透過自我對弈來學習，與 themselves（自己）下數百萬局棋。
zh.Grandmasters improve by studying the pro: 特級大師透過 study（研究）這些程式的棋風來進步。禁止它們並不會提升自己的棋藝。

questions.title: The Great Stink
parts: In the hot summer of 1858, the River Thames in London smelled so

that Parliament considered moving elsewhere. The river had become an open sewer, and repeated outbreaks of cholera had already killed thousands. At the time, many doctors believed disease was spread by bad
, so the smell itself caused alarm. The engineer Joseph Bazalgette was asked to build a new sewer system, which carried waste
from the city and greatly
cholera deaths.
why: Parliament considering moving implies an extreme stink: the river smelled so terrible. “so sweet” contradicts the description of an open sewer.
Doctors then believed disease spread through bad air, which is exactly why the smell itself caused alarm.
A sewer carries waste away from the city. “towards” reverses its purpose.
The new sewers improved public health, so they greatly reduced cholera deaths.

zh.In the hot summer of 1858, the River Tha: 在 1858 年炎熱的夏天，倫敦泰晤士河的氣味 ____ 到議會考慮搬到別處。這條河已經成了一條露天下水道，反覆爆發的霍亂早已奪走了數千條人命。當時，許多醫生認為疾病是透過污濁的 ____ 傳播的，所以這股臭味本身就引起了恐慌。工程師約瑟夫・巴澤爾杰特受命建造一套新的下水道系統，把污水運 ____ 城市，大幅 ____ 了霍亂的死亡人數。
zh.Parliament considering moving implies an: 議會考慮搬遷，暗示臭味極其嚴重：這條河的氣味 terrible（可怕）。so sweet 與露天下水道的描述相矛盾。
zh.Doctors then believed disease spread thr: 當時的醫生相信疾病透過污濁的 air（空氣）傳播，這正是臭味本身會引起恐慌的原因。
zh.A sewer carries waste away from the city: 下水道把污水運 away（離開）城市。towards 把它的用途顛倒了。
zh.The new sewers improved public health, s: 新的下水道改善了公共衛生，所以大幅 reduced（減少）了霍亂死亡人數。

questions.title: Carbon dating
parts: Radiocarbon dating allows scientists to estimate the age of materials that were once
, such as wood, bone and cloth. While an organism is alive, it takes in carbon, including a small
of radioactive carbon-14. After it dies, the carbon-14 slowly
at a known rate, halving roughly every 5,730 years. By measuring how much is
, researchers can calculate how long ago the organism died.
why: Wood, bone and cloth all come from things that were once living, and only such material can be dated this way.
Carbon-14 is a tiny share of the carbon an organism takes in: a small amount. Carbon has no colour in this sense.
Radioactive carbon decays at a known rate. It does not grow after the organism dies.
Researchers measure how much carbon-14 is left, which shows how long it has been decaying.

zh.Radiocarbon dating allows scientists to: 放射性碳定年法讓科學家能估算那些曾經 ____ 的物質的年代，例如木材、骨頭和布料。生物在活著的時候會攝取碳，其中包括少 ____ 的放射性碳十四。生物死亡後，碳十四會以已知的速率慢慢 ____ ，大約每 5,730 年減半。透過測量還 ____ 多少，研究人員就能計算出這個生物死於多久以前。
zh.Wood, bone and cloth all come from thing: 木材、骨頭和布料都來自曾經 living（活著）的東西，而只有這類物質能用這種方法定年。
zh.Carbon-14 is a tiny share of the carbon: 碳十四只占生物攝取的碳中極小的一部分：a small amount（少量）。碳在這個意義上沒有顏色。
zh.Radioactive carbon decays at a known rat: 放射性碳會以已知的速率 decays（衰變）。生物死亡後它不會 grow（增加）。
zh.Researchers measure how much carbon-14 i: 研究人員測量碳十四還 left（剩下）多少，就能看出它已經衰變了多久。

questions.title: From willow bark to aspirin
parts: For thousands of years, people chewed the bark of willow trees to
pain and fever. In the nineteenth century, chemists identified the active
, salicylic acid, but it irritated the stomach badly. In 1897, a chemist working for the Bayer company produced a modified version that was easier to
. Sold as aspirin, it became one of the most widely used
in the world.
why: Chewing bark to deal with pain and fever means using it to relieve them. “cause” is the opposite.
Fixed phrase: the active ingredient, the substance that produces the effect. A container does not produce effects.
The problem was stomach irritation, so the improvement was a version that was easier to tolerate.
Aspirin is a medicine, one of the most widely used in the world. It is not a vehicle.

zh.For thousands of years, people chewed th: 數千年來，人們咀嚼柳樹皮來 ____ 疼痛和發燒。十九世紀時，化學家找出了其中的活性 ____ ——水楊酸，但它對胃的刺激很大。1897 年，一位在拜耳公司工作的化學家製造出一種改良版本，讓人更容易 ____ 。這種藥以「阿斯匹靈」之名販售，成為全世界最廣泛使用的 ____ 之一。
zh.Chewing bark to deal with pain and fever: 咀嚼樹皮來處理疼痛和發燒，意思是用它來 relieve（緩解）症狀。cause 正好相反。
zh.Fixed phrase: the active ingredient, the: 固定用語：the active ingredient（活性成分），也就是產生效果的物質。容器不會產生效果。
zh.The problem was stomach irritation, so t: 問題在於對胃的刺激，所以改良之處是新版本更容易 tolerate（耐受）。
zh.Aspirin is a medicine, one of the most w: 阿斯匹靈是一種 medicine（藥物），而且是全世界最廣泛使用的藥物之一。它不是交通工具。

questions.title: How hurricanes form
parts: Hurricanes form over warm tropical oceans, where the water temperature is at least twenty-six degrees Celsius. Warm, moist air
from the surface, cools and forms clouds, releasing heat that powers the storm. Because of the Earth’s rotation, the system begins to
. Once a hurricane moves over land or cooler water, it loses its
of energy and gradually
why: Warm, moist air is lighter and rises; it must rise in order to cool and form clouds. “falls from the surface” is impossible.
The Earth’s rotation makes the storm system spin. Warm tropical air cannot freeze in this way.
Warm water supplies the storm’s energy, so over land it loses its source of energy.
Without its energy source, the storm gradually weakens. “strengthens” is the opposite.

zh.Hurricanes form over warm tropical ocean: 颶風形成於水溫至少攝氏二十六度的溫暖熱帶海洋上空。溫暖潮濕的空氣從海面 ____ ，冷卻後形成雲，釋放出為風暴提供動力的熱能。由於地球自轉，這個系統會開始 ____ 。一旦颶風移動到陸地或較冷的水域上空，它就會失去能量的 ____ ，並逐漸 ____ 。
zh.Warm, moist air is lighter and rises; it: 溫暖潮濕的空氣較輕，所以會 rises（上升）；它必須上升才能冷卻並形成雲。「從海面 falls（落下）」是不可能的。
zh.The Earth’s rotation makes the storm sys: 地球的自轉會讓風暴系統 spin（旋轉）。溫暖的熱帶空氣不會以這種方式 freeze（凍結）。
zh.Warm water supplies the storm’s energy,: 溫暖的海水提供了風暴的能量，所以到了陸地上，它就失去了能量的 source（來源）。
zh.Without its energy source, the storm gra: 失去能量來源後，風暴會逐漸 weakens（減弱）。strengthens 正好相反。

questions.title: The humble barcode
parts: The barcode was patented in 1952, but it was not widely used until the 1970s, when laser
became cheap enough for shops. The first product to be scanned in a supermarket was a packet of chewing gum. Barcodes
up checkouts, reduced errors and gave retailers detailed
about what customers bought. Today, two-dimensional versions such as QR codes can
far more information in the same space.
why: Reading barcodes requires laser scanners, and those had to become cheap enough for shops. A pointer cannot read a code.
Phrasal verb: “sped up” means made faster, which fits the other benefits listed. “slowed up” contradicts them.
Retailers gained detailed data about what customers bought. “gifts about what customers bought” makes no sense.
The advantage of QR codes is that they store more information in the same space. Deleting information is not a benefit.

zh.The barcode was patented in 1952, but it: 條碼在 1952 年取得專利，但直到 1970 年代，當雷射 ____ 便宜到商店也買得起時，才被廣泛使用。第一個在超市被掃描的商品是一包口香糖。條碼 ____ 了結帳速度、減少了錯誤，並讓零售商獲得關於顧客購買內容的詳細 ____ 。如今，QR 碼等二維版本能在同樣的空間中 ____ 多得多的資訊。
zh.Reading barcodes requires laser scanners: 讀取條碼需要雷射 scanners（掃描器），而掃描器必須便宜到商店買得起才行。雷射筆無法讀取條碼。
zh.Phrasal verb: “sped up” means made faste: 片語動詞：sped up（加快），與文中列出的其他好處一致。slowed up 與之相矛盾。
zh.Retailers gained detailed data about wha: 零售商獲得了關於顧客購買內容的詳細 data（數據）。「關於顧客購買內容的禮物」說不通。
zh.The advantage of QR codes is that they s: QR 碼的優點是能在同樣的空間中 store（儲存）更多資訊。刪除資訊並不是一種好處。

questions.passage: Economists have long puzzled over why firms pay the high rents of city centres when cheaper land is available only a short distance away. The standard answer is agglomeration: firms located close together benefit from a shared pool of skilled workers, from specialised suppliers and, above all, from the rapid spread of ideas. A software engineer who changes jobs in a dense technology cluster carries knowledge from one company to the next, and informal conversations spread techniques faster than any publication. Many predicted that the internet would weaken these advantages by making distance irrelevant. So far the opposite has happened: the most knowledge-intensive industries have become more concentrated in a handful of cities, not less. It seems that the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen.
questions.q: According to the passage, why have knowledge-intensive industries become more concentrated?
o: The internet has made it cheaper to rent office space in city centres.
The most valuable knowledge is difficult to share at a distance.
Governments have offered tax incentives for firms to cluster together.
Skilled workers refuse to move away from the places where they studied.
why: Never stated. The passage says city-centre rents are high, and it does not connect the internet with cheaper rent.
Correct. “the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen.”
Plausible in real life, but the passage never mentions governments or taxes. Answer only from the text.
Not mentioned. The passage talks about workers changing jobs within a cluster, not about where they studied.

zh.Economists have long puzzled over why fi: 經濟學家長久以來一直不解，為什麼企業願意支付市中心的高額租金，而只要稍微遠一點就有更便宜的土地。標準的答案是「聚集效應」：彼此鄰近的企業能從共享的技術人才庫、專業供應商中獲益，而最重要的是從思想的快速傳播中獲益。一位在密集的科技聚落中換工作的軟體工程師，會把知識從一家公司帶到下一家公司，而非正式的交談傳播技術的速度比任何出版物都快。許多人曾預測網際網路會讓距離變得無關緊要，從而削弱這些優勢。但到目前為止，情況正好相反：知識最密集的產業反而更加集中在少數幾個城市，而不是更分散。看來最重要的那些知識，恰恰是最難透過螢幕傳遞的。
zh.According to the passage, why have knowl: 根據文章，為什麼知識密集型產業變得更加集中？
zh.The internet has made it cheaper to rent: 網際網路使市中心辦公空間的租金變得更便宜。
zh.The most valuable knowledge is difficult: 最有價值的知識很難遠距離分享。
zh.Governments have offered tax incentives: 政府提供了租稅優惠，鼓勵企業聚集在一起。
zh.Skilled workers refuse to move away from: 技術人才拒絕離開他們讀書的地方。
zh.Never stated. The passage says city-cent: 文章沒有這樣說。文章指出市中心的租金很高，並沒有把網際網路和較便宜的租金連結起來。
zh.Correct. “the kinds of knowledge that ma: 正確。"the kinds of knowledge that matter most are precisely those that are hardest to transmit through a screen."
zh.Plausible in real life, but the passage: 在現實中或許說得通，但文章從未提到政府或稅。只能根據文章內容作答。
zh.Not mentioned. The passage talks about w: 文章沒有提到。文章談的是人才在聚落內換工作，而不是他們在哪裡讀書。

questions.passage: For decades, medical errors were treated as the failings of individual doctors and nurses, who were expected to be careful enough never to make them. Aviation had taken a different approach. After a series of crashes caused by crews failing to challenge a captain’s decisions, airlines introduced checklists, standard procedures and training that encouraged junior staff to speak up. The underlying assumption was that skilled people will still make mistakes, so systems should be designed to catch them. When hospitals adopted similar methods, such as a brief checklist before surgery, several studies reported substantial falls in complications and deaths. The results were not always repeated, however: where checklists were imposed without training or were completed as a formality, they made little difference. The lesson drawn by many researchers is that the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used.
questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Doctors and nurses make more mistakes than airline pilots.
Surgical checklists have failed to reduce complications in hospitals.
Safety methods from aviation help hospitals only when they are supported by the right culture.
Junior staff should be given more authority than senior doctors.
why: The passage never compares error rates between the professions. It compares how the two fields respond to errors.
Too absolute. Several studies “reported substantial falls in complications and deaths”; checklists failed only where they were imposed without training.
Correct. The passage traces aviation methods into hospitals and ends: “the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used.”
Distorted. Aviation training “encouraged junior staff to speak up”, which is not the same as giving them more authority.

zh.For decades, medical errors were treated: 數十年來，醫療錯誤一直被視為個別醫師和護理師的失職，他們被期望要謹慎到永遠不犯錯。航空業則採取了不同的做法。在一連串因機組人員未能質疑機長決定而造成的空難之後，航空公司引進了檢查清單、標準作業程序，以及鼓勵資淺人員勇於發言的訓練。其背後的假設是：技術純熟的人仍然會犯錯，所以應該設計出能攔截錯誤的系統。當醫院採用類似的方法，例如手術前的簡短檢查清單時，好幾項研究都顯示併發症和死亡人數大幅下降。然而，這些結果並非總能重現：在沒有搭配訓練就強制實施檢查清單，或只是把填寫清單當作形式的地方，成效就很有限。許多研究人員從中得出的教訓是：工具本身的重要性，不如使用工具的文化。
zh.What is the main point of the passage?: 這篇文章的主旨是什麼？
zh.Doctors and nurses make more mistakes th: 醫師和護理師犯的錯比航空公司機師多。
zh.Surgical checklists have failed to reduc: 手術檢查清單未能減少醫院的併發症。
zh.Safety methods from aviation help hospit: 來自航空業的安全方法，只有在有適當文化支持時才能幫助醫院。
zh.Junior staff should be given more author: 資淺人員應該被賦予比資深醫師更大的權力。
zh.The passage never compares error rates b: 文章從未比較這些職業的錯誤率。它比較的是兩個領域如何應對錯誤。
zh.Too absolute. Several studies “reported: 說得太絕對了。好幾項研究 "reported substantial falls in complications and deaths"；檢查清單只有在沒有搭配訓練就強制實施時才失效。
zh.Correct. The passage traces aviation met: 正確。文章追溯了航空業的方法如何被引進醫院，並以 "the tool matters less than the culture in which it is used." 作結。
zh.Distorted. Aviation training “encouraged: 扭曲了原意。航空業的訓練 "encouraged junior staff to speak up"，這和賦予他們更大的權力不一樣。

questions.passage: Supporters of app-based gig work, such as ride-hailing and food delivery, emphasise its flexibility: workers can log on and off whenever they wish, fitting paid work around study, caring responsibilities or other jobs. Surveys confirm that many drivers value this highly. Critics respond that the flexibility is partly an illusion. Because pay depends on demand, workers who want a reasonable income must be available at the busiest times, such as Friday evenings, and the algorithms that allocate jobs may reward those who accept every request. A recent study that analysed earnings data found that the hourly pay of drivers fell when more drivers joined a platform, since each driver spent more time waiting for customers. Flexibility over when to work, in other words, does not guarantee control over how much one earns.
questions.q: What does the author suggest about flexibility in gig work?
o: It is not valued by most gig workers.
It gives workers full control over their income.
It is limited in practice by demand and by how platforms allocate work.
It has led platforms to raise pay during busy periods.
why: Contradicted. “Surveys confirm that many drivers value this highly.”
The opposite of the conclusion: flexibility “does not guarantee control over how much one earns.”
Correct. Workers “must be available at the busiest times”, and algorithms “may reward those who accept every request”, so the flexibility is partly an illusion.
Not stated. The passage mentions busy periods only as times when workers must be available, not as times when pay rises.

zh.Supporters of app-based gig work, such a: 零工經濟（例如叫車和外送等以應用程式為基礎的工作）的支持者強調它的彈性：工作者可以隨時上線、下線，把有酬工作安排在讀書、照顧家人或其他工作之間。調查證實，許多司機非常重視這一點。批評者則回應說，這種彈性有一部分是假象。由於收入取決於需求，想要有合理收入的工作者必須在最忙碌的時段待命，例如星期五晚上，而負責分派工作的演算法可能會獎勵那些接下每一筆訂單的人。最近一項分析收入數據的研究發現，當更多司機加入某個平台時，司機的時薪就會下降，因為每位司機花在等待乘客上的時間變多了。換句話說，能夠彈性決定何時工作，並不保證能掌控自己賺多少錢。
zh.What does the author suggest about flexi: 作者對零工工作的彈性有什麼看法？
大多數零工工作者並不重視它。
zh.It gives workers full control over their: 它讓工作者能完全掌控自己的收入。
zh.It is limited in practice by demand and: 實際上，它受到需求以及平台分派工作方式的限制。
zh.It has led platforms to raise pay during: 它促使平台在忙碌時段提高報酬。
zh.Contradicted. “Surveys confirm that many: 與文章矛盾。"Surveys confirm that many drivers value this highly."
zh.The opposite of the conclusion: flexibil: 與結論正好相反：彈性 "does not guarantee control over how much one earns."
zh.Correct. Workers “must be available at t: 正確。工作者 "must be available at the busiest times"，而演算法 "may reward those who accept every request"，所以這種彈性有一部分是假象。
zh.Not stated. The passage mentions busy pe: 文章沒有提到。文章提到忙碌時段，只是指工作者必須待命的時間，而不是報酬提高的時間。

questions.passage: Anyone who has spent a long time in a bath has noticed that their fingers and toes become wrinkled. For many years this was explained as a simple matter of skin absorbing water and swelling. Then doctors noticed that the wrinkling does not occur in people whose nerves to the fingers have been damaged, which showed that it is an active process controlled by the nervous system. This led to the suggestion that wrinkles serve a purpose. In one experiment, volunteers were faster at moving wet marbles from one container to another when their fingers were wrinkled, although later studies have not always found the same benefit. If the effect is real, wrinkled fingers may work like the tread on a tyre, improving grip in wet conditions.
questions.q: What does the author suggest about wrinkled fingers?
o: They are caused simply by the skin absorbing water.
They may be an active response that improves grip, although the evidence is not settled.
They occur only in people whose nerves have been damaged.
They have been proven to double grip strength in all conditions.
why: This was the old explanation, which the passage says was overturned when doctors noticed the role of the nerves.
Correct. Wrinkling is “an active process controlled by the nervous system”, may improve grip “like the tread on a tyre”, but later studies “have not always found the same benefit”.
The reverse: wrinkling “does not occur in people whose nerves to the fingers have been damaged”.
Far too strong. The passage says “If the effect is real”, and no figure like “double” appears.

zh.Anyone who has spent a long time in a ba: 任何在浴缸裡泡過很久的人都注意過，自己的手指和腳趾會起皺。多年來，這被解釋為只是皮膚吸水膨脹的簡單現象。後來醫生注意到，手指神經受損的人不會出現這種皺褶，這顯示它是一個由神經系統控制的主動過程。這使人們推測，皺褶具有某種功能。在一項實驗中，志願者在手指起皺時，把濕彈珠從一個容器移到另一個容器的速度比較快，不過後來的研究並不總能發現同樣的好處。如果這種效應是真的，起皺的手指可能就像輪胎上的胎紋一樣，在潮濕的情況下提升抓握力。
zh.What does the author suggest about wrink: 作者對起皺的手指有什麼看法？
zh.They are caused simply by the skin absor: 它們純粹是皮膚吸水造成的。
zh.They may be an active response that impr: 它們可能是一種能提升抓握力的主動反應，不過證據尚無定論。
zh.They occur only in people whose nerves h: 它們只會出現在神經受損的人身上。
zh.They have been proven to double grip str: 已證實它們在各種情況下都能讓抓握力加倍。
zh.This was the old explanation, which the: 這是舊的解釋，文章說當醫生注意到神經的作用後，這個解釋就被推翻了。
zh.Correct. Wrinkling is “an active process: 正確。起皺是 "an active process controlled by the nervous system"，可能像 "like the tread on a tyre" 一樣提升抓握力，但後來的研究 "have not always found the same benefit"。
zh.The reverse: wrinkling “does not occur i: 正好相反：起皺 "does not occur in people whose nerves to the fingers have been damaged"。
zh.Far too strong. The passage says “If the: 說得太過頭了。文章說 "If the effect is real"，而且沒有出現「加倍」之類的數字。

questions.passage: English spelling is notoriously inconsistent: the letters “ough” are pronounced differently in though, through, cough and bough. Much of this inconsistency is historical. Spelling began to be standardised in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, partly through the influence of printing, at the same time as English pronunciation was changing rapidly in a process known as the Great Vowel Shift. As a result, many spellings were fixed to reflect pronunciations that soon disappeared. Later scholars made matters worse by adding silent letters to show a word’s supposed Latin origin, such as the b in debt. Several attempts at spelling reform have been proposed since, but none has succeeded, largely because changing the spelling of familiar words meets strong public resistance.
questions.q: According to the passage, why is English spelling inconsistent?
o: Printers deliberately introduced spelling mistakes to save space.
Spelling became fixed while pronunciation was still changing, and silent letters were later added.
Spelling reformers have repeatedly made English spelling more complicated.
English borrowed all of its words directly from Latin.
why: Not stated. Printing helped standardise spelling; nothing says printers introduced mistakes.
Correct. Spelling was standardised “at the same time as English pronunciation was changing rapidly”, and scholars later added silent letters, such as the b in debt.
The reverse. Reform attempts all failed: “none has succeeded”.
Distorted. Scholars added letters to show a “supposed Latin origin”, which does not mean all English words came from Latin.

zh.English spelling is notoriously inconsis: 英文的拼字出了名地不一致：「ough」這幾個字母在 though、through、cough 和 bough 中的發音各不相同。這種不一致大多有其歷史原因。拼字在十五和十六世紀開始標準化，部分是受到印刷術的影響，而同一時期，英語的發音正經歷一場稱為「母音大推移」的快速變化。結果，許多拼字被固定下來，反映的卻是很快就消失的發音。後來的學者更讓情況變得更糟，他們加入不發音的字母，來顯示一個字據稱源自拉丁文，例如 debt 中的 b。此後有人提出過好幾次拼字改革，但沒有一次成功，主要是因為改變熟悉字詞的拼法會遭到大眾強烈的抗拒。
zh.According to the passage, why is English: 根據文章，為什麼英文的拼字不一致？
zh.Printers deliberately introduced spellin: 印刷工人為了節省空間而故意製造拼字錯誤。
zh.Spelling became fixed while pronunciatio: 拼字在發音仍在改變時就被固定下來，後來又加入了不發音的字母。
zh.Spelling reformers have repeatedly made: 拼字改革者一再讓英文拼字變得更複雜。
zh.English borrowed all of its words direct: 英文的所有字彙都是直接從拉丁文借來的。
zh.Not stated. Printing helped standardise: 文章沒有這樣說。印刷術幫助了拼字的標準化，文中沒有提到印刷工人製造錯誤。
zh.Correct. Spelling was standardised “at t: 正確。拼字標準化 "at the same time as English pronunciation was changing rapidly"，後來學者又加入了不發音的字母，例如 debt 中的 b。
zh.The reverse. Reform attempts all failed:: 正好相反。改革的嘗試全都失敗了："none has succeeded"。
zh.Distorted. Scholars added letters to sho: 扭曲了原意。學者加入字母是為了顯示 "supposed Latin origin"，這並不表示所有英文字都來自拉丁文。

questions.passage: Remote work has proved surprisingly compatible with productivity for many individual tasks, from writing reports to processing data. A growing body of research suggests, however, that it may carry a hidden cost for innovation. One large study of scientific teams found that those working at a distance were more likely to develop existing ideas and less likely to produce breakthrough discoveries than teams working in the same place. The researchers suggested that breakthroughs often emerge from spontaneous conversations and the rapid exchange of half-formed ideas, which are harder to arrange through scheduled video calls. Some companies have responded with hybrid models, asking staff to come together on particular days for collaborative work while leaving focused individual tasks to be done at home.
questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Remote work reduces productivity on most individual tasks.
Remote work may suit individual tasks but make breakthrough ideas less likely.
Video calls are more effective than face-to-face meetings for creative work.
Most companies have banned remote work in order to protect innovation.
why: The reverse. Remote work “has proved surprisingly compatible with productivity for many individual tasks”.
Correct. The passage accepts that remote work suits individual tasks, then argues it “may carry a hidden cost for innovation”, as distant teams produce fewer breakthroughs.
The reverse. Spontaneous exchanges “are harder to arrange through scheduled video calls”.
Not stated. “Some companies” adopted hybrid models; nothing mentions banning remote work.

zh.Remote work has proved surprisingly comp: 事實證明，對於許多個人任務，從撰寫報告到處理數據，遠距工作與生產力出乎意料地相容。然而，越來越多的研究顯示，它可能對創新帶來隱藏的代價。一項針對科學團隊的大型研究發現，與在同一地點工作的團隊相比，遠距工作的團隊比較可能發展既有的想法，而比較不可能產生突破性的發現。研究人員認為，突破往往來自自發的對話，以及對尚未成熟的想法進行快速交流，而這些很難透過排定的視訊會議來安排。有些公司的因應方式是採用混合模式，要求員工在特定幾天聚在一起進行協作工作，而把需要專注的個人任務留在家中完成。
zh.What is the main point of the passage?: 這篇文章的主旨是什麼？
zh.Remote work reduces productivity on most: 遠距工作會降低大多數個人任務的生產力。
zh.Remote work may suit individual tasks bu: 遠距工作可能適合個人任務，卻使突破性的想法較難出現。
zh.Video calls are more effective than face: 在創意工作上，視訊會議比面對面會議更有效。
zh.Most companies have banned remote work i: 大多數公司為了保護創新而禁止遠距工作。
zh.The reverse. Remote work “has proved sur: 正好相反。遠距工作 "has proved surprisingly compatible with productivity for many individual tasks"。
zh.Correct. The passage accepts that remote: 正確。文章承認遠距工作適合個人任務，接著主張它 "may carry a hidden cost for innovation"，因為遠距團隊產生的突破較少。
zh.The reverse. Spontaneous exchanges “are: 正好相反。自發的交流 "are harder to arrange through scheduled video calls"。
zh.Not stated. “Some companies” adopted hyb: 文章沒有提到。是 "Some companies" 採用了混合模式；文中沒有提到禁止遠距工作。

questions.passage: When England introduced a small charge on single-use plastic bags in large shops in 2015, some critics dismissed it as too minor to make a difference. The results proved them wrong. Within a few years, the number of bags sold by the main supermarkets had fallen by more than ninety per cent. Behavioural economists point out that the size of the charge was less important than its existence. Before the charge, bags were free, so taking one required no decision at all. Once a price was attached, however small, shoppers had to make a conscious choice, and many began bringing their own bags. The charge also changed social norms, making it slightly embarrassing to be seen buying a new bag every time.
questions.q: According to the passage, why was the small charge so effective?
o: The charge was large enough to make bags unaffordable.
Shoppers had to make a conscious choice, and social norms changed.
Supermarkets stopped offering plastic bags entirely.
The law banned customers from bringing their own bags.
why: The passage stresses that the charge was small: “the size of the charge was less important than its existence”.
Correct. With any price attached, “shoppers had to make a conscious choice”, and the charge “also changed social norms”.
Not stated. Bags were still sold, just far fewer of them.
The reverse. “many began bringing their own bags”.

zh.When England introduced a small charge o: 2015 年英格蘭在大型商店對一次性塑膠袋收取少量費用時，一些批評者認為這筆費用太小，起不了作用。結果證明他們錯了。短短幾年內，主要超市售出的塑膠袋數量減少了百分之九十以上。行為經濟學家指出，費用的多寡不如費用的存在本身重要。在收費之前，塑膠袋是免費的，所以拿一個袋子完全不需要做任何決定。一旦附加了價格，無論多小，購物者都必須有意識地做出選擇，於是許多人開始自備購物袋。這項收費也改變了社會規範，讓人覺得每次都被看到買新袋子有點難為情。
zh.According to the passage, why was the sm: 根據文章，為什麼這筆小額收費如此有效？
zh.The charge was large enough to make bags: 這筆費用高到讓人買不起塑膠袋。
zh.Shoppers had to make a conscious choice,: 購物者必須有意識地做出選擇，而且社會規範也改變了。
zh.Supermarkets stopped offering plastic ba: 超市完全停止提供塑膠袋。
zh.The law banned customers from bringing t: 法律禁止顧客自備購物袋。
zh.The passage stresses that the charge was: 文章強調費用很小："the size of the charge was less important than its existence"。
zh.Correct. With any price attached, “shopp: 正確。只要附加了價格，"shoppers had to make a conscious choice"，而且這項收費 "also changed social norms"。
zh.Not stated. Bags were still sold, just f: 文章沒有提到。塑膠袋仍然有販售，只是數量少了很多。
zh.The reverse. “many began bringing their: 正好相反。"many began bringing their own bags"。

questions.passage: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, the town of Pompeii was buried under several metres of volcanic ash. The disaster preserved an extraordinary snapshot of daily Roman life: bread left in ovens, graffiti on walls and the outlines of people caught as they tried to flee. Excavations began in the eighteenth century, but early digging was often careless, driven by the search for treasure rather than an interest in ordinary life. Today archaeologists face a different problem. About a third of the site has never been excavated, and many experts argue it should be left that way, since the exposed ruins are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more than current ones.
questions.q: Why do many experts believe part of Pompeii should remain unexcavated?
o: The unexcavated areas contain nothing of interest.
Exposed ruins deteriorate, and future methods may reveal more.
Early excavators have already removed all the treasure.
Tourists are not allowed to visit the site.
why: Not stated, and it would make the argument pointless: experts want to preserve the area because of what it may reveal.
Correct. The exposed ruins “are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more”.
The passage says early digging searched for treasure, but not that all of it was removed, and this is not the experts’ reason.
The reverse. The ruins are under pressure from “millions of tourists”.

zh.When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, th: 西元 79 年維蘇威火山爆發時，龐貝城被埋在數公尺深的火山灰下。這場災難保存了羅馬人日常生活的一個非凡剪影：留在烤爐裡的麵包、牆上的塗鴉，以及試圖逃跑時被困住的人的輪廓。挖掘工作始於十八世紀，但早期的挖掘往往很草率，動機是尋找寶藏，而不是對日常生活感興趣。如今，考古學家面臨的是另一個問題。遺址約有三分之一從未被挖掘過，而許多專家認為應該維持原狀，因為已經暴露在外的遺跡正因天氣、植物生長以及數百萬遊客帶來的壓力而逐漸損壞，而且未來的技術可能會揭示比現在的技術多得多的東西。
zh.Why do many experts believe part of Pomp: 為什麼許多專家認為龐貝有一部分應該保持不挖掘？
zh.The unexcavated areas contain nothing of: 尚未挖掘的地區沒有任何值得研究的東西。
zh.Exposed ruins deteriorate, and future me: 暴露在外的遺跡會損壞，而且未來的方法可能揭示更多東西。
zh.Early excavators have already removed al: 早期的挖掘者已經把所有寶藏都拿走了。
zh.Tourists are not allowed to visit the si: 遊客不被允許參觀這個遺址。
zh.Not stated, and it would make the argume: 文章沒有這樣說，而且這會讓論點失去意義：專家想保留這個區域，正是因為它可能揭示的東西。
zh.Correct. The exposed ruins “are deterior: 正確。暴露在外的遺跡 "are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more"。
zh.The passage says early digging searched: 文章說早期的挖掘是在尋寶，但沒有說寶藏已全部被拿走，而且這也不是專家的理由。
zh.The reverse. The ruins are under pressur: 正好相反。遺跡正承受 "millions of tourists" 帶來的壓力。

questions.passage: In a well-known experiment, volunteers tasted several wines while lying in a brain scanner and were told the price of each one. In fact, two of the glasses contained the same wine, presented once as cheap and once as expensive. Participants not only said they preferred the wine they believed was expensive; activity also increased in a region of the brain linked to the experience of pleasure. The result suggests that expectations do not merely bias what people report but can change what they actually experience. Marketers have long relied on this effect, but it also has implications for medicine, where studies have found that patients sometimes report greater pain relief from a placebo they are told is costly.
questions.q: What does the experiment suggest?
o: Expensive wine is chemically different from cheap wine.
Information about price can change how pleasant something actually feels.
People lie about their preferences when they know they are being observed.
Brain scanners make wine taste better.
why: The experiment used the same wine twice, so there was no chemical difference at all.
Correct. Brain activity linked to pleasure rose, so expectations “can change what they actually experience”, not just what people report.
The passage argues against this: expectations “do not merely bias what people report”.
Nothing suggests the scanner affected taste; the only thing that varied was the stated price.

zh.In a well-known experiment, volunteers t: 在一項著名的實驗中，志願者躺在腦部掃描儀中品嚐幾種葡萄酒，並被告知每一種的價格。事實上，其中兩杯裝的是同一種酒，一次被說成便宜的，一次被說成昂貴的。受試者不僅說他們比較喜歡自以為昂貴的那杯酒；大腦中與愉悅感受有關的區域活動也增加了。這個結果顯示，預期不只會使人們所報告的內容產生偏差，還能改變他們實際的感受。行銷人員長久以來一直利用這種效應，但它對醫學也有啟示：研究發現，病人有時會表示，被告知價格昂貴的安慰劑能帶來更大的止痛效果。
zh.Expensive wine is chemically different f: 昂貴的葡萄酒在化學成分上與便宜的葡萄酒不同。
zh.Information about price can change how p: 價格資訊能改變某樣東西實際帶來的愉悅感受。
zh.People lie about their preferences when: 人們在知道自己被觀察時，會謊報自己的偏好。
腦部掃描儀會讓葡萄酒嚐起來更好喝。
zh.The experiment used the same wine twice,: 這項實驗用的是同一種酒兩次，所以完全沒有化學上的差異。
zh.Correct. Brain activity linked to pleasu: 正確。與愉悅有關的大腦活動增加了，所以預期 "can change what they actually experience"，而不只是改變人們所報告的內容。
zh.The passage argues against this: expecta: 文章反對這種看法：預期 "do not merely bias what people report"。
zh.Nothing suggests the scanner affected ta: 文中沒有任何跡象顯示掃描儀影響了味道；唯一改變的只有所告知的價格。

questions.passage: Robotic rovers have explored Mars for more than two decades, drilling rocks, analysing soil and sending back thousands of images. Advocates of human missions argue that a trained geologist could achieve in a week what a rover achieves in a year, because people can make quick judgements, move freely and respond to the unexpected. Critics reply that sending humans would cost many times more, since astronauts need air, food, water, radiation protection and a way to return home, and that the money could fund dozens of robotic missions. There is also the risk of contaminating Mars with Earth microbes, which could make it impossible to tell whether any life found there was native. For now, most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration.
questions.q: According to the passage, what is the view of most space agencies?
o: Human missions should replace robotic missions as soon as possible.
Robotic missions are pointless because humans work much faster.
Robots and humans have complementary roles, with robots preparing the way for human missions.
Mars should never be visited because of the risk of contamination.
why: This goes beyond the advocates’ argument and is not the agencies’ view; they see the two as working together.
The speed argument belongs to advocates of human missions, and the passage never calls robotic missions pointless.
Correct. “most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration.”
Contamination is raised as a risk, not as a reason never to go; the agencies expect “eventual human exploration”.

zh.Robotic rovers have explored Mars for mo: 機器人探測車探索火星已經超過二十年，它們鑽探岩石、分析土壤，並傳回了數千張影像。支持載人任務的人認為，一位受過訓練的地質學家一週就能完成探測車一年的工作量，因為人類能迅速做出判斷、自由移動，並應付意料之外的狀況。批評者則回應說，派人前往的成本會高出許多倍，因為太空人需要空氣、食物、水、輻射防護以及返回地球的方法，而這些錢足以資助數十次機器人任務。此外，還有用地球微生物污染火星的風險，這可能讓人無法判斷在那裡發現的任何生命是否為火星原生的。目前，大多數太空機構把機器人和人類視為互補的角色，由機器人任務為最終的載人探索鋪路。
zh.According to the passage, what is the vi: 根據文章，大多數太空機構的看法是什麼？
zh.Human missions should replace robotic mi: 載人任務應該盡快取代機器人任務。
zh.Robotic missions are pointless because h: 機器人任務毫無意義，因為人類的工作速度快得多。
zh.Robots and humans have complementary rol: 機器人和人類扮演互補的角色，由機器人為載人任務鋪路。
zh.Mars should never be visited because of: 因為有污染的風險，人類永遠不應該造訪火星。
zh.This goes beyond the advocates’ argument: 這超出了支持者的論點，也不是太空機構的看法；它們認為兩者應該相輔相成。
zh.The speed argument belongs to advocates: 速度的論點來自載人任務的支持者，而文章從未說機器人任務毫無意義。
zh.Correct. “most space agencies see robots: 正確。"most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration."
zh.Contamination is raised as a risk, not a: 污染被提出來是一種風險，而不是永遠不去的理由；太空機構預期會有 "eventual human exploration"。

questions.title: Lecture: how habits work
questions.text: Much of what we do each day is not the result of conscious decisions at all. Studies that ask people to record their actions every hour suggest that around forty per cent of daily behaviour is habitual, performed in the same context without deliberate thought. Habits form through a simple loop: a cue in the environment, a routine that follows it, and a reward that reinforces the connection. Over time, the brain shifts control of the routine from regions involved in planning to regions involved in automatic behaviour, which is why habits feel effortless. This has an important implication for anyone trying to change their behaviour. Because habits are triggered by cues, willpower is a poor tool for breaking them; it works for a while and then fails when we are tired or stressed. A more reliable strategy is to change the environment, removing the cue for an unwanted habit or making a desired behaviour easier to start. People who succeed in changing habits, the research suggests, rarely have more self-control than others. They simply arrange their surroundings so that they need it less.
keys: about 40% of daily behaviour is habitual
habits form through a loop of cue, routine and reward
the brain shifts control to automatic regions, so habits feel effortless
willpower is unreliable because habits are triggered by cues
change the environment: remove cues and make good behaviours easier
questions.model: The lecturer explained that around forty per cent of daily behaviour is habitual, formed through a loop of cue, routine and reward, as the brain shifts control to automatic regions. Because habits are triggered by cues, willpower is unreliable for changing them. Instead, people should change their environment by removing cues for unwanted habits and making desired behaviours easier, which is what successful people do.

zh.about 40% of daily behaviour is habitual: 約 40% 的日常行為是習慣性的
zh.habits form through a loop of cue, routi: 習慣透過「提示、慣性行為、獎勵」的循環形成
zh.the brain shifts control to automatic re: 大腦把控制權轉移到負責自動行為的區域，所以習慣做起來毫不費力
zh.willpower is unreliable because habits a: 由於習慣是被提示觸發的，意志力並不可靠
zh.change the environment: remove cues and: 改變環境：移除提示，並讓好的行為更容易開始
zh.The lecturer explained that around forty: 講者說明，約百分之四十的日常行為是習慣性的，透過「提示、慣性行為、獎勵」的循環形成，因為大腦會把控制權轉移到負責自動行為的區域。由於習慣是被提示觸發的，用意志力來改變習慣並不可靠。人們應該改變自己的環境，移除不良習慣的提示，並讓想養成的行為更容易開始，而這正是成功改變習慣的人所做的事。
zh.Much of what we do each day is not the r: 我們每天所做的事，有很大一部分根本不是有意識決定的結果。一些請受試者每小時記錄自己行為的研究顯示，約百分之四十的日常行為是習慣性的，是在相同情境下不經刻意思考就完成的。習慣透過一個簡單的循環形成：環境中的一個提示、隨之而來的一個慣性行為，以及強化這種連結的一個獎勵。隨著時間過去，大腦會把這個慣性行為的控制權，從負責規劃的區域轉移到負責自動行為的區域，這就是為什麼習慣做起來毫不費力。這對任何想改變自己行為的人都有重要的意涵。由於習慣是被提示觸發的，意志力並不是戒除習慣的好工具；它有效一陣子，然後在我們疲累或有壓力時就失靈了。更可靠的策略是改變環境，移除不良習慣的提示，或讓想要的行為更容易開始。研究顯示，成功改變習慣的人，很少比別人更有自制力。他們只是把周遭環境安排得讓自己比較不需要自制力而已。

questions.title: Lecture: the bridge that wobbled
questions.text: When the Millennium Bridge opened in London in 2000, it began to sway sideways as soon as crowds walked across it, and it was closed after just two days. The engineers had checked the bridge for vertical vibration, which is the usual concern with footbridges, but not for this sideways movement. The cause turned out to be the interaction between the bridge and the people on it. When a bridge sways slightly, pedestrians instinctively adjust their steps to keep their balance, and in doing so they start walking in time with the movement. That pushes the bridge further in the same direction, which makes more people fall into step, creating a feedback loop. Crucially, the effect appeared only once the number of people passed a critical threshold. The solution was to fit dampers, devices that absorb energy, under the deck, and the bridge reopened two years later. The episode changed design codes for footbridges around the world.
keys: the Millennium Bridge swayed sideways on opening and closed after two days
engineers had checked vertical vibration but not sideways movement
pedestrians adjusted their steps and fell into time with the sway, creating a feedback loop
the effect appeared only above a critical number of people
dampers fixed the problem, and footbridge design codes changed worldwide
questions.model: The lecturer described how London’s Millennium Bridge swayed sideways when it opened in 2000 and closed after two days. Engineers had only checked vertical vibration. The cause was a feedback loop: pedestrians adjusted their steps to the sway, walking in time with it and increasing the movement, once crowds passed a critical size. Dampers solved the problem, and design codes worldwide changed.

zh.the Millennium Bridge swayed sideways on: 千禧橋在啟用時左右搖晃，兩天後就關閉了
zh.engineers had checked vertical vibration: 工程師檢查過垂直方向的振動，卻沒有檢查左右方向的晃動
zh.pedestrians adjusted their steps and fel: 行人調整步伐，與晃動同步行走，形成回饋循環
zh.the effect appeared only above a critica: 這種效應只有在人數超過某個臨界值時才會出現
zh.dampers fixed the problem, and footbridg: 加裝阻尼器解決了問題，全世界的人行橋設計規範也因此改變
zh.The lecturer described how London’s Mill: 講者說明，倫敦的千禧橋在 2000 年啟用時左右搖晃，兩天後就關閉了。工程師只檢查過垂直方向的振動。原因是一個回饋循環：一旦人潮超過某個臨界規模，行人就會配合晃動調整步伐，與晃動同步行走，使搖晃加劇。加裝阻尼器解決了這個問題，全世界的設計規範也隨之改變。
zh.When the Millennium Bridge opened in Lon: 倫敦的千禧橋在 2000 年啟用時，只要有人群走過，橋就開始左右搖晃，結果僅僅兩天後就關閉了。工程師檢查過橋的垂直振動，這是人行橋通常要注意的問題，卻沒有檢查這種左右方向的晃動。原因最後被發現是橋與橋上行人之間的交互作用。當橋輕微晃動時，行人會本能地調整步伐以保持平衡，而這樣一來，他們就開始配合晃動的節奏行走。這會把橋進一步推向同一個方向，使更多人跟上同樣的步調，形成一個回饋循環。關鍵在於，這種效應只有在人數超過某個臨界值時才會出現。解決方法是在橋面下方加裝阻尼器，也就是能吸收能量的裝置，而這座橋在兩年後重新開放。這起事件改變了全世界人行橋的設計規範。

questions.title: Lecture: spacing your study
questions.text: If you have ten hours to prepare for an exam, how should you divide them? Most students cram, spending most of the time in the last day or two. More than a century of research on memory suggests this is one of the least efficient strategies available. The spacing effect, first described in the 1880s, shows that the same amount of study produces much longer-lasting memory when it is spread out over time. The reason seems to be that forgetting a little between sessions forces the brain to work harder to retrieve information, and that effort strengthens the memory. Cramming can produce good results the next morning, which is why students keep doing it, but most of what is learned disappears within weeks. The best gap depends on how long you need to remember the material: for an exam in a week, reviewing every day or two works well, while for knowledge needed in a year, gaps of several weeks are better. In practice, spacing is simple to apply, but it requires starting early.
keys: cramming is one of the least efficient ways to study
the spacing effect: study spread over time lasts much longer
forgetting a little between sessions makes retrieval harder, which strengthens memory
cramming works the next morning but most is forgotten within weeks
the best gap depends on how long you need to remember, so start early
questions.model: The lecturer explained that cramming is inefficient because of the spacing effect: the same study time produces longer-lasting memory when spread out. Partial forgetting between sessions makes retrieval harder, which strengthens memory. Cramming works briefly but fades within weeks. The best gap depends on how long material must be remembered, so students should start revising early.

zh.cramming is one of the least efficient w: 臨時抱佛腳是最沒效率的讀書方法之一
zh.the spacing effect: study spread over ti: 間隔效應：分散在一段時間內的學習能記得更久
zh.forgetting a little between sessions mak: 在每次學習之間稍微遺忘，會讓回想變得更費力，因而強化記憶
zh.cramming works the next morning but most: 臨時抱佛腳隔天早上有效，但大部分內容幾週內就會忘記
zh.the best gap depends on how long you nee: 最佳間隔取決於你需要記住多久，所以要及早開始
zh.The lecturer explained that cramming is: 講者說明，由於間隔效應的緣故，臨時抱佛腳是沒有效率的：同樣的讀書時間，分散開來能產生更持久的記憶。在每次學習之間部分遺忘，會讓回想變得更費力，因而強化記憶。臨時抱佛腳只有短暫的效果，幾週內就會淡忘。最佳的間隔取決於內容需要記住多久，所以學生應該及早開始複習。
zh.If you have ten hours to prepare for an: 如果你有十個小時準備一場考試，你應該如何分配這些時間？大多數學生會臨時抱佛腳，把大部分時間花在最後一兩天。一百多年來關於記憶的研究顯示，這是現有最沒效率的策略之一。間隔效應最早在 1880 年代被描述出來，它顯示同樣份量的學習，如果分散在一段時間內進行，能產生持久得多的記憶。原因似乎是，在每次學習之間稍微遺忘一些，會迫使大腦更努力地提取資訊，而這份努力會強化記憶。臨時抱佛腳在隔天早上可能會有不錯的效果，這就是學生一直這樣做的原因，但學到的東西大部分會在幾週內消失。最佳的間隔取決於你需要記住這些內容多久：如果考試在一週後，每一兩天複習一次效果很好；如果是一年後才需要用到的知識，間隔數週會更好。實際上，間隔學習很容易運用，但需要及早開始。

questions.title: Lecture: the cane toad
questions.text: In 1935, around one hundred cane toads were brought from Hawaii to north-eastern Australia to control beetles that were damaging sugar cane crops. The plan failed almost completely. The beetles lived high on the cane stalks, where the toads could not reach them, and the toads found plenty of other food instead. With no natural predators in Australia and the ability to lay tens of thousands of eggs at a time, the toads spread rapidly. Today there are estimated to be more than two hundred million of them, and their range expands by up to fifty kilometres a year. The damage comes mainly from their poison. Native predators such as quolls, goannas and freshwater crocodiles, which have never encountered toads before, often die after trying to eat one. Scientists are now experimenting with conditioned taste aversion, feeding predators small, non-lethal pieces of toad that make them sick, so they learn to avoid the real thing. The episode is still taught as a warning about introducing species without understanding the ecosystem.
keys: cane toads were brought to Australia in 1935 to control beetles in sugar cane
the plan failed because the toads could not reach the beetles
with no predators and huge egg numbers, they now number over 200 million
their poison kills native predators that try to eat them
scientists are teaching predators to avoid toads; the case warns against introducing species
questions.model: The lecturer explained that cane toads were introduced to Australia in 1935 to control crop beetles but failed because they could not reach them. Without predators and laying huge numbers of eggs, they now number over two hundred million. Their poison kills native predators, so scientists are teaching predators to avoid toads, and the case warns against introducing species carelessly.

questions.text: Welcome to the second week of term. I want to take a few minutes to explain how the writing centre works, because every year students discover it only a week before their dissertation is due, which is far too late to be useful. The centre offers one-to-one appointments of forty-five minutes with a trained tutor. You can book up to two appointments a week through the student portal, and I strongly recommend booking early, because slots fill up quickly after the middle of term. Please be clear about what the tutors will and will not do. They will help you plan an essay, organise an argument and understand feedback you have received from your lecturers. They will not proofread your work line by line, and they will not tell you what mark it is likely to receive. If you bring a draft, bring a printed copy and a specific question, such as whether your conclusion follows from your evidence. The centre also runs drop-in workshops on Wednesday afternoons on topics like referencing and paraphrasing. These do not need to be booked, but they are limited to twenty students, so arrive on time. Finally, the centre is free for all students, including those studying part-time or online, and online students can hold their appointments by video call.

questions.text: When cities plan for hotter summers, the first tool they usually reach for is air conditioning, but there is growing evidence that trees deserve far more attention. A mature street tree cools its surroundings in two ways. Its canopy shades pavements and walls, which would otherwise absorb heat all day and release it at night. And its leaves release water vapour, which cools the air in the same way that sweat cools skin. Measurements in several European cities have found that streets with continuous tree cover can be up to five degrees cooler at pedestrian level than similar streets without trees. The benefits are not only thermal. Tree-lined streets have been linked with lower levels of stress, and some studies suggest that people walk more where streets are shaded. However, planting a tree is not the same as growing one. In many cities, a large share of newly planted trees die within the first few years, usually because they are not watered during dry summers or because their roots have too little space under the pavement. For that reason, experts increasingly argue that budgets should be measured not by the number of trees planted, but by the number that survive to maturity, which can take twenty years or more.

questions.text: Most people assume that when they put plastic in a recycling bin, it will become a new plastic product. In reality, only a small fraction of plastic is ever recycled; global estimates put the figure at under ten per cent. There are several reasons. First, plastic is not one material but many, and different types cannot usually be melted together. A single yoghurt pot may combine two or three plastics, which makes it almost impossible to recycle. Second, each time plastic is recycled, its quality declines, so it is often turned into lower-value products, such as park benches, that cannot themselves be recycled again. Third, and most importantly, recycled plastic has to compete on price with new plastic made from oil and gas. When oil prices fall, new plastic becomes cheaper and demand for recycled material collapses. For many years, wealthy countries dealt with this by exporting their plastic waste to Asia, until China banned most imports in 2018. Since then, attention has shifted towards reducing plastic use in the first place, and towards designing packaging from a single type of plastic that is easier to process. Neither approach is a complete solution, but both are more effective than simply buying a larger recycling bin.

questions.text: Good morning, everyone. With the exam period starting in two weeks, I want to go through the arrangements, because they have changed slightly this year. First, all written exams will now take place in the sports hall rather than in individual lecture theatres, so please check your timetable for the correct seating area within the hall. You must arrive at least twenty minutes before the start time. The doors open twenty minutes early, and anyone who arrives more than thirty minutes after the start will not be admitted. Second, you need to bring your student card. If you have lost it, you can get a temporary replacement from the student office, but this takes two working days, so do not leave it until the morning of the exam. Mobile phones must be switched off and placed in the clear plastic bags provided at the entrance; they cannot be kept in pockets, even if they are switched off. Water is allowed, but only in a transparent bottle with the label removed. Finally, if you are ill on the day of an exam, do not come in. Contact the exams office before the exam starts and submit a medical certificate within five days, and you will be offered a place in the resit period without penalty.

questions.text: When coffee arrived in Europe in the seventeenth century, it did more than change what people drank. It created a new kind of public space. The first coffeehouse in England opened in Oxford in 1650, and within a few decades London had hundreds of them. For the price of a single cup, anyone could sit for hours, read newspapers and join conversations, regardless of social rank. That openness made coffeehouses centres of information. Merchants met in them to exchange news about ships and cargoes, and several important institutions grew out of particular coffeehouses: one became a famous insurance market, and another was the origin of the London Stock Exchange. Scientists also used them for informal debate, and some were nicknamed penny universities, because the conversation was said to be as educational as a university course. Not everyone approved. In 1675, the king attempted to close them all, claiming they spread false rumours about the government, but the order caused such an outcry that it was withdrawn within days. Historians sometimes describe coffeehouses as an early version of social media: noisy, influential, and difficult for the authorities to control. Their influence is a reminder that new places to meet can change how ideas spread.

zh.When coffee arrived in Europe in the sev: 十七世紀咖啡傳入歐洲時，它改變的不只是人們喝的東西，還創造了一種新型態的公共空間。英格蘭第一家咖啡館於 1650 年在牛津開幕，不到幾十年，倫敦就有了好幾百家。只要花一杯咖啡的錢，任何人都能坐上好幾個小時、看報紙、加入談話，不論社會地位高低。這種開放性使咖啡館成為資訊的中心。商人在咖啡館裡碰面，交換船隻和貨物的消息，而好幾個重要的機構就是從特定的咖啡館發展出來的：其中一家成為著名的保險市場，另一家則是倫敦證券交易所的起源。科學家也在咖啡館裡進行非正式的辯論，有些咖啡館甚至被暱稱為「一便士大學」，因為據說那裡的談話和大學課程一樣有教育意義。並不是每個人都認同。1675 年，國王試圖關閉所有咖啡館，聲稱它們散布關於政府的不實謠言，但這道命令引起了強烈的抗議，幾天之內就被撤回了。歷史學家有時把咖啡館形容為早期版本的社群媒體：喧鬧、有影響力，而且當局難以控制。它們的影響提醒我們，新的聚會場所能改變思想傳播的方式。

questions.text: If you have ever compared the price you paid for a flight with the person sitting next to you, you may have discovered a large difference. Airlines use a system called yield management, which divides the seats on a flight into many price levels, sometimes more than twenty. The cheapest levels are released first and sell out, and as the departure date approaches, the remaining seats move into higher price bands. The logic is that people who book early, such as holidaymakers, are usually sensitive to price, while those who book late, often business travellers, are more willing to pay. Airlines also adjust prices according to demand, so a flight during the school holidays will cost more than the same flight a week later. A common belief is that airlines raise prices when you search for the same flight several times, using information stored in your browser. Investigations have found little evidence for this; the rises people notice usually happen because cheaper seats have genuinely sold out in the meantime. For travellers, the practical advice is simple: book early for popular dates, and be flexible if you can. Flying midweek, rather than on a Friday or Sunday, is often noticeably cheaper as well.
questions.q: Which points does the speaker make?
o: Late bookers are usually the most price-sensitive customers.
Seats on one flight may be sold at many different price levels.
Flights during school holidays tend to cost more.
There is strong evidence that repeated searches make prices rise.
Price rises during a search are usually caused by cheaper seats selling out.

zh.Seats on one flight may be sold at many: 同一班飛機的座位可能以許多不同的價格等級出售。
