zh.If you have ever compared the price you: 如果你曾經把自己買的機票價格和坐在旁邊的人比較過，你可能發現了很大的差異。航空公司使用一種稱為「收益管理」的系統，把一個航班的座位分成許多價格等級，有時超過二十個。最便宜的等級會最先釋出並售罄，而隨著出發日期接近，剩下的座位就會進入較高的價格區間。其中的邏輯是，提早訂票的人，例如度假旅客，通常對價格很敏感，而晚訂票的人，通常是商務旅客，比較願意付錢。航空公司也會依需求調整價格，所以學校假期期間的航班，會比一週後同一班航班更貴。一種常見的說法是，當你多次搜尋同一個航班時，航空公司會利用你瀏覽器中儲存的資訊來提高票價。調查發現這種說法幾乎沒有證據；人們注意到的漲價，通常是因為較便宜的座位在這段期間確實賣完了。對旅客來說，實用的建議很簡單：熱門日期要提早訂票，而且盡可能保持彈性。在週間而不是星期五或星期日搭機，通常也會便宜不少。

questions.text: This session is about finding and evaluating sources for your essays. Most of you will start with a general search engine, and that is fine for getting an overview, but the results are ranked partly by popularity, not reliability. For academic work, you should move on to the library databases, which you can access through the library website with your university login, including from home. When you find a source, ask four questions. Who wrote it, and what are their qualifications? When was it published? In fast-moving fields, a study from fifteen years ago may be out of date. What evidence does it use, and can you check it? And why was it written: to inform, or to sell something? Peer-reviewed journal articles are usually the most reliable, but peer review is not a guarantee, so you still need to read critically. Wikipedia is a useful starting point for background and for its reference lists, but you should not cite it in your essays; follow its references to the original sources instead. Finally, keep a record of everything you read as you go, including page numbers. Trying to find a quotation again the night before a deadline is a frustrating experience that many of you will otherwise have.

questions.text: Elephants communicate using a remarkable range of sounds, but many of their calls cannot be heard by humans at all. These are infrasonic rumbles, pitched below the lower limit of human hearing. Low-frequency sounds lose little energy as they travel, so these rumbles can carry for several kilometres, particularly in the cool, still air of early morning and evening. Researchers first became aware of them in the 1980s, when a scientist standing near captive elephants noticed a strange throbbing in the air, similar to the feeling of distant thunder. Recording equipment later confirmed that the animals were producing sounds too low to hear. Elephants appear to use these calls to coordinate the movements of family groups that are out of sight of one another, and females use them to signal to males when they are ready to mate. There is also evidence that elephants detect vibrations through the ground, possibly using sensitive cells in their feet and trunks. Understanding these calls has practical value: conservationists now use listening devices in forests to monitor elephant populations, since the animals are far easier to hear than to see. The same recordings can also warn villages when elephants are approaching their crops.

questions.text: The London Underground, which opened in 1863, was the first underground railway in the world. The first line ran for about six kilometres between Paddington and Farringdon, and it was built using a method called cut and cover: workers dug a deep trench along the route of an existing road, built the tunnel, and then covered it over again. This caused enormous disruption, but it was cheaper than tunnelling. The early trains were pulled by steam locomotives, and although special engines were designed to reduce smoke, the tunnels were famously dirty and filled with fumes. Despite this, the railway was an immediate success, carrying tens of thousands of passengers on its first day. Later lines were built much deeper using tunnelling shields, which allowed workers to dig safely through the London clay without disturbing the streets above. These deep tunnels became usable for passengers only after the introduction of electric trains in the 1890s, since steam engines could not be used in narrow tunnels so far underground. The circular shape of these deep tunnels is why Londoners still call the Underground the Tube. Today the network carries several million passengers every day.
questions.q: Which of the following are true according to the lecture?

The name the Tube comes from the round shape of the deep tunnels.

zh.Which of the following are true accordin: 根據這場講座，下列哪些是正確的？

zh.The London Underground, which opened in: 1863 年通車的倫敦地鐵，是世界上第一條地下鐵路。第一條路線在帕丁頓和法靈頓之間延伸約六公里，採用一種稱為「明挖覆蓋法」的方式建造：工人沿著一條現有道路的路線挖出一條深溝，建好隧道，然後再把它覆蓋起來。這造成了極大的干擾，但比鑽掘隧道便宜。早期的列車由蒸汽機車牽引，雖然設計了特殊的引擎來減少煙霧，但隧道還是出了名地骯髒、充滿廢氣。儘管如此，這條鐵路一開通就大獲成功，第一天就載運了數萬名乘客。後來的路線利用隧道盾構機建得更深，讓工人能安全地穿過倫敦黏土層挖掘，而不會干擾上方的街道。這些深層隧道直到 1890 年代引進電力列車之後，才能用來載客，因為蒸汽機車無法在位於地下這麼深的狹窄隧道中使用。這些深層隧道的圓形外觀，就是倫敦人至今仍把地鐵稱為「管子」的原因。如今，這個路網每天載運數百萬名乘客。

questions.text: Before we finish the orientation, I want to tell you about the support that is available if you find things difficult this year, because many students only look for it when a problem has become serious. The student wellbeing centre offers free, confidential counselling. You can refer yourself online; you do not need a letter from a doctor or a tutor, and most students are seen within a week. If you need to talk to someone urgently, there is a drop-in service every weekday between twelve and two, and outside those hours the university runs a phone line that is staffed twenty-four hours a day. Counselling is not only for serious crises. Students come to us about homesickness, stress before exams, relationship problems and difficulties with sleep. We also run group workshops, for example on managing anxiety and on studying effectively, which are a good way to learn practical skills alongside other students. If you have a disability or a long-term health condition, please register with the disability service as early as possible, even if you are not sure you will need support, because arrangements such as extra time in exams can take several weeks to put in place.

曆法年和太陽年並不完全吻合。地球繞太陽一圈大約需要三百六十五又四分之一天，所以每四年會多加一天，讓季節保持同步。即使這樣也還是稍微多算了一點，因為真正的數字比四分之一略少。為了修正這個誤差，世紀年只有在能被四百整除時才是閏年。這就是為什麼 2000 年是閏年而 1900 年不是，也是為什麼這套曆法在數千年內都應該能保持準確。

parts: Healthy coral reefs are surprisingly noisy places, full of the clicks, grunts and whistles of fish and shrimp. Young fish drifting in the open ocean use these sounds to

. In one experiment, researchers placed underwater
on degraded patches of reef and played recordings of healthy reefs. Twice as many fish arrived as on silent patches, suggesting that sound could help speed up reef

健康的珊瑚礁是出乎意料地嘈雜的地方，充滿了魚類和蝦子發出的喀嗒聲、咕嚕聲和哨聲。在開闊海洋中漂流的幼魚會利用這些聲音來找到適合定居的珊瑚礁。當珊瑚礁受損時，它們會變得安靜許多，前來的幼魚也會變少。在一項實驗中，研究人員在退化的珊瑚礁區塊放置水下喇叭，並播放健康珊瑚礁的錄音。到達的魚是安靜區塊的兩倍，這顯示聲音可能有助於加快珊瑚礁的復原。

志工服務通常被認為是對他人有益的事，但越來越多證據顯示，它對志工本身也有好處。針對年長者的研究發現，定期從事志工服務的人，憂鬱的程度較低，也比較不容易罹患高血壓。這些好處似乎取決於動機：主要為了幫助他人而當志工的人，獲益比那些出於個人原因（例如為了讓履歷更好看）而當志工的人更多。研究人員認為，志工服務所帶來的目標感和社會連結，可以解釋大部分的效果。

questions.title: Wind farms at sea
parts: Offshore wind farms, built in the sea some distance from the coast, have several advantages over those on land. Winds at sea are stronger and more
, so each turbine produces more electricity. They also face fewer objections from local residents, because they are built far from
. However, construction is expensive, and maintenance is difficult in rough
, when boats cannot safely reach the turbines. Newer designs use floating platforms anchored to the seabed, which allow turbines to be placed in much deeper
, where the strongest winds are often found.

zh.Offshore wind farms, built in the sea so: 建在離岸一段距離海上的離岸風場，比陸上風場有好幾項優勢。海上的風更強也更 ____ ，所以每座風機能產生更多電力。它們也比較少遭到當地居民反對，因為它們建在遠離 ____ 的地方。然而，興建成本很高，而且在惡劣的 ____ 下維修很困難，因為船隻無法安全抵達風機。較新的設計使用錨定在海床上的浮動平台，讓風機可以設置在深得多的 ____ 中，而那裡往往有最強的風。
建在離岸一段距離海上的離岸風場，比陸上風場有好幾項優勢。海上的風更強也更穩定，所以每座風機能產生更多電力。它們也比較少遭到當地居民反對，因為它們建在遠離住家的地方。然而，興建成本很高，而且在惡劣的天候下維修很困難，因為船隻無法安全抵達風機。較新的設計使用錨定在海床上的浮動平台，讓風機可以設置在深得多的水域中，而那裡往往有最強的風。

questions.title: The modern Olympics
parts: The modern Olympic Games were first held in Athens in 1896, inspired by the ancient games that had taken place at Olympia for more than a thousand
. Only fourteen countries and around two hundred and forty
took part, all of them men. Women first competed four years later, in sports including tennis and
. Today more than two hundred countries participate, and the games have become one of the most watched
in the world, followed by billions of people on television and online.

zh.The modern Olympic Games were first held: 現代奧運會於 1896 年首次在雅典舉行，其靈感來自在奧林匹亞舉辦了一千多 ____ 的古代運動會。當時只有十四個國家、大約兩百四十名 ____ 參加，而且全都是男性。女性在四年後首次參賽，項目包括網球和 ____ 。如今有超過兩百個國家參加，奧運已成為全世界收看人數最多的 ____ 之一，有數十億人透過電視和網路觀看。
現代奧運會於 1896 年首次在雅典舉行，其靈感來自在奧林匹亞舉辦了一千多年的古代運動會。當時只有十四個國家、大約兩百四十名運動員參加，而且全都是男性。女性在四年後首次參賽，項目包括網球和高爾夫球。如今有超過兩百個國家參加，奧運已成為全世界收看人數最多的賽事之一，有數十億人透過電視和網路觀看。

questions.title: Why we blush
parts: Blushing is a uniquely human
. It happens when the blood vessels in the face widen, allowing more blood to flow close to the skin. Charles Darwin called it the most human of all
, because it seems to occur only when we are aware of what other people think of us. Recent research suggests that blushing may serve a social
: people who blush after making a mistake are judged more favourably and are more easily
than those who show no reaction at all.

zh.Blushing is a uniquely human ____ . It h: 臉紅是人類獨有的一種 ____ 。它發生在臉部血管擴張，讓更多血液流到靠近皮膚的地方時。查爾斯・達爾文稱它為所有 ____ 中最具人性的一種，因為它似乎只在我們意識到別人如何看待我們時才會發生。近來的研究顯示，臉紅可能具有一種社會 ____ ：犯錯後會臉紅的人，會被評價得比較正面，也比完全沒有反應的人更容易被 ____ 。
zh.Blushing is a uniquely human response. I: 臉紅是人類獨有的一種反應。它發生在臉部血管擴張，讓更多血液流到靠近皮膚的地方時。查爾斯・達爾文稱它為所有表情中最具人性的一種，因為它似乎只在我們意識到別人如何看待我們時才會發生。近來的研究顯示，臉紅可能具有一種社會功能：犯錯後會臉紅的人，會被評價得比較正面，也比完全沒有反應的人更容易被原諒。

questions.title: Recycling glass
parts: Glass can be recycled endlessly without losing

, which makes it one of the most sustainable packaging materials available. Recycled glass, known as cullet, melts at a lower temperature than the raw materials used to make new glass, so using it saves
and reduces emissions. However, glass is heavy, which makes it expensive to
over long distances, and different colours usually have to be kept separate. For this reason, some countries encourage people to
glass bottles rather than simply recycling them.

zh.Glass can be recycled endlessly without: 玻璃可以無限次回收而不會失去 ____ ，這使它成為現有最具永續性的包裝材料之一。回收的玻璃稱為碎玻璃，它的熔化溫度比製造新玻璃的原料低，所以使用它能節省 ____ 並減少排放。然而，玻璃很重，長途 ____ 的成本很高，而且不同顏色的玻璃通常必須分開處理。因此，有些國家鼓勵人們 ____ 玻璃瓶，而不只是回收它們。
玻璃可以無限次回收而不會失去品質，這使它成為現有最具永續性的包裝材料之一。回收的玻璃稱為碎玻璃，它的熔化溫度比製造新玻璃的原料低，所以使用它能節省能源並減少排放。然而，玻璃很重，長途運輸的成本很高，而且不同顏色的玻璃通常必須分開處理。因此，有些國家鼓勵人們重複使用玻璃瓶，而不只是回收它們。

questions.title: Buildings that survive earthquakes
parts: Earthquakes rarely kill people directly; most deaths are caused by collapsing
. Engineers have therefore developed several techniques to make structures safer. One of the most effective is base isolation, in which a building rests on flexible
that absorb much of the movement of the ground. Another is to add large dampers, which reduce
in tall towers during strong shaking. In many countries, strict building
now require these features in new construction, although older buildings often remain at risk.

zh.Earthquakes rarely kill people directly;: 地震很少直接致人於死；大多數的死亡是由倒塌的 ____ 造成的。因此，工程師發展出好幾種讓建築更安全的技術。其中最有效的一種是「隔震」，讓建築物坐落在能吸收大部分地面晃動的彈性 ____ 上。另一種是加裝大型阻尼器，在強烈搖晃時減少高樓的 ____ 。在許多國家，嚴格的建築 ____ 現在規定新建築必須具備這些設計，不過舊建築往往仍有風險。
地震很少直接致人於死；大多數的死亡是由倒塌的建築物造成的。因此，工程師發展出好幾種讓建築更安全的技術。其中最有效的一種是「隔震」，讓建築物坐落在能吸收大部分地面晃動的彈性支承上。另一種是加裝大型阻尼器，在強烈搖晃時減少高樓的擺動。在許多國家，嚴格的建築法規現在規定新建築必須具備這些設計，不過舊建築往往仍有風險。

questions.title: Saving water at home
parts: Most of the water used in homes goes on washing and
the toilet. Fortunately, simple changes can make a large difference. Taking a shorter
can save dozens of litres a day, and fixing a dripping tap prevents a surprising amount of waste over the course of a year. Many modern toilets use a dual-flush
, which allows a smaller amount of water to be used when a full flush is not needed. In dry regions, some households also collect
to water their gardens.

zh.Most of the water used in homes goes on: 家庭用水大多花在清洗和 ____ 馬桶上。幸好，簡單的改變就能帶來很大的差別。縮短 ____ 的時間每天可以省下好幾十公升的水，而修好滴水的水龍頭，一年下來能避免驚人的浪費。許多現代馬桶採用兩段式沖水 ____ ，在不需要完全沖水時，可以使用較少的水量。在乾燥地區，有些家庭還會收集 ____ 來澆花。
家庭用水大多花在清洗和沖馬桶上。幸好，簡單的改變就能帶來很大的差別。縮短淋浴的時間每天可以省下好幾十公升的水，而修好滴水的水龍頭，一年下來能避免驚人的浪費。許多現代馬桶採用兩段式沖水系統，在不需要完全沖水時，可以使用較少的水量。在乾燥地區，有些家庭還會收集雨水來澆花。

questions.text: Many people feel sleepy in the early afternoon and blame their lunch. But the afternoon dip in alertness happens even when people skip lunch entirely. It is built into the body’s daily rhythm: our internal clock produces a small drop in alertness between roughly two and four in the afternoon, a weaker version of the much larger drop during the night. A heavy meal can make the effect worse, but it does not cause it. This helps explain why the siesta developed in many hot countries, and why short naps of around twenty minutes in the early afternoon can improve performance without leaving people groggy.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: The afternoon dip in alertness is part of the body’s natural daily rhythm; lunch can make it worse but does not cause it, which helps explain the siesta and the value of short naps.
Eating a large lunch is the main reason people feel tired in the afternoon, so skipping lunch is the most effective way to stay alert.
The siesta developed in hot countries because the afternoon heat made it impossible to work outdoors.
Short afternoon naps are harmful because they leave people groggy for the rest of the day.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.The afternoon dip in alertness is part o: 午後的警覺度下降是身體自然日常節律的一部分；午餐會讓情況更糟，但並不是原因，這有助於解釋午睡習俗以及短暫小睡的價值。
zh.Eating a large lunch is the main reason: 吃一頓豐盛的午餐是人們下午感到疲倦的主要原因，所以不吃午餐是保持清醒最有效的方法。
zh.The siesta developed in hot countries be: 午睡習俗在炎熱的國家發展起來，是因為下午的高溫使人無法在戶外工作。
zh.Short afternoon naps are harmful because: 下午短暫小睡是有害的，因為會讓人一整個下午都昏昏沉沉。
zh.Many people feel sleepy in the early aft: 許多人在午後會感到昏昏欲睡，並把原因歸咎於午餐。但即使完全不吃午餐，午後的警覺度下降仍然會發生。這是內建在身體日常節律中的：我們的生理時鐘會在大約下午兩點到四點之間讓警覺度小幅下降，這是夜間那次大幅下降的較弱版本。一頓豐盛的餐點會讓這種效應更明顯，但並不是造成它的原因。這有助於解釋為什麼許多炎熱的國家發展出午睡的習俗，以及為什麼在午後早段小睡約二十分鐘，可以提升表現，又不會讓人昏昏沉沉。

questions.text: Before the railways, every town in Britain kept its own local time, set by the position of the sun. Bristol, for example, was about ten minutes behind London. For people who rarely travelled far, this caused no problems. The railways changed that. Timetables that listed a different time at every station confused passengers and, more seriously, increased the risk of collisions on single tracks. During the 1840s, the railway companies adopted London time across their networks, and many towns followed, although some resisted for years, displaying two minute hands on their public clocks. Standard time only became the legal time throughout Britain in 1880.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Towns once set their clocks by the sun, but the confusion and danger this caused on the railways led companies to adopt London time in the 1840s, and standard time became law in 1880.
Bristol refused to accept London time and kept its own local time well into the twentieth century.
Railway collisions in the 1840s were mainly caused by public clocks that had two minute hands.
Local time was introduced by the railway companies so that their timetables would match the position of the sun.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Towns once set their clocks by the sun,: 各城鎮過去依太陽來設定時鐘，但這在鐵路上造成的混亂與危險，促使鐵路公司在 1840 年代採用倫敦時間，而標準時間則在 1880 年成為法定時間。
zh.Bristol refused to accept London time an: 布里斯托拒絕接受倫敦時間，並一直使用自己的地方時間直到二十世紀。
zh.Railway collisions in the 1840s were mai: 1840 年代的火車相撞事故，主要是由有兩根分針的公共時鐘造成的。
zh.Local time was introduced by the railway: 地方時間是由鐵路公司引進的，好讓火車時刻表能與太陽的位置一致。
zh.Before the railways, every town in Brita: 在鐵路出現之前，英國的每個城鎮都依照太陽的位置，使用自己的地方時間。例如，布里斯托就比倫敦慢了大約十分鐘。對很少遠行的人來說，這並不會造成任何問題。鐵路改變了這一切。每一站都列出不同時間的時刻表讓乘客感到困惑，更嚴重的是，這增加了單線鐵軌上發生相撞的風險。在 1840 年代，各鐵路公司在其路網中採用了倫敦時間，許多城鎮也跟著採用，不過有些城鎮抗拒了好幾年，在公共時鐘上顯示兩根分針。標準時間直到 1880 年才成為全英國的法定時間。

questions.text: Archaeologists excavating ancient Egyptian tombs have found pots of honey that are thousands of years old and still, in principle, edible. Honey resists spoiling for several reasons. It contains very little water, and its high concentration of sugar draws moisture out of any bacteria or fungi that land in it, so they cannot survive. It is also naturally acidic. In addition, bees add an enzyme to the nectar that produces small amounts of hydrogen peroxide, a mild antiseptic. The combination makes honey one of the few foods that can be stored almost indefinitely, provided it is sealed so that it cannot absorb moisture from the air.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Honey keeps almost indefinitely because its low water content, high sugar, acidity and a natural antiseptic stop microbes from growing, as long as it stays sealed.
Ancient Egyptians preserved honey in tombs by adding special chemicals whose recipe has since been lost.
Honey spoils quickly once it has been opened, so it should always be kept in a refrigerator.
Bees produce honey mainly as a way of killing bacteria inside the hive.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Honey keeps almost indefinitely because: 蜂蜜幾乎可以無限期保存，因為它的低含水量、高糖分、酸性以及一種天然抗菌物質能阻止微生物生長，只要保持密封即可。
zh.Ancient Egyptians preserved honey in tom: 古埃及人在墓中保存蜂蜜時，加入了特殊的化學物質，而這種配方如今已經失傳。
zh.Honey spoils quickly once it has been op: 蜂蜜一旦開封就會很快變質，所以一定要放在冰箱裡保存。
zh.Bees produce honey mainly as a way of ki: 蜜蜂製造蜂蜜的主要目的，是殺死蜂巢內的細菌。
zh.Archaeologists excavating ancient Egypti: 考古學家在挖掘古埃及墓穴時，發現了好幾罐已有數千年歷史、理論上仍可食用的蜂蜜。蜂蜜不易腐壞有好幾個原因。它的含水量非常低，而高濃度的糖分會把落入其中的細菌或真菌的水分吸出來，使它們無法存活。它本身也是天然的酸性。此外，蜜蜂會在花蜜中加入一種酵素，產生少量的過氧化氫，這是一種溫和的抗菌劑。這些因素結合起來，使蜂蜜成為少數幾乎可以無限期保存的食物之一，前提是必須密封，讓它無法吸收空氣中的水分。

questions.text: Almost all the bananas sold in supermarkets around the world belong to a single variety, the Cavendish. Because commercial bananas are seedless, they are grown from cuttings, which means every Cavendish plant is essentially a genetic copy of every other. This makes production efficient and the fruit consistent, but it also leaves the entire crop vulnerable. A soil fungus known as Panama disease is now spreading through banana plantations on several continents, and because the plants are genetically identical, none has natural resistance. This has happened before: in the 1950s a similar disease wiped out the Gros Michel, the variety that dominated the market at the time. Scientists are now searching for resistant varieties, both by breeding and by genetic modification.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Because nearly all exported bananas are genetic copies of one variety, a spreading fungal disease threatens the whole crop, as happened to an earlier variety, so scientists are developing resistant plants.
Bananas are grown from seeds, which is why the Cavendish variety has become so varied and resistant to disease.
Panama disease was completely eliminated in the 1950s, when the Gros Michel variety replaced the Cavendish.
Supermarkets sell many different banana varieties, so the loss of any single variety would have little effect.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Because nearly all exported bananas are: 由於幾乎所有出口的香蕉都是同一品種的基因複製品，一種正在蔓延的真菌病害威脅著整個作物，就像過去曾發生在另一個品種上一樣，因此科學家正在培育具抗病性的植株。
zh.Bananas are grown from seeds, which is w: 香蕉是用種子種植的，這就是為什麼香芽蕉品種變得如此多樣且具抗病性。
zh.Panama disease was completely eliminated: 巴拿馬病在 1950 年代被完全消滅了，當時大麥克品種取代了香芽蕉。
zh.Supermarkets sell many different banana: 超市販售許多不同品種的香蕉，所以失去任何一個品種都影響不大。
zh.Almost all the bananas sold in supermark: 全世界超市販售的香蕉幾乎都屬於同一個品種：香芽蕉。由於商業栽培的香蕉沒有種子，它們是用插枝繁殖的，這意味著每一株香芽蕉基本上都是其他植株的基因複製品。這讓生產更有效率、果實品質更一致，但也讓整個作物變得脆弱。一種名為「巴拿馬病」的土壤真菌，目前正在好幾個大陸的香蕉園中蔓延，而由於這些植株的基因完全相同，沒有任何一株具有天然的抵抗力。這種事以前就發生過：在 1950 年代，一種類似的病害徹底消滅了當時主導市場的品種「大麥克」。科學家現在正透過育種和基因改造，尋找具抗病性的品種。

questions.text: Thomas Edison is often credited with inventing the light bulb, but the story is more complicated. Electric light had been demonstrated decades earlier, and more than twenty inventors had produced working incandescent bulbs before Edison. The problem was that their bulbs burned out quickly or were too expensive to be practical. Edison’s real achievement was to make the light bulb commercially viable. His team tested thousands of materials before finding a carbon filament that could last for hundreds of hours, and, just as importantly, he designed an entire system of power stations, cables and meters to supply electricity to homes. In other words, he did not invent the light bulb so much as make it useful.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Edison was not the first to make a light bulb, but he made it practical by developing a long-lasting filament and a complete system for supplying electricity.
Edison invented the first electric light, although his early bulbs burned out after only a few minutes.
More than twenty inventors worked together in Edison’s team to design the first power station.
Electric light remained impractical until the twentieth century because no suitable filament material existed.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Edison was not the first to make a light: 愛迪生並不是第一個製造出燈泡的人，但他透過研發耐用的燈絲以及一套完整的供電系統，讓燈泡變得實用。
zh.Edison invented the first electric light: 愛迪生發明了第一盞電燈，不過他早期的燈泡只用幾分鐘就燒壞了。
zh.More than twenty inventors worked togeth: 二十多位發明家在愛迪生的團隊中合作，設計出第一座發電廠。
zh.Electric light remained impractical unti: 由於沒有合適的燈絲材料，電燈直到二十世紀都還不實用。
zh.Thomas Edison is often credited with inv: 湯瑪斯・愛迪生常被認為是燈泡的發明者，但事情其實更複雜。電燈早在數十年前就已經有人展示過，而在愛迪生之前，已有二十多位發明家製造出可以使用的白熾燈泡。問題在於，他們的燈泡很快就燒壞，或是太昂貴而不實用。愛迪生真正的成就，是讓燈泡在商業上變得可行。他的團隊測試了數千種材料，才找到一種能持續使用數百小時的碳燈絲，而同樣重要的是，他設計了一整套由發電廠、電纜和電表組成的系統，把電力供應到家家戶戶。換句話說，與其說他發明了燈泡，不如說他讓燈泡變得有用。

questions.text: Many people believe that food dropped on the floor is safe to eat if it is picked up within five seconds. Researchers who tested this idea found that bacteria can transfer to food almost instantly. In their experiments, the amount of bacteria picked up did increase with time, but significant contamination occurred in less than a second. The type of food mattered more than the timing: wet foods such as watermelon picked up far more bacteria than dry foods such as sweets. The surface also made a difference, with carpet transferring surprisingly little compared with tiles or stainless steel. The researchers concluded that the five-second rule is a significant oversimplification.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Bacteria can reach dropped food in under a second, and the type of food and surface matter more than time, so the five-second rule is an oversimplification.
Food dropped on the floor is safe to eat if it is picked up within five seconds, especially from carpet.
Dry foods such as sweets pick up more bacteria from the floor than wet foods such as watermelon.
The amount of bacteria on dropped food does not change over time at all.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Bacteria can reach dropped food in under: 細菌可能在不到一秒內就附著到掉落的食物上，而食物種類和表面材質比時間更重要，所以「五秒規則」是過度簡化的說法。
zh.Food dropped on the floor is safe to eat: 掉在地上的食物只要在五秒內撿起來就可以安全食用，尤其是掉在地毯上的時候。
zh.Dry foods such as sweets pick up more ba: 糖果等乾燥食物從地上沾到的細菌，比西瓜等潮濕食物更多。
zh.The amount of bacteria on dropped food d: 掉落食物上的細菌數量完全不會隨時間改變。
zh.Many people believe that food dropped on: 許多人相信，掉在地上的食物只要在五秒內撿起來，就可以安全食用。測試這個說法的研究人員發現，細菌幾乎會立刻轉移到食物上。在他們的實驗中，沾到的細菌數量確實會隨時間增加，但在不到一秒內就已經出現明顯的污染。食物的種類比時間更重要：西瓜等潮濕的食物沾到的細菌，遠比糖果等乾燥的食物多。表面材質也有影響，與磁磚或不鏽鋼相比，地毯轉移的細菌出乎意料地少。研究人員的結論是，「五秒規則」是一種嚴重過度簡化的說法。

questions.text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to tilt during its construction in the twelfth century, after only the first few floors had been built. The ground beneath it is soft clay and sand, and the foundation, just three metres deep, was far too shallow for such a heavy structure. Construction was halted for almost a century because of wars, which may have saved the tower, as the delay allowed the soil to settle and strengthen. Over the following centuries the lean continued to increase, and by 1990 the tower was closed to visitors because engineers feared it might collapse. A stabilisation project removed small amounts of soil from beneath the higher side, reducing the tilt by around forty centimetres. Engineers believe the tower is now stable for at least two hundred years.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: The tower leaned because of soft ground and a shallow foundation; a long pause in construction may have saved it, and recent work removing soil has reduced the tilt and stabilised it.
The tower was deliberately built at an angle to show off the skill of medieval engineers.
Engineers straightened the tower completely in the 1990s by giving it a much deeper foundation.
The tower collapsed in 1990 and was rebuilt using stronger materials.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.The tower leaned because of soft ground: 這座塔之所以傾斜，是因為地基鬆軟且地基太淺；工程的長期停頓可能救了它，而近年移除土壤的工程減少了傾斜並使它穩定下來。
zh.The tower was deliberately built at an a: 這座塔是刻意以傾斜的角度建造的，為了展現中世紀工程師的技術。
zh.Engineers straightened the tower complet: 工程師在 1990 年代為塔加上深得多的地基，把它完全扶正了。
zh.The tower collapsed in 1990 and was rebu: 這座塔在 1990 年倒塌，之後用更堅固的材料重建。
zh.The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to tilt: 比薩斜塔在十二世紀建造期間，才剛蓋好最初幾層樓就開始傾斜。它下方的地面是鬆軟的黏土和沙子，而只有三公尺深的地基，對這麼重的建築來說實在太淺了。由於戰爭，工程停頓了將近一個世紀，這可能反而救了這座塔，因為這段延宕讓土壤有時間沉降並變得更結實。在接下來的幾個世紀裡，傾斜的程度持續增加，到了 1990 年，由於工程師擔心它可能倒塌，這座塔對遊客關閉。一項穩定工程從較高一側的下方移除了少量土壤，使傾斜減少了約四十公分。工程師相信，這座塔現在至少能穩定兩百年。

questions.text: The satellite navigation in your phone works by measuring time. Each GPS satellite carries an extremely accurate atomic clock and continuously broadcasts its position and the exact time. Your phone receives signals from at least four satellites and calculates how long each signal took to arrive, which tells it how far away each satellite is. Combining these distances gives your position. Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, tiny timing errors matter: an error of one millionth of a second would place you three hundred metres out. The system even has to correct for Einstein’s theory of relativity, since clocks on the fast-moving satellites run at a slightly different rate from clocks on the ground.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: GPS finds your position by timing signals from several satellites with very accurate clocks; because tiny timing errors cause large position errors, even the effects of relativity must be corrected.
GPS works by measuring the strength of signals from mobile phone towers near the user.
GPS satellites take photographs of the ground in order to locate each phone precisely.
Timing errors have little effect on GPS because radio signals travel relatively slowly.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.GPS finds your position by timing signal: GPS 透過計算來自數顆配備極精準時鐘的衛星的訊號時間來找出你的位置；由於微小的時間誤差會造成很大的位置誤差，甚至連相對論的效應都必須加以修正。
zh.GPS works by measuring the strength of s: GPS 的運作方式是測量使用者附近手機基地台的訊號強度。
zh.GPS satellites take photographs of the g: GPS 衛星會拍攝地面的照片，以精確定位每一支手機。
zh.Timing errors have little effect on GPS: 時間誤差對 GPS 影響不大，因為無線電訊號的傳播速度相對較慢。
zh.The satellite navigation in your phone w: 你手機裡的衛星導航是靠測量時間來運作的。每一顆 GPS 衛星都搭載了一個極其精準的原子鐘，並持續廣播自己的位置和精確的時間。你的手機會接收至少四顆衛星的訊號，並計算每個訊號花了多久才到達，由此得知每顆衛星距離多遠。把這些距離結合起來，就能得出你的位置。由於無線電訊號以光速傳播，微小的時間誤差也很重要：百萬分之一秒的誤差，就會讓你的位置偏差三百公尺。這個系統甚至必須修正愛因斯坦相對論的效應，因為在高速移動的衛星上，時鐘運轉的速率與地面上的時鐘略有不同。

questions.text: Most substances are denser as solids than as liquids, so their solid form sinks. Water is an unusual exception. When water freezes, its molecules, held together by hydrogen bonds, arrange themselves into an open crystal structure that takes up more space than liquid water. Ice is therefore about nine per cent less dense than water, and it floats. This property is vital for life. When a lake freezes in winter, the ice forms a layer on the surface that insulates the water below, allowing fish and other organisms to survive. If ice sank, lakes would freeze from the bottom up and many would become solid ice, with devastating effects on freshwater ecosystems.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: Unlike most substances, water expands when it freezes because of its crystal structure, so ice floats and insulates lakes from above, allowing aquatic life to survive the winter.
Ice sinks in most lakes, which is why lakes freeze from the bottom up in winter.
Water is denser as a solid than as a liquid, just like most other substances.
Fish survive the winter by moving up into the layer of ice on the surface of lakes.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.Unlike most substances, water expands wh: 與大多數物質不同，水因為其晶體結構而在結冰時膨脹，所以冰會浮在水面上，從上方為湖泊隔熱，讓水中生物得以度過冬天。
zh.Ice sinks in most lakes, which is why la: 在大多數湖泊中冰會下沉，這就是為什麼湖泊在冬天會從底部開始結冰。
zh.Water is denser as a solid than as a liq: 就像大多數其他物質一樣，水在固態時的密度比液態時高。
zh.Fish survive the winter by moving up int: 魚類透過游進湖面的冰層中來度過冬天。
zh.Most substances are denser as solids tha: 大多數物質在固態時的密度比液態時高，所以它們的固態會下沉。水是一個不尋常的例外。當水結冰時，由氫鍵連結在一起的水分子，會排列成一種開放的晶體結構，所占的空間比液態水還大。因此，冰的密度比水低約百分之九，所以會浮起來。這個特性對生命至關重要。當湖泊在冬天結冰時，冰會在水面形成一層，為下方的水隔熱，讓魚類和其他生物得以存活。如果冰會下沉，湖泊就會從底部開始往上結冰，許多湖泊會變成一整塊實心的冰，對淡水生態系造成毀滅性的影響。

questions.text: In 1993, a short study reported that students who listened to a Mozart sonata performed slightly better on a spatial reasoning task than those who sat in silence. The effect lasted only about ten to fifteen minutes. Nevertheless, the finding was widely reported as showing that classical music makes people smarter, and in some places parents of newborn babies were even given free classical music recordings. Later research painted a different picture. Many attempts to repeat the study failed, and those that found an effect showed that any enjoyable, stimulating activity, including listening to other kinds of music, produced the same brief improvement, probably because it raised the listeners’ mood and alertness.
questions.q: Which summary best represents the recording?
o: A small, short-lived improvement after listening to Mozart was exaggerated into a claim that classical music raises intelligence, but later research showed any enjoyable stimulation has the same brief effect.
Listening to Mozart as a baby permanently improves a person’s spatial reasoning skills.
The 1993 study found that sitting in silence improves performance more than listening to music.
Later research confirmed that only Mozart’s music can improve thinking skills.

zh.Which summary best represents the record: 哪一個摘要最能代表錄音內容？
zh.A small, short-lived improvement after l: 聽莫札特後出現的微小而短暫的進步，被誇大成古典音樂能提高智力的說法，但後來的研究顯示，任何令人愉快的刺激都有同樣短暫的效果。
zh.Listening to Mozart as a baby permanentl: 嬰兒時期聽莫札特能永久提升一個人的空間推理能力。
zh.The 1993 study found that sitting in sil: 1993 年的研究發現，靜坐比聽音樂更能提升表現。
zh.Later research confirmed that only Mozar: 後來的研究證實，只有莫札特的音樂能提升思考能力。
zh.In 1993, a short study reported that stu: 1993 年，一項簡短的研究指出，聽過莫札特奏鳴曲的學生，在空間推理測驗中的表現比靜坐的學生稍好一些。這種效果只持續了大約十到十五分鐘。儘管如此，這項發現仍被廣泛報導為證明古典音樂能讓人變聰明，在某些地方，甚至會送給新生兒的父母免費的古典音樂唱片。後來的研究呈現出不同的面貌。許多重複這項研究的嘗試都失敗了，而那些發現有效果的研究則顯示，任何令人愉快且具刺激性的活動，包括聽其他類型的音樂，都會產生同樣短暫的進步，這可能是因為它提升了聽者的心情和警覺性。

questions.text: I need to correct something I said last week about the final assessment for this module. I told you the research report would be worth sixty per cent and the exam forty. Having checked the module handbook, it is actually the other way round: the exam is worth sixty per cent and the report forty. The deadline for the report has not changed; it is still the twelfth of May. I realise some of you may have planned your time around what I said, so I have asked the department to run an extra revision session in the week before the exam. Details will be on the module page by Friday.
questions.q: Why does the lecturer make this announcement?
o: To announce that the report deadline has been moved to the twelfth of May.
To correct an error about how the module’s assessment is weighted.
To explain that the exam has been cancelled this year.
To ask students to attend a revision session on Friday.

zh.Why does the lecturer make this announce: 講者為什麼要發布這則公告？
zh.To announce that the report deadline has: 宣布報告的截止日期已改到五月十二日。
zh.To correct an error about how the module: 更正有關這門課評分比重的錯誤。
zh.To explain that the exam has been cancel: 說明今年的考試已經取消。
zh.To ask students to attend a revision ses: 請學生參加星期五的複習課。
zh.I need to correct something I said last: 我需要更正上週我提到這門課期末評量的一件事。我當時告訴大家，研究報告占百分之六十，考試占百分之四十。在查閱課程手冊之後，實際上正好相反：考試占百分之六十，報告占百分之四十。報告的截止日期沒有改變，仍然是五月十二日。我知道你們有些人可能已經依照我說的來安排時間，所以我已經請系上在考試前一週加開一場複習課。詳細資訊會在星期五之前公布在課程頁面上。

questions.text: Flamingos are not born pink. Chicks hatch with grey or white feathers, and their adult colour comes almost entirely from their diet. The algae and small shrimp that flamingos eat contain pigments called carotenoids, the same compounds that make carrots orange. As the birds digest their food, these pigments are deposited in their growing feathers. A flamingo that does not get enough carotenoids gradually fades, which is why zoos add them to the birds’ food. Colour also matters socially: brighter birds tend to find mates more easily, so a vivid pink is effectively an advertisement of a healthy diet.
questions.q: What is the speaker’s main point?
o: Flamingos are born pink and gradually lose their colour as they age.
Zoos use artificial dyes to make their flamingos look brighter.
A flamingo’s pink colour comes from pigments in its food and signals good health.
Carrots are the main source of food for wild flamingos.

zh.What is the speaker’s main point?: 講者的主要論點是什麼？
zh.Flamingos are born pink and gradually lo: 紅鶴一出生就是粉紅色的，隨著年齡增長逐漸褪色。
zh.Zoos use artificial dyes to make their f: 動物園使用人工染料讓紅鶴看起來更鮮豔。
zh.A flamingo’s pink colour comes from pigm: 紅鶴的粉紅色來自食物中的色素，也代表身體健康。
zh.Carrots are the main source of food for: 胡蘿蔔是野生紅鶴的主要食物來源。
zh.Flamingos are not born pink. Chicks hatc: 紅鶴並不是一出生就是粉紅色的。雛鳥孵出時羽毛是灰色或白色的，而成鳥的顏色幾乎完全來自飲食。紅鶴吃的藻類和小蝦含有一種叫做類胡蘿蔔素的色素，也就是讓胡蘿蔔呈現橘色的同一種化合物。當鳥類消化食物時，這些色素會沉積在牠們正在生長的羽毛中。攝取不到足夠類胡蘿蔔素的紅鶴會逐漸褪色，這就是為什麼動物園會在牠們的食物中添加這種色素。顏色在社交上也很重要：顏色越鮮豔的鳥往往越容易找到配偶，所以鮮豔的粉紅色實際上就是在宣告自己飲食健康。

questions.text: Every year, thousands of studies are completed that find no effect at all: the new drug works no better than the old one, or the teaching method makes no difference to results. Most of these studies are never published, partly because journals prefer positive findings and partly because researchers see little reward in writing them up. This matters more than it might seem. If only the successful studies are published, the published evidence will make treatments look more effective than they really are. Other teams may also waste years repeating experiments that have already failed. Some journals now accept studies on the basis of their design before the results are known, which makes negative findings just as publishable as positive ones.
questions.q: According to the speaker, what is the main problem with not publishing negative results?
o: Journals lose money because fewer studies are submitted.
The published evidence gives a misleadingly positive picture.
Researchers are discouraged from designing new experiments.
Positive findings become harder to publish.

zh.According to the speaker, what is the ma: 根據講者所說，不發表負面結果的主要問題是什麼？
zh.Journals lose money because fewer studie: 期刊因為投稿的研究變少而虧損。
zh.The published evidence gives a misleadin: 已發表的證據會呈現出誤導性的正面印象。
zh.Researchers are discouraged from designi: 研究人員會因此不願意設計新的實驗。
zh.Positive findings become harder to publi: 正面的研究發現變得更難發表。
zh.Every year, thousands of studies are com: 每年都有數千項研究完成後發現完全沒有效果：新藥並不比舊藥有效，或是某種教學方法對成績毫無影響。這些研究大多從未發表，部分原因是期刊偏好正面的發現，部分原因是研究人員覺得把它們寫出來沒什麼好處。這件事比表面上看起來更重要。如果只有成功的研究被發表，已發表的證據就會讓療法看起來比實際上更有效。其他團隊也可能浪費好幾年的時間，重複那些早已失敗的實驗。有些期刊現在會在結果出爐之前，就根據研究設計來決定是否接受刊登，這讓負面的發現和正面的發現一樣有機會被發表。

questions.text: Just a quick announcement before we start. As many of you know, the main library will close for refurbishment at the end of this month and is not expected to reopen until September. During that time, the book collection will still be available, but you will need to request items online, and they will be delivered to the science building within two working days. The large study space on the ground floor of the student centre has been converted into a temporary reading room, with the same opening hours as the library and around three hundred desks. Group study rooms can also be booked there. If you rely on the library computers, please note that there will be fewer of them, so bring your own laptop if you can.
questions.q: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
o: To announce that the library’s book collection is being sold.
To explain how students can use library services while the library is closed.
To encourage students to buy new laptops.
To invite students to help plan the library refurbishment.

zh.What is the main purpose of the announce: 這則公告的主要目的是什麼？
zh.To announce that the library’s book coll: 宣布圖書館的藏書將被出售。
zh.To explain how students can use library: 說明在圖書館關閉期間，學生可以如何使用圖書館的服務。
zh.To encourage students to buy new laptops: 鼓勵學生購買新的筆記型電腦。
zh.To invite students to help plan the libr: 邀請學生協助規劃圖書館的整修。
zh.Just a quick announcement before we star: 開始之前先簡短宣布一件事。你們很多人都知道，總圖書館將在本月底關閉進行整修，預計要到九月才會重新開放。在這段期間，藏書仍然可以使用，但你們需要在網路上申請借閱，書會在兩個工作天內送到理學大樓。學生中心一樓的大型自習空間已經改設為臨時閱覽室，開放時間與圖書館相同，約有三百個座位。那裡也可以預約小組討論室。如果你們依賴圖書館的電腦，請注意電腦的數量會比較少，所以如果可以的話，請自備筆記型電腦。

questions.text: Almost everyone has had the experience of a song getting stuck in their head, a phenomenon psychologists call an earworm. Research suggests that earworms are most likely to be songs with a fairly fast tempo, a simple melody and a small, unexpected twist, such as an unusual interval or rhythm. They tend to appear when the mind is not fully occupied, for example while walking or doing routine tasks. Interestingly, trying to push an earworm away often makes it return. One study found that a more effective approach is to engage the mind with a moderately demanding task, such as a crossword or an anagram puzzle, which uses the same mental resources and crowds the tune out. Chewing gum has also been shown to help, possibly because it interferes with silently rehearsing the song.
questions.q: According to the speaker, what is the most effective way to get rid of an earworm?
o: Try hard not to think about the song.
Listen to the whole song again until it fades.
Do a moderately demanding mental task, such as a puzzle.
Go for a walk or do routine tasks.

zh.According to the speaker, what is the mo: 根據講者所說，擺脫「耳蟲」最有效的方法是什麼？
zh.Listen to the whole song again until it: 把整首歌再聽一遍，直到它淡去。
zh.Do a moderately demanding mental task, s: 做一項難度適中的思考任務，例如解謎。
去散步或做例行的工作。
zh.Almost everyone has had the experience o: 幾乎每個人都有過歌曲在腦中揮之不去的經驗，心理學家把這種現象稱為「耳蟲」。研究顯示，最容易變成耳蟲的，是節奏相當快、旋律簡單，而且帶有一點小小的意外轉折的歌曲，例如不尋常的音程或節奏。它們往往在大腦沒有完全被占用時出現，例如走路或做例行工作的時候。有趣的是，試圖把耳蟲趕走，往往會讓它再次出現。一項研究發現，更有效的方法是讓大腦投入一項難度適中的任務，例如填字遊戲或字謎，這類任務會使用相同的心智資源，把旋律擠出去。嚼口香糖也被證明有幫助，可能是因為它會干擾在心裡默默重複那首歌。

questions.text: Many students prepare for a presentation by writing out the whole script and reading it through silently several times. The problem is that reading silently is a completely different skill from speaking aloud. You don’t discover that a sentence is too long to say in one breath, or that a transition sounds awkward, until you actually hear yourself. So my strongest advice is to rehearse out loud, ideally standing up and with a timer, at least three times before the day. It helps to record yourself on your phone, even though most people hate listening to their own voice. And rather than memorising a script word for word, which tends to fall apart if you lose your place, memorise the structure: the main points and the order they come in.
questions.q: What does the speaker recommend most strongly?
o: Writing out the whole script and reading it silently.
Rehearsing the presentation out loud several times.
Memorising the script word for word.
Avoiding recording yourself, as it causes anxiety.

zh.What does the speaker recommend most str: 講者最強烈建議的是什麼？
zh.Writing out the whole script and reading: 寫出完整的講稿並默讀。
zh.Rehearsing the presentation out loud sev: 把簡報大聲地演練好幾次。
zh.Avoiding recording yourself, as it cause: 避免錄下自己的聲音，因為那會造成焦慮。
zh.Many students prepare for a presentation: 許多學生準備簡報的方式，是把整篇講稿寫出來，然後默讀好幾遍。問題在於，默讀和大聲說話是完全不同的技能。在你真正聽到自己說話之前，你不會發現某個句子太長，一口氣說不完，或是某個轉折聽起來很彆扭。所以我最強烈的建議是大聲演練，最好是站著並使用計時器，在正式上場前至少練習三次。用手機把自己錄下來也很有幫助，即使大多數人都討厭聽自己的聲音。而且與其把講稿逐字背下來——那樣一旦忘了講到哪裡就容易全盤崩潰——不如記住架構：也就是重點以及它們的順序。

questions.text: The word robot is younger than many people think. It first appeared in 1920, in a play by the Czech writer Karel Čapek about artificial workers manufactured in a factory. The word comes from the Czech robota, meaning forced labour, the kind of work that peasants once owed to landowners. Čapek later said that the word was actually suggested by his brother, the painter Josef Čapek. Notably, the robots in the play were not metal machines but living beings made from synthetic flesh, and the story ends with them rebelling against their human owners. So from the very beginning, the idea of the robot carried both the dream of freeing people from hard work and the fear of losing control of what we create.
questions.q: What is the speaker’s main point?
o: The first robots were metal machines built in a Czech factory.
The word robot was invented by an engineer to describe factory machines.
From its origin in a 1920 play, the idea of the robot combined the hope of freedom from labour with the fear of losing control.
Josef Čapek wrote the play in which robots first appeared.

zh.What is the speaker’s main point?: 講者的主要論點是什麼？
zh.The first robots were metal machines bui: 最早的機器人是在捷克一家工廠製造的金屬機器。
zh.The word robot was invented by an engine: robot 這個字是一位工程師為了描述工廠機器而發明的。
zh.From its origin in a 1920 play, the idea: 從它在 1920 年一齣劇作中誕生開始，機器人的概念就同時包含了擺脫勞動的希望，以及失去控制的恐懼。
zh.Josef Čapek wrote the play in which robo: 約瑟夫・恰佩克寫了機器人首次出現的那齣劇作。
zh.The word robot is younger than many peop: robot（機器人）這個字比許多人想像的年輕。它最早出現在 1920 年，出自捷克作家卡雷爾・恰佩克的一齣劇作，內容講述在工廠中製造出來的人造工人。這個字源自捷克語的 robota，意思是強迫勞動，也就是農民過去必須為地主做的那種工作。恰佩克後來表示，這個字其實是他的哥哥、畫家約瑟夫・恰佩克建議的。值得注意的是，劇中的機器人並不是金屬機器，而是由合成肉體製成的生命體，故事的結局是它們起來反抗它們的人類主人。所以從一開始，機器人的概念就同時承載著讓人們擺脫辛苦勞動的夢想，以及對失去控制自己所創造之物的恐懼。

questions.text: The Arctic is warming roughly three to four times faster than the global average, and the main reason is a feedback involving ice. Sea ice is bright and reflects most of the sunlight that falls on it back into space. When it melts, it exposes the darker ocean beneath, which absorbs far more of the sun’s energy. That absorbed heat warms the water and melts more ice, which exposes more ocean, and so on. Other factors contribute, including changes in clouds and in the way heat is carried towards the poles by the atmosphere, but the loss of reflective ice is the process that scientists most often point to. The consequences are not confined to the Arctic, since the melting of land ice in Greenland raises sea levels around the world.
questions.q: According to the speaker, what is the main reason the Arctic is warming so quickly?
o: The Arctic receives more sunlight than other regions.
Melting ice exposes darker ocean, which absorbs more heat and causes further melting.
Changes in clouds are the only cause of Arctic warming.
Rising sea levels are heating the Arctic Ocean.

zh.According to the speaker, what is the ma: 根據講者所說，北極暖化如此迅速的主要原因是什麼？
zh.The Arctic receives more sunlight than o: 北極接收到的陽光比其他地區多。
zh.Melting ice exposes darker ocean, which: 冰融化後露出顏色較深的海洋，海洋吸收更多熱能，造成更多冰融化。
zh.Changes in clouds are the only cause of: 雲層的變化是北極暖化的唯一原因。
zh.Rising sea levels are heating the Arctic: 海平面上升正在加熱北冰洋。
zh.The Arctic is warming roughly three to f: 北極暖化的速度大約是全球平均的三到四倍，主要原因是一個與冰有關的回饋機制。海冰很明亮，會把照射在上面的大部分陽光反射回太空。當海冰融化時，就會露出下方顏色較深的海洋，而海洋會吸收多得多的太陽能量。吸收的熱能使海水變暖、融化更多的冰，於是露出更多的海洋，如此循環下去。其他因素也有影響，包括雲層的變化，以及大氣把熱量輸送到兩極的方式，但反光的冰層消失，是科學家最常指出的過程。其後果並不只局限於北極，因為格陵蘭陸冰的融化會使全世界的海平面上升。

questions.text: We usually treat boredom as something to be eliminated, and with a phone in every pocket, it has never been easier to avoid. But several studies suggest that boredom may have a useful side. In one experiment, participants who first spent fifteen minutes on a deliberately dull task, copying numbers from a phone directory, then came up with more creative uses for a pair of plastic cups than participants who had not been bored. The researchers argue that boredom pushes the mind to wander and to seek stimulation internally, which can lead to new connections between ideas. That doesn’t mean all boredom is good, but it suggests that constantly filling every quiet moment with a screen may cost us opportunities to think creatively.
questions.q: What does the speaker suggest about boredom?
o: It should always be avoided because it reduces productivity.
It may encourage creative thinking by letting the mind wander.
It is caused mainly by using phones too much.
It has no measurable effect on how people think.

zh.What does the speaker suggest about bore: 講者對無聊有什麼看法？
zh.It should always be avoided because it r: 應該總是避免無聊，因為它會降低生產力。
zh.It may encourage creative thinking by le: 無聊可能讓思緒漫遊，因而激發創意思考。
zh.It is caused mainly by using phones too: 無聊主要是因為使用手機過度造成的。
zh.It has no measurable effect on how peopl: 無聊對人們的思考方式沒有可衡量的影響。
zh.We usually treat boredom as something to: 我們通常把無聊視為應該消除的東西，而在人人口袋裡都有手機的今天，要避免無聊從來沒有這麼容易過。但好幾項研究顯示，無聊可能有它有用的一面。在一項實驗中，先花十五分鐘做一項刻意設計得很乏味的任務——從電話簿抄寫號碼——的受試者，之後為一對塑膠杯想出的創意用途，比沒有經歷無聊的受試者更多。研究人員認為，無聊會促使思緒漫遊，並向內尋求刺激，這可能帶來想法之間的新連結。這並不表示所有的無聊都是好的，但它顯示，總是用螢幕填滿每一個安靜的時刻，可能會讓我們失去創意思考的機會。

questions.text: A quick update about next week’s seminar. Because the usual room is being used for exams, we’ll be meeting in room 214 in the history building instead, at the normal time of ten o’clock. Please note that the reading has also changed. Instead of the chapter listed in the handbook, I’d like you to read the journal article I uploaded to the course page this morning. It’s shorter, around twenty pages, but it’s quite dense, so allow yourself enough time. Come prepared with two questions about the article, because we’ll build the discussion around the questions you bring. If you can’t attend, email me before Monday and I’ll send you a short alternative task.
questions.q: What must students do to prepare for next week’s seminar?
o: Read the chapter listed in the handbook.
Read the uploaded article and bring two questions about it.
Arrive at nine o’clock at the usual room.

zh.What must students do to prepare for nex: 學生必須為下週的研討課做什麼準備？
閱讀課程手冊中列出的章節。
在星期一之前寄電子郵件給講師。
zh.Read the uploaded article and bring two: 閱讀上傳的論文，並針對它準備兩個問題。
zh.A quick update about next week’s seminar: 關於下週研討課的一個簡短更新。由於平常的教室要用來考試，我們會改到歷史大樓的 214 教室上課，時間照舊是十點。請注意，閱讀材料也改了。請不要讀課程手冊中列出的那一章，而是閱讀我今天早上上傳到課程頁面的那篇期刊論文。它比較短，大約二十頁，但內容相當艱深，所以請預留足夠的時間。請針對這篇論文準備兩個問題，因為我們的討論會圍繞著你們帶來的問題進行。如果你無法出席，請在星期一之前寄電子郵件給我，我會寄一份簡短的替代作業給你。

questions.text: Many students believe that the best way to prepare for an exam is to read their notes again and again. It feels productive, because the material becomes familiar, and familiarity is easily mistaken for understanding. Research on memory suggests that a far more effective strategy is to test yourself: close the book and try to write down everything you can remember, then check what you missed. The effort of retrieving information is exactly what strengthens it. In other words, the struggle that makes self-testing feel unpleasant is the very thing that makes it

zh.Many students believe that the best way: 許多學生認為，準備考試最好的方法就是一遍又一遍地重讀筆記。這感覺很有成效，因為內容會變得熟悉，而熟悉很容易被誤認為理解。關於記憶的研究顯示，更有效得多的策略是自我測驗：闔上書本，試著寫下所有你記得的內容，然後檢查你漏掉了什麼。提取資訊時所付出的努力，正是強化記憶的關鍵。換句話說，讓自我測驗感覺不舒服的那份掙扎，恰恰就是讓它有效的原因。

questions.text: In the early days of aviation, pilots flew largely by sight, following roads, rivers and railway lines from one town to the next. This worked well in clear weather, but when cloud or fog closed in, pilots quickly lost any sense of which way was up, and many crashes followed. The solution came from instruments: an artificial horizon, a compass and an altimeter allowed a trained pilot to fly safely through cloud. By the 1930s, the most important skill for a pilot was no longer good eyesight but the discipline to trust the

zh.In the early days of aviation, pilots fl: 在航空業的早期，飛行員主要靠目視飛行，沿著道路、河流和鐵路從一個城鎮飛到下一個城鎮。這在晴朗的天氣下很有效，但當雲層或霧氣籠罩時，飛行員很快就會完全失去上下方向感，許多墜機事故也隨之發生。解決方法來自儀器：人工地平儀、羅盤和高度計讓受過訓練的飛行員能安全地穿越雲層。到了 1930 年代，飛行員最重要的技能已不再是良好的視力，而是信任儀器的紀律。

questions.text: Researchers studying happiness have found that people are surprisingly poor at predicting what will make them happy. We expect a pay rise or a bigger house to improve our lives for years, but within a few months we usually return to roughly the same level of satisfaction as before. Psychologists call this hedonic adaptation. Experiences, by contrast, such as travel or learning a new skill, seem to provide more lasting satisfaction, partly because we share them with others and partly because they become part of our

zh.Researchers studying happiness have foun: 研究快樂的學者發現，人們在預測什麼會讓自己快樂這件事上，表現出乎意料地差。我們以為加薪或換更大的房子能讓生活改善好幾年，但通常在幾個月內，我們的滿足感就會回到和以前差不多的程度。心理學家稱之為「享樂適應」。相較之下，像旅行或學習新技能這樣的經驗，似乎能帶來更持久的滿足感，部分是因為我們會與他人分享這些經驗，部分則是因為它們會成為我們身分認同的一部分。

questions.text: For much of the twentieth century, doctors advised patients with back pain to rest in bed until the pain went away. Research has since shown that this advice was wrong. Patients who stayed active, doing gentle walking and continuing their normal activities as far as possible, recovered faster and were less likely to develop long-term pain. Today, guidelines in most countries recommend the opposite of what doctors once said. For most people with back pain, the best treatment is to keep

zh.For much of the twentieth century, docto: 在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，醫生都建議背痛的病人臥床休息，直到疼痛消失為止。後來的研究顯示，這個建議是錯的。保持活動的病人——做些輕鬆的散步，並盡可能維持日常活動——恢復得比較快，也比較不會發展成長期疼痛。如今，大多數國家的指引所建議的，正好與醫生過去所說的相反。對大多數背痛的人來說，最好的治療方法就是持續活動。

questions.text: When the first telephones were installed, nobody was quite sure how to begin a conversation. Alexander Graham Bell himself preferred to answer by saying ahoy, the word sailors used to hail another ship. It was Thomas Edison who suggested hello, a variation of an older word used to attract attention. Telephone companies printed it in their instruction booklets, and it quickly became standard. So the word we now use to greet people face to face was popularised by the

zh.When the first telephones were installed: 最早的電話安裝好時，沒有人確定該怎麼開始一段對話。亞歷山大・格拉漢・貝爾本人比較喜歡用 ahoy 來接電話，這是水手用來招呼另一艘船的用語。是湯瑪斯・愛迪生提議使用 hello，這是一個用來引起注意的古老字詞的變體。電話公司把它印在使用說明手冊中，它很快就成為了標準用語。所以，我們現在用來當面打招呼的這個字，是因為電話而普及的。

questions.text: Many cities have tried to reduce traffic by building more roads, only to find that congestion returns within a few years. Some have tried the opposite approach, removing roads or closing them to cars. When a major highway in Seoul was demolished and replaced by a stream and a park, traffic did not become worse, as many had feared. Drivers changed their routes, their timing or their means of transport. It seems that traffic behaves less like water in a pipe and more like a gas, expanding to fill the

zh.Many cities have tried to reduce traffic: 許多城市曾試圖透過興建更多道路來減少交通量，結果卻發現壅塞在幾年內又回來了。有些城市嘗試了相反的做法，拆除道路或禁止汽車通行。當首爾一條主要的高架道路被拆除，改建成一條溪流和一座公園時，交通並沒有像許多人擔心的那樣變得更糟。駕駛人改變了他們的路線、出行時間或交通方式。看來交通的表現與其說像管子裡的水，不如說更像一種氣體，會擴散填滿可用的空間。

questions.spoken: The first vaccines against polio were tested in 1954 in one of the largest medical trials ever conducted. Nearly two million children took part, and the results, announced a year later, showed that the vaccine was safe and effective. Within a few years, cases in the United States had fallen dramatically.
questions.shown: The first vaccines against polio were tested in 1954 in one of the smallest medical trials ever conducted. Nearly three million children took part, and the results, announced a year earlier, showed that the vaccine was safe and effective. Within a few years, cases in the United States had fallen slightly.

zh.The first vaccines against polio were te: 第一批小兒麻痺疫苗於 1954 年進行測試，那是有史以來規模最小的醫學試驗之一。將近三百萬名兒童參與，而一年前公布的結果顯示，這種疫苗安全又有效。短短幾年內，美國的病例就略微下降了。
第一批小兒麻痺疫苗於 1954 年進行測試，那是有史以來規模最大的醫學試驗之一。將近兩百萬名兒童參與，而一年後公布的結果顯示，這種疫苗安全又有效。短短幾年內，美國的病例就大幅下降了。

questions.spoken: Many of the world’s great cities were built beside rivers. A river provided fresh water, a way to move goods and a natural defence against attack. Over time, however, cities grew far beyond their original banks, and today the river is often hidden beneath roads or confined within concrete walls.
questions.shown: Many of the world’s great cities were built beside rivers. A river provided clean water, a way to move people and a natural border against attack. Over time, however, cities grew far beyond their original banks, and today the river is often visible beneath roads or confined within concrete walls.

zh.Many of the world’s great cities were bu: 世界上許多大城市都建在河邊。河流提供了乾淨的水、運送人員的途徑，以及抵禦攻擊的天然邊界。然而，隨著時間過去，城市的發展遠遠超出了原本的河岸，如今河流常常在道路下方清晰可見，或被限制在混凝土牆之間。
世界上許多大城市都建在河邊。河流提供了淡水、運送貨物的途徑，以及抵禦攻擊的天然屏障。然而，隨著時間過去，城市的發展遠遠超出了原本的河岸，如今河流常常被掩埋在道路下方，或被限制在混凝土牆之間。

questions.spoken: Scientists studying sleep in birds have found that some species can rest one half of the brain at a time. While one side sleeps, the other stays alert, and the eye connected to the awake half remains open. Ducks at the edge of a group use this ability to watch for predators while they rest.
questions.shown: Scientists studying sleep in birds have found that some species can rest one third of the brain at a time. While one side sleeps, the other stays alert, and the eye connected to the awake half remains closed. Ducks at the centre of a group use this ability to watch for food while they rest.

zh.Scientists studying sleep in birds have: 研究鳥類睡眠的科學家發現，有些鳥類可以一次讓三分之一的大腦休息。當一邊在睡覺時，另一邊保持警覺，而連接清醒那一半大腦的眼睛則保持閉著。位於群體中央的鴨子會利用這種能力，在休息時留意食物。
研究鳥類睡眠的科學家發現，有些鳥類可以一次讓一半的大腦休息。當一邊在睡覺時，另一邊保持警覺，而連接清醒那一半大腦的眼睛則保持睜開。位於群體邊緣的鴨子會利用這種能力，在休息時留意掠食者。

questions.spoken: The first public museum in Britain opened in Oxford in 1683. Its collection included natural history specimens, coins and objects brought back by travellers. Visitors paid an entry fee, and the museum quickly became popular with students and scholars from across the country.
questions.shown: The first public library in Britain opened in Oxford in 1683. Its collection included natural history specimens, stamps and objects brought back by travellers. Visitors paid an entry fee, and the museum quickly became popular with children and scholars from across the country.

zh.The first public library in Britain open: 英國第一座公共圖書館於 1683 年在牛津開幕。它的收藏包括自然史標本、郵票以及旅行者帶回來的物品。參觀者要付入場費，而這座博物館很快就受到來自全國各地的兒童和學者歡迎。
zh.The first public museum in Britain opene: 英國第一座公共博物館於 1683 年在牛津開幕。它的收藏包括自然史標本、錢幣以及旅行者帶回來的物品。參觀者要付入場費，而這座博物館很快就受到來自全國各地的學生和學者歡迎。

questions.spoken: Sharks have existed for more than four hundred million years, which means they were swimming in the oceans long before the first trees appeared on land. Many species have changed very little over that time, and their skeletons are made of cartilage rather than bone.
questions.shown: Sharks have existed for more than two hundred million years, which means they were swimming in the oceans long before the first flowers appeared on land. Many species have changed very much over that time, and their skeletons are made of cartilage rather than bone.

zh.Sharks have existed for more than two hu: 鯊魚已經存在了兩億多年，這意味著早在第一批花朵出現在陸地上之前，牠們就已經在海洋中游動了。許多物種在這段期間變化很大，而牠們的骨骼是由軟骨而不是硬骨構成的。
zh.Sharks have existed for more than four h: 鯊魚已經存在了四億多年，這意味著早在第一批樹木出現在陸地上之前，牠們就已經在海洋中游動了。許多物種在這段期間幾乎沒有什麼變化，而牠們的骨骼是由軟骨而不是硬骨構成的。

questions.spoken: Many students find that working in short, focused sessions is more productive than studying for hours without a break. A popular method involves working for twenty-five minutes and then resting for five, repeating the cycle four times before taking a longer rest.
questions.shown: Many students find that working in long, focused sessions is more productive than studying for hours without a break. A popular method involves working for forty-five minutes and then resting for ten, repeating the cycle three times before taking a longer rest.

zh.Many students find that working in long,: 許多學生發現，以長時間、專注的方式讀書，比連續好幾個小時不休息更有效率。一種很受歡迎的方法是讀四十五分鐘後休息十分鐘，重複這個循環三次後，再休息比較長的時間。
